The reaction proceeds with complete stereospecificity and broad functional‐group tolerance, furnishing a C2 sulfide handle on thiazole that serves as a versatile linchpin for downstream C–S diversification. A formal asymmetric synthesis of a bioactive thiazole γ‐secretase inhibitor was demonstrated to further highlight the synthetic utility of our LiBAP protocol.
n4c46fe91c424: Understanding how second metal species modulate catalytic performance remains a central challenge in bimetallic heterogeneous catalysis. Here, we report a controllable strategy to construct atomically contacted and spatially isolated structures between Pt3 clusters and Cu atoms on γ‐Al2O3 by atomic layer deposition (ALD), enabling direct interrogation of metal–metal synergy. By regulating anchoring sites around Pt clusters, Cu atoms can be selectively positioned either by bonding to Pt to form Pt3Cu1 clusters or by separating into isolated Cu single atoms. Comprehensive characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that Cu single atom can act as an effective promoter only when directly bonded to Pt3 clusters. As electron donator, the bonded Cu atom can enhance the hydrogen dissociation ability of Pt clusters, weaken their strong acetylene adsorption, and facilitate ethylene desorption, thereby overcoming the activity‐selectivity trade‐off in selective hydrogenation of trace acetylene. In contrast, isolated Cu single atom fails to promote Pt3 clusters and even deteriorate selectivity. These results demonstrate that Pt─Cu bond formation, rather than simple proximity, governs synergistic effects in bimetallic cluster catalysts. This work establishes a clear design principle for atomically engineered catalysts and offers a general strategy to independently optimize catalytic activity and selectivity.
n0c7ac7d0ad77: Despite the importance of heteroaryl atropisomers in medicinal chemistry and catalysis, straightforward access to these motifs via direct enantioselective C─H heteroaryl‐aryl coupling remains challenging. We report an enantioselective Pd(0)‐catalyzed arylation at the C4‐position of thiazole N‐oxides, forging the critical atropochiral axis. A designer point‐ and axially chiral monodentate phosphine is instrumental to enable high reactivities along with tight stereocontrol. A broad range of substrate combinations is coupled in high enantioselectivities, including two different heteroarenes. The enantioenriched thiazole N‐oxides are amenable to derivatizations around the substituents contributing to the stability of the chiral axis, including a reduction of the N‐oxide moiety without racemization.
n15248444703d: Herein, we report the Aza‐Büchner–Curtius–Schlotterbeck reaction (ABCS)– a novel method for the uncatalyzed C─C insertion reaction of photogenerated donor‐donor diazo compounds into aryl aldimines. The transformation proceeds under very mild conditions and high chemoselectivity, favoring C─C over C─H insertion pathways. In a single step, two C(sp2)─C(sp3) bonds are formed, granting access to homologated imines bearing a newly constructed quaternary carbon center in good yields. Subsequent hydrolysis gave homologated aldehydes, enabling versatile downstream transformations. The diazo intermediate is generated using a continuous‐flow microreactor, enhancing both safety and scalability. Mechanistic insights, supported by density functional theory (DFT) calculations, reveal the origins of the observed selectivity and reactivity.
n320d9e8f9aff: Photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production has emerged as a sustainable alternative to the energy-intensive anthraquinone process, yet its efficiency remains fundamentally limited by inefficient charge transport and electron-hole recombination. Here, we report a bioinspired strategy for constructing face-to-face supramolecular co-assembled arrays (FF-SCAAs), in which periodic co-facial organization serves as a structural platform for programming electron transport pathways toward enhanced photocatalytic H2O2 production. Inspired by the signal-transport arrays of natural compound eyes, cationic trioxatriangulenium (TOTA+ ) and electron-rich benzophenanthrene derivatives are integrated into highly ordered FF-SCAAs through directional cation-π interaction. The resulting FF-SCAAs feature enhanced dipole moments and favorable orbital alignment, enabling extended charge transport channels while intrinsically suppressing electron-hole recombination. On this basis, FF-SCAAs achieve a H2O2 photosynthesis rate up to 6.46 mmol g−1 h−1 with a solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency of 0.84%. Ultrafast spectroscopic and mechanistic studies demonstrate that the periodic co-facial arrays promote directional excited-state electron migration and selective two-electron oxygen reduction pathways for H2O2 generation. Furthermore, the in situ generated H2O2 is fed into a cascade wastewater treatment system and consumed in a downstream Fenton process for efficient degradation of phenolic pollutants.
n3d132543698e: Sluggish bulk hole transport fundamentally limits the performance of bismuth vanadate (BiVO4) photoanodes in photoelectrochemical (PEC) water splitting. Herein, we report a BiVO4/Fe-MOF/NiFeOOH trilayer photoanode, wherein an iron-based bipyridine dicarboxylate metal–organic framework (FeBPDCA), grown on BiVO4 via coordination-assisted in situ synthesis, serves as a dedicated hole-transport layer. The Fe-MOF layer provides a favorable band alignment and a built-in electric field at the BiVO4/Fe-MOF interface to drive directional bulk hole extraction, while NiFeOOH acts as a surface water-oxidation cocatalyst. Experimental characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the Fe-MOF primarily accelerates bulk hole extraction, whereas NiFeOOH suppresses surface recombination through rapid water oxidation, together boosting both bulk charge-separation efficiency (η bulk) and surface charge-transfer efficiency (η trans) up to 97%. The optimized photoanode achieves a high photocurrent density of 7.15 mA cm−2 at 1.23 V vs. RHE, with an onset potential of 0.24 V and a maximum applied bias photon-to-current efficiency (ABPE) of 2.56%. This work demonstrates that deliberate tuning of MOF energy levels through metal node and ligand selection enables the simultaneous engineering of favorable band alignment and efficient charge separation at semiconductor/MOF junctions, providing a practical design strategy for photoanodes where bulk charge extraction is the primary efficiency bottleneck.
n5a6df1c85780: We report that water undergoes rapid oxidative addition to readily accessible dioxaphospholes and ‐phospholanes within minutes at room temperature. The resulting phenylphosphinate esters release dihydrogen under mild conditions (room temperature to 60°C) in a borane‐catalyzed process. Remarkably, a pinacol‐derived dioxaphospholane reacts spontaneously with atmospheric moisture under ambient conditions to form the corresponding phenylphosphinate ester, thereby enabling the direct utilization of water from air for catalytic hydrogen evolution. The mechanism of the borane‐catalyzed dehydrogenation was investigated by variable time normalization analysis, targeted synthesis of intermediates, and DFT calculations. These studies support a catalytic pathway initiated by hydrogen elimination from the borane adduct of the phosphinate ester, followed by retro‐hydroboration to regenerate the catalyst.
n4f10ecefb24d: Lenacapavir (LEN), the first-in-class HIV-1 capsid inhibitor (CAI) with picomolar potency and long pharmacokinetics (PK), is approved for both treatment and pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP). However, the frequently selected M66I mutation confers complete resistance to LEN. Potent antivirals against the M66I variant remain elusive. In this work, we have designed LEN analogs featuring a distinctive R 2 moiety to directly address the molecular mechanism of resistance. Our analog synthesis also entailed developing a new synthetic procedure for R 2 incorporation. Significantly, the newly designed analogs were highly potent against both WT HIV-1 and the M66I mutant. Particularly, lead compound 3S conferred 2.6-fold higher potency than LEN against WT HIV-1 and remained highly potent (EC50 = 5.8 nM) against the M66I mutant, a drastically advanced activity profile over LEN (EC50 > 15 µM). The unprecedented potency of our lead 3S against M66I was corroborated by a thermal shift assay. In a head‑to‑head intravenous (IV) PK study in rats, lead 3S demonstrated superior systemic exposure, showing a 4.6‑fold greater plasma area-under-curve (AUC) than LEN and largely retaining the long PK characteristic of LEN. These results strongly validate our design and represent a breakthrough in LEN-based HIV-1 therapy and prophylaxis.
nb58f0620a7be: Transition‐metal‐catalyzed nitrene transfer reactions offer a powerful strategy for direct C─H bond amination; however, the nature of the key reactive intermediates, particularly with Cp*Co(III) systems, remains elusive. Herein, we report a cobalt‐catalyzed allylic C─H amidation of unactivated alkenes using dioxazolones as practical nitrene precursors. The isolation of a well‐defined π‐allyl‐cobalt(III) complex provides a platform for direct interrogation of the reactive nitrene species. Mechanistic studies, including EPR spectroscopy and DFT calculations, support the involvement of an open‐shell singlet cobalt–nitrenoid intermediate. Both the neutral cobalt(III) precatalyst and the synthesized π‐allyl‐cobalt(III) complex are catalytically active, and the catalytic system displays broad substrate scope, good functional‐group tolerance, and moderate to high regioselectivity. These results provide key mechanistic insights into cobalt‐mediated nitrene transfer reactions and establish a foundation for the development of selective cobalt‐catalyzed C─H amination reactions.
n7674ca4520f5: The introduction of ortho‐methyl substituents on aryl‐substituted ortho‐tetrafluoroazobenzene photoswitches breaks the π‐conjugation and improves photoswitching selectivity and increases the thermal half‐life of the metastable isomer. Using this approach, a visible‐light‐responsive ligand was assembled with a non‐switchable ligand and palladium(II) ions into a mixture of molecular cages. When irradiated with 530 nm light, the system converges to form a single product, a metastable, mixed‐ligand molecular cage. This cage can be reversibly disassembled using 424 nm light, an example of integrative self‐sorting controlled by light. The metastable assembly can catalyze both Michael addition and nitroaldol reactions. Importantly, visible light accesses a metastable catalytic state inaccessible under thermodynamic control. We demonstrate that the active assembled species can be switched on and off at will using visible irradiation and the metastable species is the most catalytically active assembly.
nafacf0e3f208: Catalyst‐controlled nitrene transfer enables divergent amination reactions of bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes through distinct modes of activation of their highly strained central σ‐bond. Under Rh(II) catalysis, bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes undergo selective strain‐release amination to furnish aminocyclobutenes, which provide efficient access to cyclobutane amino acids through a simple amination–hydrogenation sequence. In contrast, photocatalytic nitrene activation redirects the reaction pathway toward double amination and skeletal remodeling, affording functionalized dihydropyrrolidines that can be readily converted into pyrrole heterocycles under acidic conditions. The synthetic utility of both approaches is further demonstrated, for example, in a telescoped synthesis of cyclobutane amino acids from diazo precursors or downstream diversification reactions. Mechanistic experiments and computational studies reveal distinct catalyst‐dependent nitrene activation pathways that govern the fate of a common reactive intermediate and underpin the observed divergent reactivity.
n0b1aa42e57c4: Photo‐induced hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) catalysis has become a powerful platform for the direct and selective functionalization of ubiquitous C─H bonds. Traditionally, the outcome of these transformations is dictated by the interplay between C─H bond dissociation energies and polar effects, enabling predictable yet inherently substrate‐controlled selectivity. Recently, a fundamentally new strategy has emerged that relies on the catalytic and reversible modulation of substrate electronics to transiently enhance the reactivity of targeted C─H bonds. Notably, catalytic full or partial deprotonation of oxygen‐ and nitrogen‐containing functional groups has proven remarkably effective in selectively activating adjacent C─H bonds toward HAT, a phenomenon known as the anionic substituent effect. Rather than relying solely on the intrinsic properties of a substrate, this concept allows chemists to reprogram C─H bond reactivity in situ, unlocking previously inaccessible levels of selectivity in the direct functionalization of abundant functional groups under mild photocatalytic conditions. In this minireview, we discuss the mechanistic principles underpinning catalytic anionic substituent effects (CASE), the diverse strategies developed to generate them, and their impact on photocatalytic HAT‐mediated C–H functionalization. By highlighting recent advances and emerging opportunities, we illustrate how transient electronic activation is reshaping the design of selective C–H functionalization reactions.
na1a3b0fa4025: There has been a recent surge in research aimed at synthesizing inherently chiral macrocycles that lack point, axial, planar, or helical chirality. To overcome the structural limitations of existing inherently chiral macrocyclic systems, which often suffer from facile racemization due to conformational flexibility, we report herein an asymmetric synthesis of a new class of inherently chiral double‐macrocyclic molecules through an intramolecular macrocyclization strategy, employing calix[4]arenes as the starting platform. Catalyzed by [Pd(allyl)Cl]2 and a chiral phosphoramidite ligand, calix[4]arene derivatives bearing a monoaryl bromide linker at the upper rim underwent a facile enantioselective remote transannular Suzuki–Miyaura coupling with the adjacent upper‐rim position of the neighboring arene unit, furnishing the desired inherently chiral double‐calixarene macrocycles in up to 71% yield and 91% ee. The resulting double macrocycles feature stable conformations and unique semi‐enveloped chiral cavities, and exhibit promising chiral catalytic and chiroptical properties.
n647b387306d5: Purely organic luminescent materials are pivotal for optoelectronics, with chalcogen‐fused phenazines serving as basic building blocks owing to their strong electron donating ability and enhanced spin–orbit coupling effect. However, a systematic understanding of how the chalcogen identity governs intrinsic conformational preference between quasi‐axial (QA) and quasi‐equatorial (QE) forms remains elusive. To address this, we designed a series of derivatives featuring phenoxazine, phenothiazine, and phenoselenazine donors coupled with a terpyridine acceptor. We demonstrate that the chalcogen atom dictates molecular conformation: phenoxazine derivative exclusively adopts the QE conformation, phenothiazine derivative predominantly favors QE, while phenoselenazine derivative stabilizes in the QA form. Notably, heating induces a phase transition in polymorphs toward their thermodynamically favored conformations. Furthermore, Zn2+ coordination enhances intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) strength, shifting the thermodynamically preferred conformation and triggering a switch from room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) to dual RTP–delayed fluorescence (DF) emission. This work validates the chalcogen‐determined conformation and ICT strength can effectively modulates DF/RTP performance, deepening the fundamental understanding of the chalcogen‐mediated conformation and properties for the rational design of organic luminescent materials.
n4bf9e90ab524: Polyketides constitute a major class of natural products with remarkable structural diversity and biological activities. While bacteria predominantly produce polyketides via modular type I polyketide synthases (PKSs), eukaryotic modular PKSs remain largely unexplored. Here, we report the functional characterization of a fungal modular PKS system from Lasiodiplodia theobromae through heterologous expression in Aspergillus oryzae, leading to the production of the antimalarial macrolide strasseriolide C (1). Intriguingly, biosynthesis of 1 involves C‐methylation of the starter malonyl unit despite the absence of a methyltransferase domain in the loading module. Furthermore, module 2 of the PKS system contains an unusual arrangement of four consecutive acyl carrier protein (ACP) domains. Although the catalytic basis of this methylation remains unresolved, our isotope‐labeling experiments, mutational analyses, and in vitro biochemical assays support a model in which the malonyl unit loaded onto the module 2 ACPs is transferred to the loading ACP, where starter‐unit methylation is proposed to occur prior to chain initiation. Our study reveals unexpected biosynthetic logic and establishes a foundation for mechanistic studies and engineering of eukaryotic modular PKSs.
n67e637e15c0f: The stereochemical outcomes of pericyclic reactions provide direct insight into the geometry and directionality of concerted bond reorganization. Although torquoselectivity has emerged as a defining concept for electrocyclizations, an analogous principle for sigmatropic rearrangements on a single cyclic π system has remained unknown. We report that a homoannulene‐based photoswitch undergoes an auxiliary‐controlled, stereoselective photochemical [1,11]‐sigmatropic rearrangement, thereby establishing selectivity over directional migration on a single cyclic π framework. We coin the term calderoselectivity for such an unreported stereoselective sigmatropic rearrangement. The switching process is reversible, proceeds to photostationary mixtures of homoannulene and iso‐homoannulene isomers, and furnishes diastereomeric products in a 56:44 ratio; combined chiral HPLC, NMR, ECD, and DFT studies assign the major directionality of acyl migration in pro‐R directionality. This study provides the first experimental realization of calderoselectivity and reveals a direct analogue in sigmatropic rearrangements to torquoselectivity with implications for both mechanistic physical organic chemistry and chiroptical switch design.
n98bb4c98dc6c: Achieving general asymmetric catalytic manifolds that accommodate broad substrate diversity remains a long‐standing and highly sought‐after goal in synthetic chemistry. Herein, we report an efficient cobalt‐catalyzed desymmetric hydrogenation of structurally diverse cyclic 1,2‐ and 1,3‐diacid anhydrides, enabling access to pharmaceutically relevant chiral γ‐ and δ‐lactones with broad substrate scope and excellent enantioselectivity (up to 99% ee). The reaction is readily scalable, as demonstrated by gram‐scale synthesis of several representative products. Notably, this 3d‐metal catalytic platform represents a rare example that outperforms platinum‐group‐metal‐based counterparts in both generality and stereoselectivity. DFT studies identify a catalytically active d7 Co(II) dihydride complex with an outer‐sphere hydride transfer mechanism, wherein a relatively flexible chiral pocket underlies the broad substrate compatibility of this catalytic system.
n3c8cebfcd1c6: Strained bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) have emerged as versatile precursors for accessing highly reactive intermediates, enabling unconventional bond constructions through strain‐release pathways. Herein, we report a cobalt(II)‐catalyzed strategy that combines thermal activation of BCBs with selective radical capture by Co(II) to afford head‐to‐head fused bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes (BCHex). We propose that thermal activation of the BCB generates a reactive diradical intermediate, which is intercepted by a tailored bidentate phosphine Co(II) cationic complex via oxidative radical coupling, followed by a [2σ+2π] cycloaddition with indoles. Mechanistic investigations, including 31P NMR spectroscopy, cyclic voltammetry, electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), and density functional theory (DFT) studies, provide insights into the plausible reaction pathway. The involvement of paramagnetic Co(II) species is consistent with the broad features observed in both EPR and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra of the catalyst. In addition, four structurally distinct Co(II) complexes were synthesized, fully characterized by UV–Vis and Fourier‐transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, and evaluated as catalysts for the transformation. The cationic nature of the Co(II) species was further confirmed by phosphine oxide trapping experiments and single‐crystal X‐ray crystallography.
n60a494e0f275: Selectivity of electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (ECO2RR) is typically pursued by optimizing immobilized catalyst films biased at constant potential, an approach referred to as “catalyst‐fixed electrochemistry”. This architecture hinges on two variables that are difficult to tune: the electron‐transfer (ET) environment and local mass transport. Here we introduce a fundamentally different concept: a “catalyst‐fluidized electrochemistry” platform, where freely suspended catalyst particles make stochastic, short‐lived contacts with the electrode. This dynamic system co‐engineers the ET duty cycle (intermittent vs. continuous) and the local proton supply (spherical/fast vs. planar/slow transport), transforming two traditional constraints into tunable operating parameters. Co‐modulating these levers and, when desired varying them independently, improves the selectivity of high‐value products and reveals how each steers pathway branching. Using AuCu2 nanoparticles as a model catalyst, fluidization boosts 9.2‐fold and 2.5‐fold enhancement in Faradaic efficiency (FE) for ethylene (C2H4) and formic acid (HCOOH) under high and low overpotentials, respectively, relative to the corresponding fixed‐film configuration. Pulsed‐potential emulation isolates ET intermittency, while experiments together with DFT‐informed microkinetic modeling indicate that increased surface proton availability further biases the reaction toward C2 formation at high overpotentials. Reaction environment programming thus emerges as a catalyst‐agnostic lever for reconfiguring reaction networks, complementing conventional materials design.
n65bd1637e7e4: Flavonoid 6‐O‐glycosides from Carthamus tinctorius (safflower) represent a unique class of potential antithrombotic agents. However, their pharmaceutical development has been hindered by limited natural resources. In this study, we characterized four key biosynthetic enzymes from C. tinctorius: Ct6OGT (6‐O‐glycosyltransferase), Ct7OGT (7‐O‐glycosyltransferase), Ct3OGT (3‐O‐glycosyltransferase), and CtFLS (flavonol synthase). Among them, Ct6OGT is the first identified high‐regioselectivity flavonoid 6‐O‐glycosyltransferase. By combining these enzymes with upstream genes identified from safflower, we established an in vitro enzymatic approach for the synthesis of 6‐hydroxykaempferol 3,6,7‐tri‐O‐glycosides. Notably, enzymatic assays demonstrated that the 3,6,7‐O‐triglycosides were synthesized via a sequential linear glycosylation pathway, in the order of 6‐O‐, 7‐O‐, and finally 3‐O‐glycosylation. Through combinatorial biosynthesis, we further produced 26 flavonoid 6‐O‐glycosides, including naturally occurring compounds from C. tinctorius and novel analogs. Subsequent evaluation in a zebrafish model revealed these flavonoid 6‐O‐glycosides exhibited antithrombotic activities, with 6‐hydroxylation and 6‐O‐glycosylation remarkably enhancing the potency. This work represents the first report of an enzymatic synthetic method for flavonoid 6‐O‐glycosides, and provides a valuable foundation for their future drug development.
n7233ce2d39f0: Aqueous solutions of HF and HCl behave very differently at intermediate concentrations: HCl dissociates completely, whereas HF only partially dissociates and forms bifluoride (HF2−${\rm HF}_2^-$). This should lead to markedly different excess‐proton spectra in HF and HCl solutions, in contrast to experimental reports. Using ab initio molecular dynamics, we show that in HF the proton is not firmly bound to F−${\rm F}^-$, as suggested by textbook chemistry, but dynamically shared with a hydrating water molecule. This is rationalized by a modified Eigen‐picture description which also explains the formation of HF2−${\rm HF}_2^-$. The similar vibrational spectra of HF and HCl solutions are explained by a complementary Zundel picture in terms of almost identical excess proton transfer free‐energy profiles for HF and HCl. These results reconcile thermodynamic and spectroscopic observations and provide a unified microscopic picture of excess protons in aqueous solution.
n42078b9bdccf: Chemically induced protein dimerisation (CID) is a widely used approach for detecting and actuating small‐molecule‐protein interactions. Here, we demonstrate that CID systems can be used as building blocks for higher‐order ligand‐controlled protein systems. To this end, we converted classical FK506‐ and cyclosporine A‐controlled CIDs into single‐chain pseudo‐allosteric proteins. These systems displayed 15‐ and 50‐fold gains in ligand affinity compared with the parental components operating in trans. Using these fusion proteins as baits in mRNA display, we identified FN3con binding domains that recognise the holo state of each bait with subnanomolar affinity and >100‐fold selectivity over the apo form. Integration of the binding domains and intramolecular CIDs into two‐component enzymatic protein biosensors enabled quantification of the cognate ligands with low‐nanomolar limits of detection (LODs). ELISA assays based on the developed systems displayed mid‐picomolar LODs and accurately quantified FK506 and cyclosporine A in unprocessed blood samples from transplant patients with accuracy comparable to that of LC‐MS/MS. This work establishes a generalisable strategy for harnessing the affinity gains of intramolecular CID systems to create gain‐of‐signal assays for small molecules and ions.
n30c16ce7aaf8: Ethane‐selective adsorbents enable direct production of high‐purity ethylene, yet rational improvement of selectivity and productivity remains challenging. Here, we report a strategy of adaptive flexibility control. A family of isostructural metal azolate frameworks featuring bent linkers and size‐tunable substituents were designed and synthesized. Single‐crystal X‐ray diffraction and computational simulations unveiled a bending‐adsorption coupling mechanism: the stronger ethane binding drives more pronounced linker flattening to reinforce itself. Crucially, bulkier substituents reinforce this adaptive response, further elevating ethane selectivity. Notably, mixture breakthrough experiments demonstrated that navigating the selectivity–capacity trade‐off via substituent‐tuned adaptive flexibility afforded superior ethylene purification productivity.
nee548eea2177: Solar‐driven direct propane dehydrogenation (PDH) represents a promising strategy to overcome the high‐temperature demands and selectivity limitations of conventional thermocatalysis, yet the identification of effective photoactive phases remains challenging. In situ spectroscopic analyses combined with density functional theory calculations reveal a photoactivated dual‐site mechanism, in which PtO2 nanoparticles function as oxidation centers for hole‐driven C─H bond activation, whereas neighboring interfacial Pt single atoms act as electron‐accepting sites to promote H2 evolution, enabling efficient spatial separation and utilization of photogenerated charge carriers. Catalyst deactivation arises from partial reduction of PtO2, which can be exactly regenerated via a facile oxidative annealing process in air, affording excellent reusability. These findings identify photoactivated PtO2 as a distinct active phase for selective PDH and provide a design principle for solar‐driven alkane valorization.
n7cafd0a1d52c: Organic diradicals with stimuli‐responsive spin interaction tunability have attracted considerable interest due to their unique controllable magnetic behaviors. After coordination, the spin interaction through boron is weakened, resulting in a significant reduction in the antiferromagnetic coupling strength while shortening the average spin‐spin distance. The non‐coordinated form possesses a singlet ground state, while the adduct has nearly degenerate singlet and triplet states. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first experimental demonstration of coordination‐triggered coupling pathway control in organic diradical cations, thereby providing a new approach for controlling spin interactions through chemical coordination.
n7c63ecde7a29: Cooks and coworkers (Angewandte Chemie 65 (2026), e1888676, https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.1888676) claim that cyclic ketones are oxidized by H2O•+. ncd84eaa0fcce: Polyglycolide (PGA) is a leading biodegradable polyester, but controlled access to high‐molecular‐weight PGA remains challenging. The resulting high‐molecular‐weight PGA exhibits high crystallinity and tensile strength, highlighting (thio)urea‐alkoxide covalent integration as a powerful strategy for the precision synthesis of high‐performance biodegradable polyesters.
n576cc79419e9: The completeness of photoswitching is a key figure of merit for molecular photoswitches. The resulting supramolecular polymer assembles in aqueous media and undergoes light‐induced disassembly in the condensed phase. In the broader context, coupling photoswitching to threshold‐dependent assembly provides a novel route to convert subtle changes in PSS composition into an amplified, non‐linear supramolecular response.
n4e37667c1b4b: Soft porous crystals exploit adaptive structural dynamics for molecular recognition, yet their elusive nature hinders the fundamental understanding of rational design and reliable applications. n8b4b6c232077: A direct difluoromethylenation of alkynes has been developed using HF/pyridine as a dual acidic and fluorinating medium. n69833b0e3ee2: Chiral β‐hydroxy‐α‐amino amides represent important structural motifs ubiquitous in pharmaceuticals and bioactive molecules. n311aa419b647: Two geranylated chalcone oligomers, artocarpusones A (1) and B (2), featuring a highly functionalized 6/5/6/5/6‐fused pentacyclic hemiketal, were discovered from the medicinal plant Artocarpus communis, along with six related compounds 3−8. n4079b6b993f2: The detection of soluble amyloid-β (Aβ), the most neurotoxic species in early Alzheimer's disease (AD), remains a major analytical challenge. ne22bf045228d: Chiral self‐sorting enables molecular systems to translate stereochemical information from small building blocks into highly organized architectures across length scales, echoing the hierarchical expression of chirality in biological systems. In both cases, the products form cleanly without detectable stereoisomeric byproducts, and their stereochemical assignments are confirmed by X‐ray crystallography. Computational analyses support the view that distinct linker conformational preferences provide a rationale for the divergent sorting pathways. This work establishes COPs as a model platform for understanding chiral self‐sorting and provides a conceptual basis for selecting, amplifying, and expressing stereochemical information in complex molecular architectures.
ne379f9e6c636: Manipulating the spillover of reactants represents a pivotal strategy to govern reaction pathways and boost the efficiency of heterogeneous catalysis, enabling reactive species to spontaneously navigate the path of least kinetic resistance. ne6cb2a18b7de: Preparative biocatalytic synthesis of substituted pyrroles remains challenging despite recent advances in enzymatic α‐aminoketone generation. nc4e865cc4d4b: Diffusion models (DMs) have emerged as a class of generative models for controllable small-molecule design in drug discovery capable of progressively transforming noisy or partially specified molecular states into candidate structures under structural, geometric, and property constraints. This Review provides a comprehensive overview of the methodological foundations and representative applications of diffusion-based molecular generation, emphasizing the alignment among molecular representations, generative dynamics, controllable design, and evaluation and validation. Particular attention is given to recent advances in property- and structure-guided generation, target-aware and fragment-based design, multiobjective optimization, and synthesis-aware generation. We also discuss the roles of data sets, computational evaluation, and prospective experiments in assessing the chemical and biological relevance of generated molecules. By organizing these developments within a unified conceptual framework, we provide computational chemists and drug discovery researchers with a structured roadmap that balances the mathematical rigor with chemical intuition. Throughout, we highlight current methodological limitations and unresolved challenges and conclude with future directions toward chemically credible and experimentally grounded molecular design. To facilitate navigation of this rapidly evolving field, we introduce an interactive companion platform (https://diffsmd.scbdd.com) that provides a curated, continuously updated repository of model architectures and visualizations.

n227f7a0289e3: Two-dimensional (2D) magnetic skyrmions hold great promise for next-generation high-density information storage, yet their low-dimensional behavior and controllable size remain challenging. ne120cc753fcc: Directional charge transport is essential for efficient photocatalysis, yet carrier transfer in semiconductor nanocrystals is often random and limited by recombination. Combined spectroscopic measurements, radical-trapping experiments, and density functional theory calculations reveal a phonon-enhanced directional charge-transfer mechanism. These findings provide a general strategy for regulating directional charge transport through lattice dynamics.

n1c026acdafcf: The self-labeling protein HaloTag is used to install a wide variety of functional small molecules in cells and living organisms with exquisite specificity with respect to cell type and subcellular localization. HaloTag is a core part of many biotechnology-based tools for sensing, tracking, and manipulating biological systems with a high degree of spatial and temporal control. Due to the limitations of fluorescent proteins and other self-labeling proteins, most of these tools have historically been restricted to a single channel. In this work, we used structure-guided rational design and directed evolution to produce an orthogonal HaloTag protein called OrthoTag which reacts selectively with a modified chloroalkane substrate. OrthoTag retains many of HaloTag’s superior properties, and reaction rate measurements with purified proteins show OrthoTag and its substrate have 109-fold mutual orthogonality to HaloTag with respect to substrate concentration. We demonstrate the application of OrthoTag for multiplexed labeling experiments in mammalian cells with minimal optimization. Going forward, OrthoTag should be straightforward to incorporate into HaloTag-based systems to allow simultaneous measurement or manipulation of two biological targets or processes. The availability of multiple high-performance self-labeling proteins will enable the continued development of new multiplexed biotechnology methods.
nad25f0b3765c: Conversion of μ-N2 complexes into nitrogenous compounds is one of the most important and challenging chemical transformations in N2 fixation. Although photochemical N2 splitting has been demonstrated, existing approaches predominantly rely on high-energy ultraviolet light that generally affords low efficiency and poor selectivity. Herein, we establish a visible-light-driven molecular photosensitization strategy that enables efficient and selective N–N bond cleavage in a dinuclear rhenium dinitrogen complex. Blue light excitation of the organic photosensitizer 4DPAIPN (2,4,5,6-tetrakis(diphenylamino)isophthalonitrile) is shown to initiate N–N scission to afford the corresponding rhenium nitride in 96% yield. Kinetic analysis of nanosecond transient absorption data through the Balzani-Scandola model indicates energy transfer from the photosensitizer to an acceptor state that lies approximately 2.31 eV above the ground state of the μ-N2-bridged dirhenium complex. This photosensitization strategy decouples light harvesting from N–N bond activation, eliminates the need for UV light, and shows broad applicability across different visible-light absorbing photosensitizers, including transition metal complexes and organic chromophores with long-lived, high-energy triplet excited-states. These findings establish dye-sensitization as a powerful strategy for visible-light-driven N–N bond cleavage for mechanistic study and the future realization of a photochemical pathway for nitrogen fixation.
n1125d752fa9d: The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is a key heterogeneous process underpinning energy conversion, catalytic, and sensing technologies. However, reported ORR kinetics at oxide surfaces often vary widely because surface chemistry evolves under operating conditions. Ceria-based fluorites have been proposed as protective layers to stabilize perovskite electrodes, but ORR kinetics are typically considered sluggish and reported values have large variability. Herein, we demonstrate that cathodic polarization triggers an unexpected activation in Gd-doped ceria (CGO) dense thin films at 500 °C, enabling oxygen incorporation rates that surpass state-of-the-art materials such as La0.5Sr0.5FeO3−δ and approach the performance of La0.6Sr0.4CoO3−δ. Operando near-ambient-pressure X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (NAP-XPS), supported by ex situ surface-sensitive tip-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (TERS), reveals that CGO surface activation coincides with a reversible, overpotential-dependent modulation of sulfate adsorbates. Integration of these measurements with nondilute space-charge modeling suggests that charged adsorbates dynamically tune the near-surface electrostatic potential and electron concentration, thereby controlling oxygen incorporation kinetics. These results support adsorbate-induced electrostatic effects as a key mechanism in ceria and show that ORR kinetics are dynamically set by surface chemistry under operation, rather than by intrinsic bulk defect chemistry alone.
nd73468d2ad0b: Strong metal–support interaction (SMSI) plays an important role in heterogeneous catalysis, but remains poorly understood, particularly on the origin of SMSI under an oxidative atmosphere. Hereby grand canonical structure exploration of over 4 million bulk PtTi alloys and Pt or PtTi-supported Ti oxide (TiOx) surface structure candidates, we resolve the Pt/TiOx system, a text-book example of SMSI, under both reductive and oxidative conditions: it experiences an encapsulation─deep encapsulation─decapsulation dynamic reconstruction under a sequence of H2 reduction─O2 oxidation─H2 plus O2 redox thermal treatment. The whole process was kinetically simulated by long-time (69 ns) molecular dynamics simulations, revealing in detail how a 3 nm Pt nanoparticle undergoes nonclassical SMSI under an oxidative and redox atmosphere. We find that Pt-assisted TiO2 amorphization is the key to the transition of various SMSI states at different conditions, which elevates Ti chemical potential via amorphization toward low-coordinated [TiO4]. Finally, explainable machine learning models were developed to predict nonclassical SMSI cases and clarify their rarity in nature.
n686ef4beffc8: Through-space charge-transfer thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TSCT-TADF) emitters often employ conformationally constrained donor–acceptor architectures to control through-space electronic coupling, particularly for long-wavelength emission. Here, we report conformationally adaptive orange-to-red TSCT-TADF emitters based on an S-shaped donor−π–acceptor−π–donor framework composed of phenoxazine donors, xanthene linkers, and a dibenzo[a,j]phenazine acceptor. Structural and NMR analyses reveal substantial conformational mobility, while systematic conformational searches and excited-state calculations identify thermally accessible conformers with distinct donor–acceptor geometries and excited-state characteristics. Comparative studies with reference compounds and fragment-resolved transition-density analysis show that the xanthene linker primarily acts as a conformational regulator and that the low-energy CT states have predominant TSCT character with only minor linker involvement. Temperature-dependent early-time photoluminescence measurements reveal continuous spectral relaxation in fluid toluene that slows upon cooling and is absent in rigid Zeonex and mCBP hosts, providing strong evidence for structural relaxation following photoexcitation within a pre-existing conformational ensemble. The emitters exhibit orange-to-red TADF with reverse intersystem crossing rates on the order of 105–106 s–1. Organic light-emitting diodes employing these emitters show electroluminescence at 598–624 nm, external quantum efficiencies up to 14.9%, and limited efficiency roll-off over a broad luminance range. These results demonstrate that efficient long-wavelength TSCT-TADF can be realized without permanent conformational locking and establish a framework for understanding the interplay between ground-state conformational heterogeneity and excited-state structural relaxation.
n3f51902218b4: Selective photocatalytic methane coupling requires directing methane-derived intermediates toward C–C bond formation while limiting their oxidation to CO2, yet how the reaction environment controls this competition through surface chemistry remains unclear. Water is ubiquitous in photocatalytic methane conversion, but its influence is commonly interpreted through specific chemical functions rather than through its broader effects on working-surface chemistry. Here, Au/ZnO is used as a compositionally defined, coupling-competent model catalyst to reveal how hydration regulates carbon transformation pathways by reshaping the working-surface chemistry. Systematic variation of water availability reveals three hydration-dependent catalytic regimes with markedly different product distributions. Moderate hydration increases the ethane production rate from 1590 to 8407 μmol g–1 h–1 and enables ethylene formation, whereas excessive hydration increases CO2 production and lowers C2 selectivity. In situ spectroscopies show that these catalytic regimes are accompanied by hydration-dependent changes in methane adsorption, methane-derived and coupling-related surface intermediates, and oxygen-deficient surface states within a reaction network involving both carbon- and oxygen-centered radical chemistry. Moderate hydration establishes surface conditions that favor C–C coupling and C2 hydrocarbon accumulation, whereas excessive hydration favors oxidized surface species and carbonate formation. These results identify hydration as a key determinant of the steady-state surface chemistry governing carbon partitioning between C–C coupling and oxidation during photocatalytic methane conversion.
nb17eec0f1db6: Lithium metal batteries promise high-energy-density storage but are limited by unstable solid–electrolyte interphases, which couple poor passivation, sluggish Li+ transport, dendritic deposition, and safety risks. Herein, we report a multiphase inorganic-rich solid–electrolyte interphase (m-SEI) containing P- and Al-derived species including Li3P, LiAl5O8, Li3PO4, and Li2Al, which is formed from the in situ reaction between a flame-retardant aluminum diethyl hypophosphite (ADP) interlayer and lithium metal. This multicomponent inorganic SEI enables an integrated capture-transport mechanism by combining high Li+ affinity, facilitated desolvation, and low-barrier Li+ migration pathways in individual inorganic phases and their heterophase interfaces, thereby facilitating rapid Li+ interfacial migration. Its chemical inertness and high Young’s modulus of 17.14 GPa further suppress electrolyte decomposition and Li dendrite growth. As a result, the Li-metal batteries with m-SEI deliver an extended lifespan of 1000 h at a high current density of 4 mA cm–2. Li||NCM811 full cells with a high cathode loading (20 mg cm–2) and ultrathin Li foil (50 μm) retain 80% capacity after 250 cycles, while Li||NCM811 pouch cells retain 90% capacity after 500 cycles. This work establishes the capture-transport mechanism as an effective design principle for regulating Li+ interfacial dynamics and offers a practical interphase-engineering strategy for constructing ion-conductive and chemically protective interphases in durable lithium metal batteries.
n44ef863c88dd: Muscle integrates molecular-machine motion with hierarchical structural organization, enabling it to sustain large deformations under physiological loads. Mechanically interlocked molecules offer a versatile platform to mimic such molecular-level motion, but efficiently translating it into macroscopic material performance, akin to muscle, remains challenging. Herein, we report a mechanically interlocked network (MIN) with [an]daisy chain backbone which can efficiently scale up the photoresponsive behavior of mechanical bonds, exhibiting intelligently tunable mechanical properties. In specific, photoresponsive unit of arylazopyrazole (AAP) is embedded onto the axis of each mechanical bond in the [an]daisy chain backbone. Ultraviolet light triggers the trans-to-cis (E/Z) isomerization of the AAP moieties, and when amplified through the [an]daisy chain backbone, it brings about significant changes in the material’s properties. On one hand, the E/Z isomerization significantly shortens the dimension of the [an]daisy chain framework, resulting in a notable increase in the material modulus (from 1.6 to 4.0 MPa). On the other hand, the cis configuration of AAP formed after the isomerization restricts the mobility of the mechanical bonds, resulting in a shorter elongation at break (from 343% to 272%). Our work presents an efficient method for amplifying mechanical bond responsiveness, providing a fresh perspective for the development of intelligent materials.
n174370785002: Designing redox proteins with predictable and tunable electron transfer properties is a major goal in de novo bioenergetics. Here we show that replacing heme B with a series of structurally conservative non-natural metalloporphyrins enables broad modulation of redox potentials over 400 mV in the de novo designed monoheme m4D2 and diheme 4D2 T19D. The non-natural porphyrins bind with high affinity and do not compromise either the heme binding site or global protein structure, as evidenced by X-ray crystallography and NMR spectroscopy. We also report the native-like NMR structure of m4D2 loaded with the non-natural and symmetric iron 2,4-dimethyldeuteroporphyrin IX, confirming our modular approach to tetrahelical redox protein design. This work establishes a versatile platform for constructing tunable electron carriers for engineered bioenergetic pathways and bioelectronic applications.
n7c7c5ec875e8: Achieving switchable 2e–/4e– oxygen reduction selectivity within a single molecular catalyst remains an unmet challenge because the key metal–oxygen intermediate typically commits to one pathway. Herein, we demonstrate that this limitation can be overcome by elevating the basicity of the peroxo intermediate to a level where both proton-transfer (PT) and proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) manifolds become accessible, with the dominant pathway dictated solely by the external acid strength. A dicobalt μ-1,2-peroxo complex supported by an electron-rich macrocyclic poly-NHC ligand exhibits a computed pKa1 of ∼8.8, placing it in a unique thermodynamic window. Stoichiometric protonation bifurcates cleanly: strong acids (HClO4) trigger rapid diprotonation to release H2O2, whereas weak acids (Et3NHOTf) promote O–O bond cleavage to afford a μ-hydroxo complex. Under catalytic conditions, this dichotomy translates into complete selectivity switching─100% H2O2 with HClO4 versus 90% H2O with Et3NHOTf, accompanied by a switch in the rate-determining step from O2 binding to PCET (KIE = 1.60). Crucially, a structurally analogous but less basic peroxo complex predictably inverts the selectivity to H2O under identical conditions, providing a closed-loop validation of the basicity-selectivity relationship. These results establish intermediate basicity as a general, tunable design parameter for programming product selectivity in multielectron catalysis.
nc4334b8e5e80: Methanetetrol, C(OH)4 (orthocarbonic acid), is an elusive tethrahydroxymethane that, due to its rapid dissociation under ambient conditions, has never been synthesized in bulk. A recent study detected the formation of C(OH)4 molecules in the gas phase. Here, we show that C(OH)4 can be synthesized in a diamond anvil cell through the reaction between H2O and CO2 at 45(3) GPa and 50(3) GPa and temperatures <1200(200) K. The crystal structure of C(OH)4 was determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and corroborated by density-functional theory calculations together with Raman spectroscopy. It is composed of isolated [C(OH)4]-molecules linked by strong hydrogen bonds. Under high-pressure conditions, orthocarbonic and carbonic acids are denser than coexisting water ice phases, allowing them to segregate gravitationally and form stable reservoirs of oxidized carbon. These phases incorporate large amounts of carbon into their crystal structures as part of [CO4]4–- or [CO3]2–-building blocks. Because the amount of carbon that can be stored as CO2 in clathrates or filled-ices is significantly smaller, orthocarbonic and carbonic acids may provide a host mechanism for sequestering large carbon inventories in the icy mantles of water-rich exoplanets.
nd967541ceaac: Manganese-based cation-disordered rock-salt (DRX) cathodes offer high capacities without relying on cobalt and nickel, but maintaining that capacity over extended cycling often requires bulk fluorination. The challenge is that incorporating fluorine into Mn-rich DRX host structures is hindered by unfavorable thermodynamics and the stability of LiF, often necessitating elevated synthesis temperatures that promote severe lithium and fluorine volatilization. This study overcomes that limitation by manipulating the solid-state reaction pathway using unconventional Li6MnO4 and MnF2 precursors in a challenging Mn-rich model system (Li1.2Mn0.6Ti0.2O2–xFx). This precursor engineering strategy reshapes the thermodynamic landscape. Computational modeling and in situ X-ray diffraction reveal that by using reactive starting materials, we suppress the crystallization of less reactive intermediates, enabling bulk fluorination at a lower temperature. The resulting DRX retains both a high fluorine content and the lithium excess required for three-dimensional percolation, delivering improved electrochemical performance relative to material synthesized from conventional precursors.
n108e93789bdc: Most luminescent clusters that exhibit pronounced chiral signals typically rely on predesigned chiral ligands; however, stimulating the intrinsic chirality of clusters in the absence of exogenous asymmetric ligands remains a significant challenge. In this study, based on a series of structure-correlated Cu2 clusters, we demonstrate that intramolecular spatial confinement effectively induces distortions in flexible ligands, thereby imparting asymmetry to the cluster framework. This molecular asymmetry further determines the orientation of cluster entities during supramolecular assembly, thus enabling the modulation of chirality across this cluster series between inactive (“off”) and active (“on”) states. In addition, these structure-correlated Cu2 clusters display bright and tunable luminescence, allowing for the fabrication of uniform thin films that function as practical scintillation materials for high-resolution X-ray imaging. Collectively, this work provides a novel perspective for regulating the chiroptical properties of metal clusters through the activation of intramolecular spatial confinement and offers valuable insights into the fabrication of cluster-based nanomaterials with tailored photophysical performances.
nb5bcd12a1be3: This review examines how the intrinsic properties of zinc metal influence its stability in aqueous electrolytes, highlighting multiscale correlations among morphology, microstructure, electronic structure, and electrochemical behavior. It outlines emerging strategies and future directions for enhancing zinc reversibility and utilization toward practical aqueous zinc ion batteries.
n583e5ff018c5: Hybridization of light and excitons can change how materials absorb and emit light, but achieving this in the ultraviolet remains challenging. We show that a layered silver phenylthiolate forms hybrid light-matter states in simple mirror structures. This material expands the options for controlling ultraviolet light and provides a foundation for exploring future light sources and light-driven chemistry.
n294045e42341: Tunnel junctions are essential for various technologies ranging from classical microelectronics to quantum information and cryogenic electronics. Aluminum and its oxide (AlOx) have long dominated cryogenic and quantum tunnel junction applications for their excellent material quality and superconductivity. However, some applications require junctions to remain normal conducting, either as standalone components or integrated with superconducting circuitry. Magnetic fields, impurity doping, or proximity effects can suppress superconductivity, but often pose challenges for scalability and integration. Here, we present a CMOS-compatible normal conducting tunnel junction platform using TiW alloy electrodes and AlOx tunnel barriers, achieving high yield and uniformity through wafer-scale fabrication. As a cryogenic use-case, the wafers incorporate junction arrays designed for Coulomb blockade thermometry, confirming reliable normal conducting state performance down to 20 mK. These results demonstrate a scalable and integrable normal conducting junction technology, supporting its use in cryogenic, quantum, and nanoelectronic systems, including hybrid superconducting-normal metal circuits.
n424346185a23: The sodium–potassium pump (Na,K-ATPase) is an essential plasma-membrane transporter that consumes 20%–30% of cellular energy, and up to approximately 50% in the kidneys. Whether it assembles into defined oligomers in its native membrane has been debated for decades. Resolving this question demands imaging precision at molecular length scales. Here, we combine 3D MINFLUX nanoscopy with DNA-PAINT to map EGFP-tagged Na,K-ATPase α1 and β1 subunits in mammalian cells with 3–5 nm localization precision. We introduce two point-cloud analysis tools: a data-driven algorithm that assigns localizations to the apical or basal membrane, removing trans-membrane artifacts, and a sequential nearest-neighbor analysis that estimates oligomer stoichiometry without structural priors. Both subunits show preferential nearest-neighbor distances of approximately 7 nm, direct evidence of dimerization, and are further organized into nanoclusters of approximately 7 to 12 molecules. These results provide direct structural evidence of Na,K-ATPase self-assembly and a framework for quantifying membrane-protein clustering at single-molecule resolution.
nb46f2ff9db3b: Resistance threatens to render antibiotics ineffective, which is posing a threat to global public health. Innovative strategies against drug-resistant bacteria are urgent. The outer membrane protein BamA, a hollow barrel with a pore of 2–4 nm, is a unique and essential structure in Gram-negative bacteria. We prepared chiral 3 nm gold nanoclusters (AuNCs) targeting BamA, exhibiting enantiomer-dependent antibacterial activity against drug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The AuNCs with right-handed wavelike lattices (D-AuNCs) preferentially interacted with BamA through the screw-in effect, creating pores in the cell wall and resulting in bacterial death. P. aeruginosa was still susceptible to D-AuNCs due to their excellent antibiofilm activity even after 20 successive passages. D-AuNCs were applied to P. aeruginosa-infected skin wounds in mice, achieving superior wound healing compared to levofloxacin. Our work documented that chiral nanoclusters targeting BamA can efficiently kill P. aeruginosa through the screw-in effect, providing an innovative strategy to combat Gram-negative bacteria.
nf79138ed7cc3: Hafnia-based ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) are promising for post-Moore memories, offering fast, low-power polarization switching and compatibility with the technological maturity of the hafnia platform. Yet nanometer-scale barrier thinning, while desirable for higher speed and energy efficiency, introduces a critical reliability bottleneck. Here, we develop an all-atomic layer deposition (ALD) process for reliable sub-2 nm hafnia FTJs through precise growth and low-roughness interface formation. The resulting devices combine sub-2-V operation with a high breakdown field of ∼12.1 MV/cm, while maintaining stable ferroelectric switching through 1010 cycles without breakdown. Further interface optimization extends the resistance-state endurance toward 1010 cycles, reconciling aggressive barrier scaling with reliable device operation. We further exploit 4-bit nonvolatile multilevel operation to demonstrate an in-memory computing simulation with 95.78% accuracy. By combining the advantages of scaling with high reliability, this work advances hafnia-based FTJs toward high-speed, energy-efficient, and robust memory applications.
n7f5f71f80ad5: Moiré superlattices provide a versatile route to engineering correlated electronic and topological states in van der Waals heterostructures, yet their use to organize structural polymorphism and phase-selective charge, magnetic, and superconducting states within a single two-dimensional material remains elusive. Here, we report modulated charge order and proximity superconductivity in an intrinsically moiré-patterned 1T/1T′ polymorphic network of monolayer VTe2 grown epitaxially on superconducting NbSe2. Scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy and first-principles calculations show that in situ annealing of twist-moiré VTe2/NbSe2 creates alternating 1T and 1T′ domains. The origin of the selective 1T-to-1T′ conversion is due to the moiré-induced anisotropic strain. This moiré-registered network hosts phase-specific short-range charge orders: 4 × 4 in 1T and 3 × 3 in 1T′. In the proximity-superconducting regime, spatially modulated in-gap bound states and suppressed coherence peaks reveal phase-dependent magnetic pair breaking. This work establishes intrinsically moiré-patterned polymorphism as a route to programmable two-dimensional quantum materials.
nc5565cf971f1: Metallenes have appealing properties, but stabilizing them in a monolayer phase poses synthesis challenges. A recent experiment showed that the van der Waals squeezing method can stabilize certain metallenes in a MoS2 sandwich. This pioneering work motivates systematic studies, but such studies are experimentally impractical, while first-principles modeling remains prohibitive. Here, using universal machine-learning interatomic potentials, we constructed 1620 metallene sandwich heterostructures containing 6 different sandwich layers and 45 metals. We performed phonon calculations, which revealed 1208 dynamically stable structures and narrowed them to 331 after structural filtering. We found that Se-based transition-metal dichalcogenides stabilize metallenes effectively. Specifically, hexagonal and buckled hexagonal crystal lattices exhibit the greatest stability. We further evaluated the thermal stability of selected heterostructures with density-functional-theory molecular dynamics simulations at room temperature. By uncovering the physical and chemical factors that govern metallenes stabilization, our results provide systematic insights to guide and accelerate synthesis for future applications.
n20a5388c4996: Dielectric nanoparticles and microparticles show rich optical responses due to their electric and magnetic multipolar Mie modes and low losses. These optical resonances can be modified via the particle size, shape, and dielectric environment. Here we tune the infrared multipolar Mie resonances of dielectric polystyrene microspheres using the plasmonic phase-change material In3SbTe2 (IST). IST exhibits a phase change between a dielectric amorphous phase and a crystalline phase that is metallic in the infrared. We show that a reversibly switchable particle-on-mirror geometry can be created by locally switching the IST under the polystyrene microspheres. Measuring the light-scattering spectra of single polystyrene microspheres before and after crystallization and reamorphization, we observe huge shifts of the resonance wavelength, e.g., from 5.2 to 8.9 μm and back for 6 μm diameter spheres. Our work is a first step toward a controlled tuning of multipolar Mie modes of various particles using reprogrammable IST mirror structures.
n4ac446f0c4d8: Recent transport experiments reported a quantum spin Hall insulator phase in monolayer 1T-TaIrTe4 gated away from charge neutrality. This phase is not predicted by band structure calculations and has been attributed to an electronic instability induced by strong correlations at a putative Van Hove singularity. Here, we investigate the electronic structure of exfoliated monolayer 1T-TaIrTe4 using microfocus laser angle resolved photoemission. We find a strongly anisotropic band structure susceptible to density wave instabilities. Our data further reveal a saddle point singularity in the density of states. However, we find that the saddle point lies at a density for which linear transport experiments found no anomalies. Moreover, the quasiparticle line widths suggest weak electron correlations only. This points to a secondary role of Van Hove singularities and electron correlations in the transport phase diagram of monolayer 1T-TaIrTe4.
nd0cc627381fb: Noble metal nanoparticles with sharp edges and corners, such as triangles, tetrahedrons, bipyramids, etc., support superior plasmonic field enhancement for enhanced spectroscopy. However, high-yield synthesis of gold right bipyramids (Au RBPs) with sharp tips has remained limited because they have a single-twinned (ST) crystal structure whose growth pathway is hard to control. Here, we report the seed-mediated growth of Au RBPs using ST seeds, achieving a yield exceeding 70% by moderately increasing the size of these seeds. Au RBPs with sizes from 34 to 94 nm and controlled corner sharpness are achieved through the regulation of seed and bromide amounts. Uniform and strong near-field enhancement is generated in the Au RBPs-on-mirror configuration, which outperforms the well-established nanocube-on-mirror configuration in Raman enhancement. This work highlights the merits of ST seed-mediated growth for anisotropic nanocrystals and their potentials in plasmonic near-field focusing.
nbc1c1e21b62d: 3D nanohelices provide a direct route to control light–matter interactions with circular polarization at the nanoscale. Here, we report periodic arrays of W–C nanohelices fabricated by He+ focused-ion-beam-induced deposition (FIBID), combining direct-write 3D growth with high spatial resolution and W-rich deposits (∼65 at. % W). Two arrays with the same lateral geometry were fabricated while varying only the vertical pitch, corresponding to helical ratios HR ≈ 1 and HR ≈ 2. Transmittance measurements under circularly polarized light reveal a clear geometry-dependent response. The compact nanohelices (HR ≈ 1) show a larger circular-polarization-dependent transmission contrast (g ≈ 0.17, θ ≈ 2.35°), moderate transmittance (∼30–50%), and a sign inversion near 600 nm. The larger-pitch helices (HR ≈ 2) show higher transmittance (∼35–100%) with a weaker but stable response (g ≈ 0.13, θ ≈ 1.60°). Qualitative simulations reproduce the main spectral trends and support distinct optical responses of the two pitch geometries.
ne268ce2eb88a: The performance of electrocatalytic reactions has rapidly advanced in recent years, yet there remain numerous controversies in the underlying mechanistic understanding of these systems. This Perspective proposes a framework for rating the strength of evidence and cross-community validation of mechanistic claims for the most-studied electrocatalytic reactions.
nd63a2498399a: Chiral helical superstructures provide a platform to control photon polarization and electron spin, yet they are challenging to construct using inorganic materials. Now, homochiral triple helices that exhibit pronounced circularly polarized luminescence have been assembled from gold by tailoring the steric and stereochemical properties of supporting chiral cyclic ligands.
n28ac8abb902d: Author Correction: Heat treatment in an oxygen-rich environment to suppress deep-level traps in Cu2ZnSnS4 solar cell with 11.51% certified efficiency
n5672bca96e89: Soft polymer coatings spontaneously rearrange on nanosphere surfaces to form directional bonds, unlocking an alternative route to delicate nanoparticle superlattices.
nf8033d4b8d5c: Direct biological conversion of CO2 into value-added chemicals is severely restricted by sluggish enzyme kinetics and inefficient intracellular carbon flux. Here, we address these catalytic bottlenecks by synergizing multimodal deep learning, mechanistic enzyme engineering, and synthetic organelle assembly. Using CASKP, a TransKP-guided candidate-prioritization framework that integrates sequence representations with a docking-derived scalar feature, we prioritized and experimentally identified a highly active β-carbonic anhydrase, PbCA, for improving intracellular CO2 supply. Structural analysis and molecular dynamics simulations guided the design of the R71A and V112A variants. The R71A–V112A variant displayed a specific activity of 26.1 U/mg and increased the intracellular 13C-labeled 3-phosphoglycerate ratio 4.9-fold. The simulations were consistent with a more hydrated active-site environment and a strengthened Tyr108-centered hydrogen-bond network. To overcome diffusion and thermodynamic limitations, these optimized biocatalysts were encapsulated into hybrid carboxysomes and coupled with an ATP-generating carboxykinase. 13C tracing confirmed incorporation of inorganic carbon into l-malate, with 95.2% of malate detected as 13C-labeled isotopologues. Subsequent promoter optimization yielded an l-malate titer of 22.7 g/L. This multiscale approach provides an integrated strategy for heterotrophic CO2-incorporating biocatalysis.
n161b17c373f1: Diastereoselective sp3-rich heteroatom-based bowl-shaped polycyclic molecules are a key structural scaffold in various bioactive molecules. Due to the inherent steric congestion of these structures, achieving precise stereochemical control remains a significant challenge in contemporary synthetic chemistry. We herein disclose a practical iron-catalyzed assembly of an indole-derived tertiary amine-based pentacyclic molecule through an intermolecular, iminium-triggered dearomative inverse electron-demand formal aza-Diels–Alder (IEDFADA) reaction. Detailed computational and deuterium labelling experiments strongly suggest that the diastereoselective formation of this complex core involves a stepwise in situ generation of a short-lived, highly reactive azadiene. Moreover, the negative slope (ρ = –0.29) from the Hammett plot indicates the formation of a partial positive charge and that the electron-donating groups enhance the reaction rate. Notably, the concise tagging of drug molecules and downstream synthetic transformations with good yields and diastereoselectivity should highlight the potential applications of this methodology in drug discovery settings in medicinal chemistry.
nc1289907da8f: The discovery of doped spinel Co3O4 electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is hindered by the large catalyst design space and the high computational cost of density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Here, we establish a hierarchical interpretable machine learning (ML) framework that decouples electronic structure prediction from catalytic activity prediction. By starting with predicting the electronic descriptor (d-band center) from readily accessible structural descriptors and subsequently predicting adsorption energetics, the framework removes the need for expensive electronic structure DFT calculations during catalyst screening while preserving physical interpretability. A random forest model was trained on adsorption free energies of OH*, O*, and OOH* from 144 representative active sites and achieved a test mean absolute error of 0.21 eV. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis identified surface energy, active site undercoordination, and the d-band center as the dominant descriptors governing adsorption energetics. To avoid additional DFT calculations of the d-band center during screening, a second ML model predicted it directly from structural and elemental descriptors with a test mean absolute error of 0.23 eV. The resulting framework enabled rapid evaluation of OER overpotentials across 252 active sites, while subsequent targeted DFT calculations identified Al-, Ca-, Fe-, and Mn-doped Co3O4 as promising candidates. Targeted DFT calculations and electrochemical measurements further validated the improved OER activity of Al- and Fe-doped Co3O4. This work establishes an interpretable and computationally efficient strategy for connecting structural descriptors, electronic properties, adsorption energetics, and experimentally measurable catalytic activity, thereby accelerating the discovery of high-performance spinel oxide catalysts.
n0deddbc45b3b: SktA from the cyanobacterium Nostoc punctiforme NIES-2108 belongs to the versatile heme oxygenase-like domain-containing nonheme oxidase superfamily, whose natural function is to transform 5-bromotryptophan (5-Br-Trp) to 5-bromoskatole in an oxygen-dependent manner. As SktA is also capable of transforming tryptophan (Trp) to skatole, this enzyme represents a skatole synthase that operates under aerobic conditions. Here, the crystal structure of SktA and its complex with 5-Br-Trp and Trp are reported. The amino acids responsible for the substrate binding and the diiron cluster formation were revealed, and their roles in the catalytic reaction were examined via mutagenesis experiments. In addition, we found that SktA is capable of transforming 7-bromotryptophan and 5,7-dibromotryptophan to yield 7-bromoskatole and 5,7-dibromoskatole, respectively, and resolved the crystal structures of SktA in complex with these alternative substrates to elucidate the plasticity of the substrate-binding pocket. Finally, we show that combining SktA and regiospecific self-sufficient Trp halogenases in one-pot reaction systems efficiently transforms Trp to 5-bromo-7-iodo-skatole or 5-iodo-7-bromo-skatole. In summary, this study reveals the structural information, substrate scope, and potential applications in synthetic biology as a module to generate differentially halogenated skatoles of SktA.
n072860963a38: The selective hydrogenation of acetylene is a key reaction step for purification in ethylene production, as trace amounts of acetylene can poison downstream polymerization catalysts. Industrial acetylene hydrogenation is currently performed almost exclusively using palladium-based catalysts, motivating the search for more abundant alternatives. In this study, supported Fe-Ag catalysts with different Fe:Ag ratios were synthesized and evaluated for the selective hydrogenation of acetylene under industrially relevant front-end conditions. The catalysts were characterized by XRD, N2-physisorption, TPR, XPS, STEM-EDX, ICP-OES and XRF, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations on idealized local Fe-Ag surface motifs were used to investigate composition-dependent trends in adsorption energetics. Catalyst characterization revealed no evidence for the formation of an extended Fe-Ag alloy phase after air exposure. Instead, Fe- and Ag-rich domains were found to coexist in close nanoscale proximity providing a structural basis for considering possible local Fe-Ag interactions. Accordingly, the DFT calculations were performed on idealized local Fe-Ag surface motifs to investigate how the local chemical environment around adsorption sites affects the adsorption energetics of reaction intermediates. DFT calculations predict a gradual weakening of adsorption strength with increasing local Ag content, while the experimental catalyst series independently shows a decrease in ethane selectivity with increasing Ag loading. Under CO-containing front-end conditions, catalyst selectivity increased further due to competitive adsorption effects, while the influence of catalyst composition became less pronounced. The combined experimental and computational results indicate that changes in the local Fe-Ag environment influence adsorption energetics and may contribute to the composition-dependent catalytic behavior in acetylene hydrogenation. These findings provide design principles for the development of palladium-free hydrogenation catalysts based on earth-abundant metals.
n20e604698cd6: Perovskite quantum dot (PQD)-polymer composites are widely pursued for display devices due to their excellent film-forming capacity, low cost, and favorable process compatibility. However, interfacial incompatibility between PQDs and polymers from mismatched surface chemistry triggers PQD aggregation and severe photoluminescence quenching, hindering microdisplay applications. Herein, a dual-solvent screening strategy is demonstrated for I-184-initiated crosslinked PQD-PMMA photoresists to balance solubility and lead-ion coordination strength. Undesired lead-solvent intermediate formation and residual solvent accumulation are suppressed to homogenize PQD dispersion and preserve optical performance. The 20 μm green patterned film retains 93% of the initial photoluminescence quantum yield with no photoluminescence peak shift and a narrow full width at half-maximum of 16.6 nm. The PQD pattern presents sharp pixel edges, 7.10% critical dimension deviation, 97.1% replication rate, and intersection over union of 0.92. This solvent engineering enables the revitalization of conventional polymers and addresses bottlenecks in photolithographic patterning of PQD-polymer composites.
nc0dd645fc239: The memristive artificial synapse, which typically operates on the basis of various filamentary conductance-update mechanisms, has been extensively utilized to implement hardware neural networks for brain-inspired computing. However, the stochastic conductance-switching characteristics that arise from uncontrollable filamentary evolution within the two-terminal device have long hindered hardware neural networks from achieving training and recognition performance comparable to their software neural network. Here, we propose a flexible complementary memristive synapse that achieves highly linear conductance-update behavior while preserving a large dynamic range. This synapse consists of a homogeneous bilayer of two amorphous indium–gallium-tin oxide (a-IGTO) films deposited under different oxygen partial pressures: an oxygen-deficient, VO-rich layer formed without O2 supply and an oxygen-supplied, VO-poor layer formed with O2 supply, exhibiting incremental and decremental conductance-update behaviors, respectively. The distinct oxygen-vacancy-related states and filament-evolution characteristics of the two layers suggest vacancy-mediated layer-to-layer redistribution, which can mutually compensate the nonideal conductive filament evolution of the two different layers, thereby facilitating more gradual modulation of the net conductance. The proposed flexible synapse exhibits robust mechanical stability and durability after 12,000 bending–release cycles, as confirmed by electrical characterization while maintained in the bent state at a bending radius of 2 mm. Finally, the applicability of the proposed flexible synapses to HW-NNs is evaluated through a VGG-8-based CIFAR-10 image recognition simulation using experimentally measured synaptic characteristics for weight updates in the two fully connected layers.
n7b3c2d06833d: Vaccines have profoundly reduced the global burden of infectious diseases and are increasingly being explored for cancer immunotherapy. However, developing vaccine platforms capable of simultaneously achieving efficient antigen delivery, precise immune modulation, and durable protective immunity remains a major challenge. Bacteria-derived micro/nanoparticles (BPs) have recently emerged as promising vaccine platforms that integrate the structural advantages of nanomaterials with the intrinsic immunostimulatory properties of bacterial components. Their micro-to-nanoscale dimension, pathogen-mimicking architecture, and capacity for multivalent antigen presentation facilitate efficient lymphatic trafficking, antigen-presenting cell targeting, and coordinated activation of both innate and adaptive immunity. Moreover, the endogenous pathogen-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs) within BPs serve as built-in adjuvants, potentiating antigen cross-presentation, inducing trained immunity, and eliciting robust T-cell and B-cell responses. These unique structure–function relationships have accelerated the clinical translation of BP-based vaccines, with several candidates now in clinical trials or already commercialized. In this review, we discuss the fundamental mechanisms, engineering strategies, and clinical research progress of BPs in vaccine development, while critically emphasizing the current challenges in safety, mechanistic elucidation, and scalable manufacturing. We further outline future opportunities for harnessing BPs as precision-tailored platforms for next-generation immunization paradigms.
n9a93c97e05aa: Supramolecular host–guest complexation provides a powerful strategy for stabilizing organic radicals and organizing them into functional spin architectures. Here, we investigate the kinetic pathways for on-surface complexation of spin-1/2 azafullerene radicals (C59N•) within templated [10]cycloparaphenylene ([10]CPP) nanohoop monolayers on Au(111), revealing a strongly anisotropic energy landscape that governs radical migration and encapsulation. Migration of isolated C59N• along the [10]CPP rims proceeds via relatively low energy barriers (∼0.45 eV), leading to preferential confinement at the nanohoop periphery prior to azafullerene encapsulation. C59N• relocation to the global energy minimum at the [10]CPP center requires overcoming substantially higher barriers of at least ∼0.8 eV, with interfullerene interactions raising these barriers further.
