High C59N• mobility and relaxed lateral confinement at [10]CPP template edges also activate an alternative assembly pathway in which azafullerene intercalation induces in-plane exfoliation of [10]CPP lines from the 2D [10]CPP array, creating a reconstructed two-dimensional superlattice composed of alternating zigzag chains of azafullerenes and linear rows of encapsulated C59N•⊂[10]CPP complexes. This edge-driven reorganization gives rise to anisotropic lattices of encapsulated radicals with one-dimensional structural motifs. The control over the rich energy landscape of C59N•⊂[10]CPP complexation thus enables access not only to geometrically frustrated two-dimensional lattices but also to quasi-one-dimensional chain motifs of spin-1/2 carrying radicals within a single supramolecular platform.
n266b9d2107a5: Raman spectroscopy is used widely to probe phonon properties and layer thickness in two-dimensional MoS2. However, relative peak heights of the out-of-plane (A1g) and in-plane (E2g1) Raman modes can vary with layer numbers. The explanation for origin of this variation has remained elusive. In this work, we show through statistical analysis of hundreds of Raman spectra on hundreds of samples that the A1g/E2g1 peak height ratio is ∼1.4 for monolayer and <1.0 for bilayer MoS2. However, in tri- and four layered MoS2, the A1g/E2g1 ratio can be both above or below 1.0, and gradually rises with thickness – approaching a saturation value of ∼1.3. We find – based on measurements on different dielectrics and at multiple temperatures down to 8 K – that the peak height ratio is modulated by the A1g line width, which depends on both substrate-dependent electronic effects and thermally activated contributions associated with interlayer-related phonon scattering. In monolayer MoS2, the anomalous area ratio originates from suppression of the E2g1 peak area and depends on excitation energy, suggesting the influence of its distinct electronic structure. Our results show that the variation of the A1g/E2g1 peak height ratio arises from the coupling of line width and monolayer-specific Raman response.
n0752d666b37b: In redox-active materials, atoms dynamically change their oxidation states in response to excess charge and electronic transport, with the potential for novel technologies spanning electronics, catalysis, and energy storage and conversion. Despite the remarkable progress of modern artificial intelligence methods in accelerating atomistic simulations, capturing the quantum-mechanical nature of charge transport and dynamically varying oxidation states remains a fundamental challenge, limiting scientific and technological progress. In this work, we introduce a machine-learning-based molecular dynamics framework capable of explicitly tracking the oxidation state dynamics arising from small-polaron hopping (excess charges trapped on single lattice sites that diffuse upon thermal activation). Our model uses descriptors augmented with charge localization information at each time step and is trained on density functional theory data to capture signatures of polaronic diffusion. We apply our method to the rutile TiO2(110) surface, which is a prototypical reducible oxide. Our simulations reveal that charge-carrier diffusion is highly sensitive to the local surface environment: polarons preferentially localize near oxygen vacancies, whereas their interaction with hydroxyl groups is weaker. These results provide a microscopic interpretation of experimental observations, highlight strategies to tune charge-carrier mobility through surface engineering, and demonstrate the applicability of our approach to investigating charge transport in complex materials.
nbd0c5ea21560: Tumor immunometabolism plays an important role in tumor progression and immune cell activity and is therefore critical to the efficacy of cancer immunotherapy. Modulation of immunometabolism to boost cancer immunotherapy is mostly based on targeting tumor cell metabolism, which often fails to address the tumor-promoting functions maintained by stromal cells. In contrast, targeting a metabolic checkpoint shared by tumor cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) can potentially overcome this limitation but has been relatively underexplored. Herein, a locally delivered, ultrasound activatable nanocatalytic platform is reported for immunometabolic cancer therapy. The platform is composed of sulfasalazine and a gallium-modified Fe-TCPP metal–organic framework nanozyme codelivered in an oxidized sodium alginate-based hydrogel. Ultrasound-activated gallium-modified Fe-TCPP boosts electron transfer, peroxide activation, and reactive oxygen species production while disrupting iron balance. Simultaneously, sulfasalazine inhibits SLC7A11-mediated cystine uptake in CAFs and tumor cells, reducing matrix remodeling and weakening the tumor’s antioxidant defense. This dual approach increases oxidative stress, reshapes the tumor microenvironment, induces immunogenic tumor cell death with ferroptotic traits, matures dendritic cells, and strengthens CD8+ T-cell responses. Consequently, it suppresses tumor growth in an immunocompetent osteosarcoma model and remains effective in a patient-derived OSCC xenograft model. Together, these findings demonstrate that targeting shared SLC7A11-mediated cystine dependence integrates stromal remodeling, tumor redox disruption, and antitumor immune activation.
n170f1adfadfd: Electrocatalytic hydrodechlorination (ECHD) provides a sustainable method for treating water polluted with chlorinated organic compounds under ambient conditions. Cobalt phthalocyanine (CoPc) represents a molecular catalyst with economic benefits and high selectivity, although its performance is limited by significant molecular stacking. To this end, we constructed ordered CoPc nanotubes (CoTs) for ECHD studies, alongside conventional CoPc single molecules and disordered aggregates as reference systems. All materials catalyzed ECHD via a direct electron transfer (DET) route on the CoPc active state under turnover conditions. The ordered CoT architecture accelerated interfacial and internal electron transfer, boosting the intrinsic activity. Degradation involves simultaneous reduction of terminal nitro and chloro groups, and the latter is suggested to follow an energetically favorable remote attack pathway. At full chloramphenicol (CAP) conversion, CoTs delivered an ECHD ratio of 83.9%, which is superior to recent benchmarks. For practical use, a flow-cell system achieved a treatment flux of 6.79 L h–1 g–1, which is 5 times that of a standard H-cell. This work underscores the pivotal role of molecular ordering in enhancing ECHD and offers design guidelines for non-noble metal heterogeneous electrocatalysts.
nbdc20bf04cd7: Cardiovascular implants (e.g., vascular stents, occluders) face persistent challenges of thrombosis, immune activation, and delayed endothelial healing. Moreover, functional surfaces that can synergistically balance the demands of antithrombosis and pro-endothelialization remain suboptimal. Here, we develop a genetically engineered, recombinant humanized collagen V (rhCol V) that promotes vascular endothelial cell proliferation via the αvβ3-FAK pathway and induces smooth muscle contractile transition. Proteomics indicates reduced platelet adhesion via αIIbβ3 inhibition, thereby reducing thrombogenicity. In rabbit models, rhCol V-coated stents outperformed drug-eluting stents in long-term endothelial repair and remodeling, while suppressing acute thrombosis and immune activation. This engineered biomaterial has the potential to enhance the safety and efficacy of cardiovascular implantable devices.
ndafa9bbdeaac: Long-range ordered cellulose nanocrystal (CNC) architectures are vital for photonic applications, but conventional self-assembly predominantly yields defective, multidomain nanostructures. Herein, this study proposes a slit-confined self-assembly (SCSA) strategy to construct a scalable CNC cholesteric liquid crystal structure with a single orientational domain. Distinct from conventional methods relying on extreme external fields or drying protocols, SCSA utilizes a simple glass slit to steer CNC assembly through synergistic physical effects: gravity drives tactoids sedimentation and interfacial hydrogen bonding enforces preferential alignment. Concurrently, the geometric constraint effectively suppresses the nucleation and propagation of topological defects, enabling the formation of centimeter-scale monodomain cholesteric architectures. As a result, brilliant structural color in aqueous CNC suspensions is achieved without external fields or active stimuli, enabled solely by the synergistic effects of geometric confinement, gravity-driven sedimentation, and interfacial hydrogen-bond anchoring. The resulting highly ordered architecture achieves an exceptional orientation factor of 0.98 and a structural color dissymmetry factor (g) as high as 1.3, accompanied by reversible structural reassembly behavior. Furthermore, upon coassembling with luminescent guests, the system exhibits a giant circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) dissymmetry factor (glum) reaching −1.1. Collectively, this work establishes a robust, straightforward, and scalable route for highly controllable liquid crystal self-assembly, offering promising avenues toward high-performance photonic applications.
n70bb9fd49d0b: Nanoparticles have been developed as delivery vehicles to achieve uniform distribution of drugs in the tumor, but they are still not optimal for deep tumor penetration due to the hindrance by the dense extracellular matrix. Enabling active transport via tumor cells has been explored as a solution, which has been achieved by tuning the size and surface chemistry of nanoparticles. Here, we show that particle stiffness is another key determinant. Using positively charged polyglycerol nanogels with matched size, charge, and composition, we found that stiff nanogels preferentially enter cells via clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME), undergo lysosomal processing, and are efficiently exocytosed, enabling transcellular transport. In contrast, soft nanogels are taken up mainly by macropinocytosis, accumulate in the Golgi apparatus, and exhibit prolonged intracellular retention. Finally, the efficient CME and subsequent exocytosis of stiff nanoparticles contribute to the enhanced transcytosis efficiency, allowing them to penetrate 3D tumor spheroids. This stiffness-dependent cellular itinerary operates without additional surface modifications, revealing a general design principle whereby intrinsic mechanical properties can control intracellular and intercellular transport behavior of nanoparticles.
n54dc5b27c055: Dynamic holography is pivotal for next-generation displays with critical applications in augmented reality, virtual reality, and beyond. While metasurfaces have emerged as powerful approaches for dynamic holography, existing works remain largely confined to intensity-only modulation, restricting the available channels for display and information storage. Herein, we realize a generalized platform applicable to major types of dynamic holography (monochromatic, color, 3D, and vectorial) by introducing a learned metasurface and aperture synthesis framework (LMAS). This paradigm extends Fourier duality from the intrinsic static real-momentum mapping relationship into the dynamical regime and establishes a learned mapping between real-space aperture displacement and momentum-space holographic evolution via gradient optimization. Crucially, the aperture’s inherent field-agnostic nature provides a universal physical interface that unifies diverse optical degrees of freedom, allowing us to demonstrate four distinct types of dynamic meta-holography. The LMAS approach establishes metasurfaces as a generalized, compact, and scalable architecture for holographic evolution within a minimalist system configuration, offering broad potential in advanced displays, optical storage, and information multiplexing.
nea4417bc3a71: Porous carbon materials are critical hosts for chalcogen‐ and halogen‐based conversion‐type cathodes, as they govern the activity and durability of electrochemical reactions. Understanding how their microstructures regulate electrolyte‐electrode interactions remains challenging given multiple coupling factors and dynamic changes during electrochemical cycling. Herein, machine learning was first used to screen three pore structure parameter windows relevant to electrochemical features from a large experimental dataset (23 carbon hosts and 1055 specific‐capacity data points). Based on these screened windows, three representative carbon hosts, namely micropore‐rich carbon, balanced carbon, and meso/macropore‐rich carbon, were synthesized as model systems. We reveal that pore structure governs sulfur species evolution, thereby dictating the competition between polysulfide‐mediated reactions and solvent self‐decomposition. The resulting spatial‐compositional differences of the cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) were found to profoundly impact energy efficiency, reversibility, and rate performance. The balanced carbon cathode with optimized inorganic‐organic distribution delivers an initial capacity of 1249.4 mAh g−1 and retains a capacity of 784.8 mAh g−1 after 500 cycles. This work not only proposes a data‐driven strategy for identifying CEI‐relevant pore structure windows, but also provides mechanistic insight into how physical metrics of porous carbon modulate multi‐step complex reactions and ultimately influence electrochemical performance.
n3199a75e17b4: Renewable intermittency is widely regarded as a durability stressor in water electrolysis, yet its impact on competing degradation and recovery processes within the cell remains unclear. Here, we show that realistic intermittent operation redistributes catalyst recovery and membrane degradation in anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE). A Ni–Fe‐based AEMWE single‐cell was operated under high‐resolution, solar‐mimicking load profiles that reproduce day–night intermittency without external buffering. Electrochemical diagnostics reveal reversible changes in activation, Ohmic, and mass‐transport losses, indicating partial performance recovery during zero‐current intervals. In situ X‐ray absorption spectroscopy attributes this behavior to reversible oxidation‐state and coordination changes of Ni and Fe, associated with the reversible formation and relaxation of amorphous (oxy)hydroxide surface layers. In contrast, hydrogen crossover measurements reveal increased crossover under low‐current operation, while post‐mortem membrane analyses provide independent evidence of membrane deterioration, identifying a critical system‐level limitation. These results show that intermittency does not uniformly mitigate degradation but redistributes it across cell components, enabling catalyst self‐restoration while exacerbating membrane vulnerability. This work establishes intermittency as a double‐edged operational parameter and provides a framework for designing materials and operating strategies for durable, battery‐free AEM water electrolysis.
n07b5cfb1ef94: Extreme fast charging in lithium‐ion batteries is limited by their poor charge acceptance at high C‐rates. We use overpotential component analysis to decouple ohmic, kinetic and transport voltage losses during fast charging. The concentration gradients are identified as the primary culprit in poor charge acceptance, so we study carbonate electrolytes that utilize acetonitrile, a low viscosity, high dielectric liquid, as a co‐solvent to improve ion transport. Our results indicate acetonitrile co‐solvent successfully reduces fast charging concentration gradients and therefore improves charge acceptance at high C‐rates, particularly when used in combination with interface‐stabilizing additives. Molecular dynamics simulations show that ACN enhances Li+ transport through a combination of reduced bulk viscosity and increased solvation‐shell lability, with shorter solvent residence times and faster coordination exchange producing transport gains beyond those expected from viscosity reduction alone. Finally, we use three‐electrode cells to deconvolute overpotential at each electrode, and the specific LiNi0.8Mn0.1Co0.1O2 (NMC811) electrode architecture and loading used in our study is found to have much higher overpotentials than our graphite electrode. In particular, the significant differences in NMC811 concentration gradients between electrolytes with or without acetonitrile indicate that the design of electrode architecture is crucial for extreme fast charging applications.
n7177821e141c: Dual‐locked activatable theranostics have been emerging as a promising cancer therapy platform. However, most of the reported dual‐locked systems only restricted to enzyme‐responsive probes, new molecular tools with other biomarker‐responsiveness still remain challenging. Moreover, optical manipulation in the second near‐infrared (NIR‐II) window can potentially boost the theranostic efficacy, but having rarely been explored. In this study, we report a dual‐locked and gas tandem‐activatable NIR‐II nanoagent for colon cancer theranostics. Water‐dispersible nanoparticles containing a nitrated organic small molecule (CTBN) and an acid‐responsive NO donor (NONOate; CTBNN‐NPs) are fabricated, displaying negligible emission in visible‐NIR region. Upon uptake by colon cancer cells, CTBNN‐NPs can be tandemly activated by the overexpressed H2S and the in situ released NO, thus turning on NIR‐II emission extending to 1200 nm. Moreover, the activated CTBNN‐NPs also demonstrate augmented NIR absorption as well as robust photothermal and type‐I photodynamic performance, achieving NIR‐II fluorescence imaging‐guided efficient photo‐elimination of colon cancer together with NO gas therapy, while exhibiting limited efficacy in the tested cervical and breast cancer models. This work provides a new molecular design approach to dual‐locked and H2S‐NO tandem‐activatable nanoagents with gas‐responsive and NIR‐II active capabilities, highlighting the exciting potential for cancer theranostics.
nffd6b8c4e641: Fe single‐atom catalysts with Fe‐N4 configurations typically suffer from excessive adsorption of oxygenated intermediates, leading to intrinsic limitations in catalytic efficiency. Here, we propose a Bi‐mediated Fe‐adjacent Zn extraction strategy to create defects adjacent to Fe‐N4 moieties on ZIF‐8‐derived carbon support, thereby tailoring the local microenvironment of Fe single atoms. The resulting Fe‐N‐pCd catalyst exhibits outstanding oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity in alkaline electrolyte, delivering a half‐wave potential of 0.918 V versus RHE along with excellent durability. The assembled quasi‐solid‐state Zn‐air battery using Fe‐N‐pCd as the air cathode catalyst affords stable operation for over 3000 h at −40°C. Mechanistic investigations demonstrate that the formed carbon defects adjacent to Fe‐N4 sites redistribute the local electron density and favor the formation of an axial *OH‐bound Fe state under ORR conditions. This defect‐modulated coordination environment lowers the Fe d‐band center and alleviates the overly strong Fe‐*OH coupling, thereby changing the potential‐limiting step from *OH removal to *OOH formation and accelerating ORR kinetics. This study provides a neighboring‐template extraction route for engineering defect microenvironments adjacent to metal single atoms, opening new opportunities for the design of efficient ORR electrocatalysts.
n0cc39a9fccb5: Human intestinal organoids (hIOs) are powerful models for studying development and disease, yet dissecting how physical and matrix cues shape epithelial and mesenchymal responses remains challenging due to reliance on ill‐defined matrices. Here, a fully defined hIO workflow was developed in which Matrigel was replaced by recombinant human substrates during pluripotent stem cell differentiation and by polyethylene glycol (PEG) hydrogels during 3D culture, while maintaining organoid viability and epithelial cytodifferentiation. Transcriptomic analyses show that both PEG‐ and Matrigel‐cultured hIO epithelial cells are most similar to human duodenal reference populations, and have greater transcriptional similarity to fetal than adult duodenal references. Despite this overall similarity, PEG culture is associated with subtle shifts in epithelial differentiation‐associated gene expression, together with altered mesenchymal ECM‐remodelling and integrin‐associated programs. Increasing matrix stiffness produces modest effects in epithelial cells, including increased MUC2‐positive cells, whereas mesenchymal transcriptional responses to stiffness are limited. Together, these findings establish a fully defined hIO platform that retains responsiveness to inflammatory stimulation while enabling controlled investigation of how matrix composition and stiffness shape epithelial and mesenchymal cell states in models of intestinal development and fibrosis.
n91c78ed0a8c3: Preventing thermal runaway propagation (TRP) is critical for the safety of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs). While hydrogel interlayers actively cool through water evaporation, their mechanical reinforcement with conventional fillers dilutes the water-rich matrix and reduces enthalpy. Here, we propose a paradigm-shifting strategy by using boric acid (BA) as a thermochemically active cross-linker in a poly(AMPS) hydrogel. BA reconstructs the hydrogel network through dual N─H⋯O hydrogen bonding and B⋯O═C coordination, simultaneously enhancing compressive strength by 567%. Upon thermal runaway, the composite provides dual-mode protection: (1) synergistic heat absorption (volumetric enthalpy > 2000 J cm− 3) via water evaporation and BA stepwise dehydration, accompanied by flame-inhibiting SO2 release. (2) In situ formation of a highly insulating ceramic–carbon hybrid barrier. Post-test analysis reveals a critical BA content of 25 wt%, where tetrahedral boron coordination (63.3% BO4) maximizes covalent B─O─C bonds that chemically “weld” B2O3 to carbon. This trend in BO4 fraction with BA loading quantitatively explains the exceptional TRP suppression, reducing the adjacent cell's peak temperature by over 500°C. Beyond a high-performance material, this work establishes a general design principle: employing reactive fillers that orchestrate both multi-stage energy management and tailored barrier synthesis, paving the way for next-generation battery safety materials.
na48e0ee50aab: Cryopreservation supports cell therapy, transfusion medicine, and tissue banking, but cryoprotectant selection remains constrained by empirical screening, toxicity, and ice recrystallization. We used pretrained language models as SMILES sequence encoders to prioritize small‐molecule cryoprotectants for experimental testing. Hierarchical representations were coupled to descriptor reconstruction, gated fusion, and downstream prediction of normalized mean grain size and thresholded labels. Splat‐cooling measurements assessed candidate ice recrystallization inhibition, followed by compatibility and cryopreservation experiments in red blood cells, human umbilical cord‐derived mesenchymal stem cells and rat abdominal aortas. Selected additives improved recovery or preservation endpoints within the tested formulations. This representation‐based screening workflow connects molecular property prediction with experimental cryobiology across ice, cellular, and tissue endpoints.
nfbd5d6017ae4: Articular cartilage defects remain a major clinical challenge due to the tissue's limited self‐repair capacity. Although numerous biomaterial‐based strategies have been explored, achieving a stable and functional cartilage interface remains difficult. A critical barrier is the poor integration between grafts and native cartilage, leading to fibrocartilage formation, delamination, and repair failure. Current approaches show limited success due to inadequate wet adhesion, mechanical mismatch, and insufficient chemical bonding. Here, we report a dynamically adaptive wet‐adhesive hydrogel composed of oxidized hyaluronic acid, quaternized chitosan, and silk fibroin (OHA/QCS/SF) for enhanced cartilage interface healing. The precursor exhibited rapid underwater spreading on hydrated substrates and displaced interfacial fluid in a fluid‐covered assay. Fluorescence imaging further revealed wetting and infiltration into the PAAm hydrogel. Dynamic Schiff‐base bonding between aldehyde groups in the hydrogel and amine‐containing components at the cartilage interface further promoted wet adhesion, while the reversible network enabled self‐healing under mechanical disturbance. In a rabbit cartilage defect model, the hydrogel loaded with synovial membrane‐derived mesenchymal stem cells (SMSCs) improved defect filling, host–graft integration, and cartilage‐like regeneration. This study provides a dynamic wet‐adhesive hydrogel strategy for improving biomaterial–cartilage interface healing in fluid‐rich joint environments.
n3ce4b84ca867: Homogeneous lithium‐aluminosilicate‐glass scintillators offer transparency, scalable fabrication, and compositional flexibility, but their neutron response is limited by defect trapping and activator loading concentration. Here, fluoride‐mediated host‐activator engineering is introduced to overcome these coupled limitations in Ce3+‐activated lithium aluminosilicate glasses. F− preferentially coordinates with Li+ and Mg2+, preserving the primary Si/Al─O tetrahedral units while reorganizing inter‐tetrahedral linkages. The resulting host‐network reconfiguration suppresses electronic disorder and defect‐mediated trapping, modulates medium‐range Ce‐centered correlations, broadens the viable Ce‐concentration window, and enables efficient excitation capture at ∼9 wt% CeO2 (twice that of GS20). After 6Li enrichment, it delivers 8003 photons neutron−1, an energy resolution of 6.8%, a decay time of 85.06 ns, and a neutron peak‐to‐trough ratio of 77:1. To the best of our knowledge, these values represent the highest light yield and best energy resolution reported for a homogeneous transparent 6Li‐enriched glass scintillator, achieving single‐digit neutron energy resolution for the first time and approaching the performance of 3He proportional counters and high‐performance crystalline scintillators. A transparent plate exceeding 2 inches further enables proof‐of‐concept two‐dimensional thermal‐neutron imaging with a system‐level spatial resolution of 1.35 mm, demonstrating the scalability of the glass for position‐sensitive neutron imaging.
ne4d6e1ed8f29: Metasurface‐enabled terahertz imaging and spectroscopy are moving toward compact, high‐throughput systems, but current approaches remain limited by discrete spectral sampling, computational reconstruction, and the trade‐off between spatial resolution and resonance quality in nonlocal designs. Here, we introduce a fundamentally different paradigm based on photonic crystal heterojunction‐enabled pixelated metasurfaces that directly encode spatial information into spectrally resolved, high‐quality‐factor resonances. By embedding bound‐state‐in‐the‐continuum metapixels within a bandgap‐engineered heterostructure, we simultaneously suppress lateral leakage and control vertical radiation, enabling effective three‐dimensional photon confinement in finite metasurfaces. This mechanism overcomes the conventional dependence of resonance quality on pixel size, yielding enhanced quality factors and figure of merit without increasing the device footprint, and enabling metapixels with lateral dimensions of ∼2λ that retain high spectral fidelity and signal‐to‐noise ratio. Leveraging this capability, we realize a 3 × 3 pixelated metasurface supporting nine independently addressable resonances, all retrieved in a single‐shot broadband terahertz measurement. The resulting spectral‐spatial encoding strategy establishes a direct one‐to‐one mapping between resonance signatures and spatial pixels, enabling hyperspectral imaging with a single‐pixel detector and a THz pulse, without raster scanning or algorithmic inversion. These results provide a scalable route toward real‐time terahertz imaging and integrated photonic sensing.
n51809c39ee9f: A key limitation of current artificial visual systems lies in their single‐channel signal transduction, which fundamentally departs from the parallel processing architecture of the biological retinas enabled by rod and cone cells. To bridge this gap, we developed a retinomorphic vision device by ion‐electron coupling transport based on carbon nanotube (CNT)/zinc oxide (ZnO) heterostructured nanotubes. Upon optical stimuli, this device generates two distinct ionic and electronic current signals, effectively mimicking the parallel phototransduction pathways in biological vision. This dual‐channel property enables efficient machine vision perception, achieving luminance adaptation and color discrimination accuracies of 96.5% and 98.2%, respectively. Furthermore, traffic‐light‐guided closed‐loop navigation of a mobile vehicle in a real scene has verified its application potential in embodied intelligence. This “single device enabled, distinguishable dual‐channel readouts” principle opens a new avenue toward artificial vision systems.
n5a8cc94a62e8: Next‐generation flexible optoelectronics and soft robotics require adaptive luminescent materials that withstand extreme environments while remaining deformable. However, the photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of current solvent‐free ionic liquids suffers from fundamental limitations arising from aggregation‐caused quenching and rapid nonradiative decay, and these liquids degrade under thermal and chemical stress. This study presents a supramolecular locking strategy that overcomes these limitations through kinetically stabilized anion–π+ interactions. Specifically, a rigid N‐doped fluorene (10H‐pyrido[1,2‐a]‐5‐indolium, PIn+) was paired with selected anions to maintain fluidity and suppress nonradiative molecular motion by locking radiative pathways in the liquid state. This ionic tethering approach yielded an unprecedented PLQY of 80% in the liquid state while preserving the solvent‐free liquid nature of the material. These highly emissive ionic liquids exhibited extreme physicochemical robustness, withstanding thermal decomposition up to 400°C, retaining intense emission without volatilization even under reduced pressure at 250°C, and resisting strongly acidic and basic environments. Derived from a versatile and readily synthesizable fluorene platform, this system also provides broad opportunities for structural customization. These findings establish a general molecular design principle for highly robust and emissive liquid fluorophores, providing a foundation for indestructible and flexible photonic technologies operating under extreme conditions.
n147e5217e9d2: The advancement of flexible sensing technologies is of paramount importance in biomedical engineering. However, achieving high‐fidelity multi‐modal temperature‐humidity sensing without inter‐channel cross‐talk and computational post‐processing remains a formidable challenge due to overlapping transduction mechanisms. In this study, an unprecedented electron‐ion synergistic functional material, featuring a unique inherent self‐decoupling capability, was developed based on the Janus hierarchical heterostructure. Through interfacial chemical engineering of Pd single‐atom anchoring and heterogeneous‐nucleation‐driven vertical growth of BiOCl on hollow MXene, the constructed material architecture successfully establishes fundamentally segregated electronic and ionic stimulus‐response pathways. Specifically, humidity fluctuations trigger ultra‐fast quasi‐2D proton conduction facilitated by localized potential wells and electronic redistribution generated around atomically dispersed Pd sites, while temperature gradients induce entropy‐driven carrier diffusion within the conductive MXene network. By suppressing signal cross‐talk through rigorous mechanistic orthogonality, the fabricated sensing array exhibits outstanding response characteristics (37.5/50 ms for humidity response/recovery and 25/62.5 ms for high/low‐temperature response), alongside superior oxidation resistance and robust functional durability (enduring 5000 cycles of testing). Ultimately, leveraging this multi‐modal sensing platform and machine learning algorithm, the integrated closed‐loop therapeutic system enables accurate evaluation of wound healing progression as well as on‐demand drug release, pioneering a new paradigm for next‐generation flexible electronics and adaptive healthcare modalities.
n71d921a6d95a: The crystal structure of a material profoundly influences its physical, optical, and electronic properties. However, precise control over polymorph formation of non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) in bulk heterojunction active layers remains challenging for optimizing organic solar cell (OSC) performance. Here, we employ a non‐halogenated mixed‐solvent system comprising carbon disulfide (CS2) and o‐xylene (OXY) to selectively regulate the crystallization of the high‐performance acceptor BTP‐eC9. A specific polymorph (Form II) is preferentially induced and consistently identified in powder, neat‐film, and bulk heterojunction samples by correlating wide‐angle x‐ray scattering (WAXS) and grazing‐incidence wide‐angle x‐ray scattering (GIWAXS) patterns with simulations derived from the corresponding single‐crystal structures. Compared with Form I, Form II exhibits improved optoelectronic properties, including extended exciton diffusion length, balanced charge mobility, and suppressed non‐radiative recombination. Consequently, Form II‐based devices achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.61% with a fill factor of 82.85%, representing a 27.0% relative improvement over Form I devices (PCE = 16.23%). Moreover, this method enables scalable manufacturing, with flexible OSCs (1 cm2 active area) fabricated by slot‐die coating achieving a PCE of 17.93%. This work establishes a practical pathway for solution‐processed polymorph control and reveals the relationship among single‐crystal packing, acceptor molecular packing, and device performance.
n615f22c9fdb4: Lithium-rich manganese-based oxide (LRMO) cathode materials deliver a reversible specific capacity exceeding 250 mAh g−1 through synergistic anionic and cationic redox, promising for next-generation high-energy-density batteries, yet their poor rate capability remains a critical barrier to practical deployment, particularly for fast-charging applications. This review deconstructs rate-limiting mechanisms at three levels, namely direct charge-transport impediments, kinetic sluggishness of anionic redox, and degradation cascade of phase transformations, voltage decay, and microcracking that exacerbates kinetics. A central insight is that the rate-determining step (RDS) shifts from electron-transfer to ion-diffusion dominance, governed by the exchange current density (j0 ) and the limiting current density (jd ). Modification strategies are classified into two threads, kinetic enhancement by shortening diffusion paths and lowering migration barriers, and structural stabilization by reinforcing bonds and suppressing oxygen release. Importantly, the often-overlooked charging kinetics are critically assessed, as the asymmetric nature of anionic redox imposes a more severe bottleneck for fast charging than for high-rate discharging. Methodological limitations in cross-study C-rate comparisons, arising from variations in electrode loading and testing protocols, are also examined to enable more rigorous evaluation of reported performance. This review ultimately provides a theoretical foundation for rational design of high-rate LRMO cathodes toward practical energy storage applications.
nb25d99f2463c: Conventional short‐wave infrared (SWIR) photodetectors confront cost disadvantages and fabrication complexity, whereas two‐dimensional (2D) van der Waals devices exhibit inherent performance limitations. Mixed‐dimensional organic/inorganic heterostructures offer a promising strategy for SWIR photodetection, synergizing strong optical absorption and tunability of organic semiconductors with high charge mobility and stability of inorganics. However, critical challenges remain in architecture design, including optimal carrier‐collection geometry, material selection, and interface engineering for boosting devices’ performance. Herein, a type‐II band‐aligned PTF/WSe2 mixed‐dimensional heterostructure is reported for high‐performance broadband SWIR photodetection via heterostructure synergy and rational Schottky barrier engineering. The Cr/p‐WSe2/PTF configuration (∼ 0.28 eV barrier) achieves superior performance, while Cr/n‐WSe2/PTF suffers from a higher barrier (∼ 1.18 eV). The optimized device achieves broad spectral photoresponsivity (∼ 103 A/W, 1060–1470 nm) and exceptional performance at 1310 nm: ultrahigh photoresponsivity (R = 2894 A/W), robust specific detectivity (D* = 1.0×1012 Jones), and excellent long‐term ambient stability. Versus standalone PTF, it delivers 17‐fold higher photoresponsivity and 96% lower bias voltage. High‐resolution SWIR image‐pattern reconstruction, together with concurrent performance improvements after six months of controlled storage, validates this PTF/WSe2 mixed‐dimensional heterostructure's potential for advancing next‐generation high‐performance SWIR detectors.
n9655b2a20c3c: Near‐infrared (NIR)‐responsive polymer actuators doped with inorganic photothermal agents face trade‐offs between photothermal performance and mechanical properties due to limited compatibility. Besides, most systems remain confined to 808 nm operation, as extending to 980 nm is hindered by poor absorption. Inspired by skunk cabbage thermogenesis, we develop ultra‐fast, multicolor fluorescent NIR‐responsive actuators by integrating aggregation‐induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) with excellent compatibility and photothermal properties into Janus‐structured polyimides (PIs) at ultra‐low doping (0.25 wt%). The multi‐donor‐π structure of AIEgen achieves redshifted NIR absorption extending to 980 nm and enhanced photothermal abilities through boosted intramolecular donor–acceptor interactions and molecular motion‐facilitated nonradiative decay (MMFND). Mirroring the mitochondrial working mode, AIEgens are uniformly embedded within PIs without compromising structural integrity, preserving mechanical properties above 100 MPa. Under NIR illumination, PI actuators achieve deformation with a bending speed of 900°/s, which facilitates crawling, gripping, and rapid continuous bidirectional flipping. The combination of multiwavelength photoresponse and multicolor fluorescence endows materials with dynamic information encoding. Programmable motions are implemented under different wavelengths through sequential, penetrative, and heat‐transfer actuation. This work provides guidelines for smart materials requiring precise 980 nm actuation with maintained mechanical robustness.
n6797794d92c6: Soft electronics have driven emerging advancements, which are expected to have wide‐range and large‐scale applications in health management, electronic skins, soft robotics, and interactive human‐machine interfaces. However, existing strategies mainly focus on isolated components, and system‐level soft electronic devices combining sustainable fabrication, robust performance, and versatile integrated functions have rarely been explored. Herein, we develop a recyclable soft electronic system enabled with multifunctional poly thioctic acid (TA) elastomer and high‐performance elastic metallic conductors. The multifunctional TA elastomer exhibits an exceptional combination of stretchability (435% strain), fracture energy (5.5 kJ/m2), apparent adhesion energy on Cu (10.7 kJ/m2), and thermal conductivity (0.69 W/m·K). These properties enable robust mechanical and electronic interfacing with different electronic components for sustainable soft circuits, while also endowing the electronic systems with outstanding self‐healing and recycling capabilities. Furthermore, by integrating with printable and recyclable elastic conductors based on eutectic liquid metals, the sustainable soft electronic systems can fully restore circuit functionality after complete mechanical rupture with the selfhealing capability of the composite elastomer and the elastic conductor. The system can be reprocessed to achieve full functionality restoration. The materials strategy developed in this study renders a promising solution for the development of soft and sustainable electronic devices.
n50a2759e4ea9: Efficient and durable catalysts for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) are critical for hydrogen production but remain limited by reliance on scarce iridium (Ir). We present an ultralow-loading Ir catalyst (3 at%, <16 µgIr cm− 2) integrated within a hollandite MnO2 framework, which lowers the overpotential at 10 mA cm− 2 from 580 mV (undoped α-MnO2) to 303 mV and delivers an Ir mass activity an order of magnitude higher than commercial IrOx. Varying pH and potential, we combine ICP-MS dissolution measurements with x-ray absorption spectroscopy, electron energy loss spectroscopy, and 4D scanning transmission electron microscopy. Dissolution is modest, with at least 79% of the Ir and 76% of the Mn remaining after 6 h under applied potential, and Ir remains oxidized and associated with the hollandite framework. Mn, in contrast, undergoes pH- and potential-dependent reduction and local structural disorder. Notably, the strongest Mn reconstruction (pH 0, 1.65 V) coincides with moderate dissolution, whereas the greatest Ir and Mn loss (pH 0, 1.60 V) occurs where the residual material is less reconstructed. Net dissolution therefore does not report on local structural change, highlighting the need to evaluate dissolution, reconstruction, and oxidation state together when designing and assessing Ir-efficient mixed-metal oxide catalysts.
n81637c770399: High-value piezoelectric single-crystal debris remains an untapped resource for flexible electromechanical materials. Although relaxor-based ferroelectric single crystals offer exceptional piezoelectric properties, off-cuts inevitably generated during precision processing are typically discarded because their irregular geometries prevent direct device integration. Here, we report a recycling-to-device upcycling strategy that converts industrial Pb(Mg1/3Nb2/3)O3–PbTiO3 (PMN–PT) single-crystal debris into high-performance flexible 0–3 piezoelectric composites and energy harvesters through material–structure–mechanics co-design. A ball-milling-based particle refinement procedure converts the debris into dispersible particulate fillers, while dielectrophoresis (DEP)-assisted curing reorganizes randomly dispersed particles in a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) matrix into vertically connected quasi-1–3-like networks. The polymer matrix provides mechanical tunability, allowing flexibility and dynamic stress transfer to the aligned single-crystal network to be jointly optimized. The optimized composite achieves a d 33 of 118.5 pC N−1 while retaining mechanical flexibility, placing it among the highest-performing flexible 0–3 piezoelectric composites. Comparative experiments and finite-element simulations reveal that single-crystal-derived fillers exhibit stronger DEP-induced enhancement than polycrystalline counterparts owing to more coherent intraparticle electromechanical conversion. Integrated into flexible energy harvesters, the optimized composite delivers a peak areal power density of 284.2 µW cm− 2. This work establishes a scalable upcycling pathway for reutilizing high-value functional crystal waste in flexible self-powered electromechanical systems.
n294f32d4629e: Lipid membrane‐bound synthetic cells provide programmable, cell‐like compartments for on‐demand biomolecule production. n13aa0410aad5: Composite electrodes containing physical mixtures (“blends”) of multiple active materials have generated commercial interest for lithium battery applications due to the possibility of enhanced electrochemical performance, which are not fully characterised. Results of experiments using a specially adapted three-electrode setup show that the effective rates of the components vary considerably depending on the cell state of charge, with much higher effective rates being reached than the applied cell rate. The same setup allows the direction of lithium redistribution to be visualised when the system relaxes following a current pulse, and this directionality also varies with cell state of charge. Electrochemical investigations and Raman spectra reveal that blending reduces chemical sensitivity to ambient storage conditions and leads to reduced degradation by forming a protective LMFP layer around the more reactive NMC particles. Operando data shows that the blend components evolve largely as expected when taking into account their specific effective rates, in line with the materials retaining their individual electrochemical properties. This study highlights the importance of considering relative windows of electrochemical activity when selecting blend components and paves the way for future optimisation of electrode blends for high rate lithium-ion batteries.
n588d850fb5ac: Hollow particles are designed to keep their cavities open, but a cavity can also be consumed as a structural resource. n2c8a76c446ba: Controlling matter with nanoscale spatial selectivity is a key hurdle for plasmonic applications such as nanophotonics, sensing, and catalysis. Plasmon-assisted nanolithography has recently emerged as a powerful strategy to address this challenge by exploiting the highly confined electromagnetic fields and hot carriers generated during plasmon excitation to confine organic or inorganic layers at the nanoscale. Among the surface chemistries compatible with this approach, aryl diazonium salts are particularly attractive because their reduction produces highly reactive aryl radicals that form robust covalent bonds with metallic surfaces under mild conditions. Under light excitation, the plasmon-induced reduction of aryl diazonium salts enables the rapid and site-selective grafting of functional organic layers confined to plasmonic hot spots. The resulting functional films provide versatile chemical handles for further modification. However, to date, the use of plasmon-mediated diazonium grafting as a spatially controlled primer layer to direct the site-selective immobilization of colloidal nanoparticles remains unexplored. We address this gap by using lithographic gold nanodisc arrays as optically programmable templates. Under plasmon excitation, these nanostructures enable the formation of positively charged nanoscale anchoring domains at plasmonic hot spots, derived from diazonium salts bearing amine groups. These localized charged domains can then guide the spatial organization of negatively charged colloidal gold nanoparticles. The geometrical parameters of the plasmonic arrays, including nanodisc diameter and interparticle spacing, were carefully tuned to access different plasmon excitation regimes around the 633 nm laser wavelength, enabling blue-shifted, near-resonant, and red-shifted conditions, and expanding the variety of achievable hybrid patterns. Complementary characterization using SEM, UV−vis spectroscopy, and FDTD simulations demonstrates that this approach provides a straightforward and versatile strategy to direct the assembly of colloidal nanoparticles on lithographic nanostructures via optical excitation.
