n3e692bd3627d: Catalytic conversion of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste into biodegradable plastic monomers, terephthalic acid (TPA) and glycolic acid (GA), has emerged as a compelling strategy toward sustainable plastic valorization. Conventional two-step...
n8efab071cfee: Oxidation governs the stability and functional conversion of two-dimensional semiconductors, yet its propagation through layered crystals remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the thickness-dependent oxidation of GaSe using optical spectroscopy, cross-sectional microscopy, and first-principles calculations. Experiments reveal concurrent top-down and edge-initiated oxidation, accompanied by Se redistribution and transient Ga2Se3 formation. Calculations identify Se vacancies as favorable sites for O2 adsorption and activation, which weaken neighboring Ga–Se bonds and promote oxygen incorporation. Molecular O2 faces a 4.03 eV barrier when penetrating a monolayer Ga2O3 model, compared with 0.54 eV along a GaSe van der Waals gap. This contrast supports interlayer diffusion as a plausible pathway for lateral oxidation, consistent with the pronounced thickness dependence and spatial anisotropy observed experimentally. Oxidation also yields a progression from p-type GaSe through ambipolar Ga2O3/GaSe heterostructures to n-type Ga2O3, whose devices retain stable characteristics after 300 °C air annealing.
nfecb34b17aec: Two-dimensional (2D) van der Waals (vdW) magnet-based heterostructures provide a vital platform for manipulating magnetic ground states and hosting complex spin textures. The topological Hall effect (THE) is a powerful tool for probing these textures in such systems. However, achieving a sizable THE in 2D vdW ferromagnets remains challenging due to the absence of broken inversion symmetry and sufficiently strong spin–orbit coupling (SOC). Here, we report an emergent giant topological Hall resistivity of 6.9 μΩ·cm at 10 K by interfacing the 2D ferromagnet Fe3GeTe2 (FGT) with the topological insulator BiSbTeSe2 (BSTS). Systematic temperature- and thickness-dependent studies suggest the origin of this pronounced signal to be the interfacial Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction (DMI). Furthermore, temperature-field mapping reveals the coexistence of two distinct phases that we identify as having opposite topological charge. Our results establish these vdW ferromagnet/topological insulator heterostructures as a robust platform for enhanced interfacial THE, opening new avenues for high-efficiency topological spintronics.
n70f75f0de887: Controlling doping density in correlated quantum materials offers a route to tuning their electronic states, but chemical doping can introduce disorder and limits dynamic control. Here, we demonstrate optically tunable electron doping of the layered Mott insulator α-RuCl3 through photoinduced interlayer charge transfer in MoS2/α-RuCl3 heterostructures. Photoluminescence and transient absorption measurements support electron transfer to α-RuCl3, leaving holes in MoS2. The layer-separated carrier population persists for more than 100 ps with an estimated doping density tunable through the excitation fluence. Selective excitation of α-RuCl3 further reveals hole transfer to MoS2. Transient absorption microscopy yields an early time effective hole diffusion coefficient of approximately 100 cm2 s–1 in the heterostructure, supporting a predominantly unbound carrier population. These results establish photoinduced charge transfer as a means of dynamically controlling carrier doping in α-RuCl3, providing a route toward optical manipulation of correlated electronic states.
n72d73a2d9bd9: Quasi-bound states in the continuum (quasi-BICs) offer a powerful platform for refractometric sensing by combining narrow resonances with strong electromagnetic confinement, promising high spectral resolution and large figures of merit (FOM). In practice, however, these advantages are often compromised by stringent angular alignment in passive transmission/reflection interrogation. Here, we demonstrate an active sensing platform that couples the defect-related photoluminescence (PL) of a freestanding silicon nitride nanomembrane to quasi-BIC modes. The substrate-free architecture suppresses radiation leakage and sustains tightly confined high-Q resonances, while emission-based readout bypasses stringent angular alignment. The resulting PL resonances exhibit line widths of 0.17 nm (Q ≈ 4000) in air and 0.26 nm in water. In aqueous sensing, the platform achieves a FOM of 250, substantially exceeding representative values reported for passive quasi-BIC sensors in the visible regime. This synergy translates the high-Q advantage of quasi-BICs into a practical active platform for high-performance refractometric and surface-binding sensing.
n13fe6e555fad: Lithium niobate (LiNbO3) crystals have been widely used in photonic and electronic devices owing to their outstanding intrinsic optoelectronic properties. However, fabricating hundreds-of-micrometer-thick LiNbO3 wafers remains dominated by diamond wire sawing, which causes substantial material loss. Although ultrafast laser processing offers a promising alternative, the intrinsic noncentrosymmetric lattice, spontaneous polarization, and anisotropic photothermal response of LiNbO3 severely hinder high-quality laser cutting. Here, a thermal dissipation-guided vector scanning technology is proposed to realize ultrafast laser slicing of LiNbO3 crystals for the first time. By tailoring the scanning direction according to the anisotropic thermal dissipation, we achieve crystal exfoliation with an ultrathin subsurface damage layer of 10 μm and an exceptionally high-quality separation surface. The results establish vector scanning technology as an innovative route for high-quality femtosecond laser processing and low-damage separation of anisotropic crystals.
naad0a4dfa2c3: Redox processes in oxides are central to materials synthesis and functionality, but their control is often hindered by surface instabilities. Using ambient-pressure X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, we show that a nominally 1 nm-thick SrTiO3 (STO) cap markedly enhances the surface stability of La0.05Sr0.95FeO2.5-δ (LSFO) thin films during H2 reduction by suppressing the formation of a secondary metallic Fe0 phase. Kinetic analysis indicates that the STO cap reduces the effective Fe0 formation rates by more than 6-fold at both 250 and 350 °C. These findings highlight ultrathin capping layers as an effective strategy for stabilizing oxide surfaces during redox.
nab3528a186d8: Ru single-atom catalysts are promising for NH3 oxidation but still suffer from poor activity and N2 selectivity, mainly owing to the poisoning of the isolated Ru active sites by the over-strong NH3 adsorption. Herein, we fabricated an asymmetric Ru-W atomic pair anchored on CeO2 (Ru1–W1/Ce) exhibiting considerable low-temperature activity (∼90% at 200 °C), high N2 selectivity (∼85% at 350 °C), and notable stability (∼500 h at 200 °C), surpassing most of the previously reported catalysts for NH3 oxidation. Systematic experimental and theoretical investigations demonstrated that a strong d-f orbital interaction between Ru and W atoms was revealed, inducing the smooth electron transfer from W to Ru atoms. The electron-rich Ru single atom not only weakened NH3 adsorption strength to alleviate NH3 poisoning but also reduced the energy barrier of the rate-determining step of NH3 activation. Besides, isolated W atoms coordinated with active Ru species, leading to a decrease in Ru–O–Ce coordination number. This could suppress the activation of O2 and thereby the deep oxidation of NH3. Accordingly, the reaction mechanism over this asymmetric Ru–W catalyst changed from the initial i-SCR to an imide-like pathway, accounting for its considerable catalytic performance. This work provided a paradigm for advanced Ru-based catalysts enabling both high activity and high N2 selectivity in NH3 oxidation.
n8d31f1b33dd3: A fundamental challenge in harnessing substrate promiscuity for industrial biocatalysis lies in reconciling broad substrate acceptance with high catalytic specificity. Although promiscuous enzymes provide attractive starting points for accessing non-natural transformations, their native active-site architectures and conformational dynamics often lack the precision required for efficient and selective conversion of desired unnatural substrates. Thus, systematically decoding and reprogramming the interplay between promiscuity and specificity remains a key obstacle toward versatile biocatalysts. Here, we address this challenge by integrating virtual screening, machine learning, and molecular dynamics simulations into a unified engineering framework. A tropinone reductase from Cochlearia officinalis (CoTR) was identified as a broadly promiscuous scaffold. By converting complex enzyme–substrate interaction dynamics into quantifiable and actionable design principles, we predict and validate key residues that govern substrate promiscuity. Guided by these insights, distinct CoTR variants were engineered for three representative substrates. The optimized variants—CoTR‑8M, CoTR‑5M‑1, and CoTR‑5M‑2—exhibited 7.0‑ to 16.3‑fold higher catalytic efficiencies than wild-type CoTR toward their respective target substrates and supported substrate loadings of up to 50 or 100 g L–1 while maintaining >99% ee. This work not only delivers scalable routes to three industrially valuable chiral alcohols but also provides mechanistic insights into the synergistic modulation of promiscuity and specificity. This study demonstrates a general strategy for translating intricate molecular-recognition features into rational design principles, thereby facilitating the development of tailored biocatalysts for non-native substrates.
nf27e7805d3f1: Tin–lead (Sn–Pb) perovskites are essential narrow-bandgap absorbers for two-terminal perovskite–perovskite tandem solar cells, yet their extreme air sensitivity has confined stability studies indoors, leaving real-world durability unexplored. Here, we substantially lower this barrier using industrially relevant, lamination-based encapsulation that enables, to our knowledge, the first outdoor demonstration of Sn–Pb devices. Combining polyisobutylene edge sealing with polyolefin elastomer encapsulation, we demonstrate that the lamination process is highly compatible with Sn–Pb devices, causing negligible performance loss while preserving optoelectronic quality during short-term air exposure. Under package-oriented accelerated aging, epoxy-based encapsulation fails rapidly, whereas the lamination-based package remains intact. Outdoors under tandem-relevant filtered illumination, lamination-encapsulated devices retain ∼80% of initial efficiency after 12 days, while epoxy-encapsulated devices lose all output within 6 days. By adapting manufacturable module packaging to Sn–Pb devices, this work enables their realistic field evaluation, marks a critical step toward deployable all-perovskite tandems, and strengthens confidence in their commercial viability.
nc0ed9774edbf: The lack of clear identification or understanding of the key perpetrators activating the tumor microenvironment (TME) impedes development of TME-modulating therapeutic strategies that could overcome the challenges associated with tumor growth, metastasis, and therapy resistance. Here, we report the development of a hybrid nanomaterial designed to genetically silence one key regulator, IGFBP2 (insulin-like growth factor binding protein 2), responsible for multicellular crosstalk within the TME. We demonstrated that silencing of IGFBP2 by this hybrid nanomaterial suppressed angiogenesis, stromal activation, and tumor cell phenotypes both in vitro and in vivo in preclinical models of ovarian cancer. Mechanistically, the hybrid nanomaterial utilizes the caveolae-mediated intracellular uptake pathway rather than a mixture of clathrin and caveolin as seen with a nonhybrid counterpart. Given the role of IGFBP2 as a prognostic factor for several cancers, and the absence of any small molecule inhibitor of IGFBP2, the current strategy may be exploited as a promising and generalized approach to target the TME and improve therapeutic outcomes in numerous cancers, including ovarian cancer
nee4603330991: Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) represent promising cell-free therapeutics for spinal cord injury (SCI). However, their therapeutic efficacy remains limited by variable cargo potency and insufficient cell-selective delivery. Here, we developed a modular biomimetic vesicle platform integrating hypoxic remodeling of mesenchymal stem cell-derived sEV (MSC-sEV) cargo with astrocyte membrane engineering. In a rat model of SCI, hypoxia-preconditioned MSC-sEVs (Hyp-sEVs) attenuated C3-positive astrocyte reactivity and improved functional outcomes. Proteomic profiling and functional analyses identified ERBIN as a key therapeutic cargo enriched in Hyp-sEVs that contributed to suppression of the NOD2/IRF3/GBP1 signaling axis. To enhance astrocyte-directed delivery, Hyp-sEVs were fused with astrocyte-derived membranes to generate astrocyte membrane-engineered vesicles (A-EVs). A-EVs were preferentially taken up by astrocytes, and blocking and knockdown experiments implicated MERTK and the ligands PROS1/GAS6 in this uptake. A-EVs outperformed Hyp-sEVs in preserving spinal cord tissue and promoting functional recovery. Together, these findings indicate that coupling hypoxia-remodeled sEV cargo with astrocyte membrane engineering promotes preferential vesicle uptake by astrocytes, attenuates C3-positive astrocyte reactivity, and improves functional recovery after SCI in rats.
ncb5a7cf80538: As conventional complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology approaches its fundamental scaling limits in binary logic, alternative device concepts have attracted increasing attention. Negative differential resistance (NDR) devices offer a promising route toward multivalued logic. However, their practical implementation requires both a high peak-to-valley current ratio (PVCR) and high drive current density at room temperature, necessitating complex device architectures and fabrication processes. Here, we report a heterojunction-free WSe2 NDR device on a hexagonal boron nitride dielectric, exhibiting a PVCR of up to 42.9 and a width-normalized peak current density of approximately 280.8 μA/μm at room temperature. The NDR emerges evidently after gate-polarity reversal, thus suggesting the formation of a bias-history-dependent nonequilibrium carrier configuration. Systematic variations of the gate-bias magnitude, duration, hold time, and sweep rate indicate that the relaxation of this nonequilibrium carrier configuration governs the peak current, peak voltage, and PVCR of the NDR characteristics. Surface passivation using poly(methyl methacrylate) further enhances both the PVCR and peak current, highlighting the sensitivity of the NDR to the surface electrostatic environment. These findings establish a bias-history-driven electrostatic mechanism for NDR in homogeneous two-dimensional layered semiconductors and provide a simple and scalable strategy for realizing high-performance heterojunction-free NDR devices.
n50c95ed372a2: Bloodstream infections (BSIs) are life-threatening systemic syndromes with a high mortality rate, characterized by a highly sequential pathophysiological progression. Although early antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory treatments have improved short-term survival rates, single-stage interventions are insufficient to reverse the high risk of long-term mortality among survivors. To address the urgent clinical need for stage-specific interventions to improve patient outcomes, nanomaterials have emerged as a highly promising platform due to their design flexibility and intelligent microenvironmental responsiveness. This Review first outlines the pathophysiological characteristics of BSIs at each stage, from the initial pathogen invasion to the final multiple-organ dysfunction, which serves as the basis for the design of nanomaterials. Then, following the progression of BSIs, the representative nanotherapeutic strategies developed in recent years for different pathological stages are systematically categorized and discussed. Finally, the review discusses the challenges confronting nanomaterials in BSI management, such as the selection of optimal treatment timing and clinical translation, and provides future perspectives on design strategies and developmental directions for nanomaterials in BSI treatment.
nd4f78996163a: The continued scaling of silicon-based dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) slows down due to increased process complexity and reduced storage capacitance. Oxide semiconductors (OS), represented by InGaZnOx (IGZO), offer an attractive alternative owing to their ultralow leakage and low thermal budget, making them promising candidates for next-generation DRAM as well as monolithic three-dimensional (M3D) architectures. However, realizing IGZO devices with well-balanced overall performance, including high performance and high reliability under ultrascaled dimensions, remains challenging. Here, we report ultrascaled IGZO field-effect transistors (FETs) fabricated using an optimized O2 plasma-enhanced atomic-layer deposition (PE-ALD) process. The IGZO FETs deliver state-of-the-art performance, including an on-state current (Ion) of 785 μA/μm at a drain voltage of 0.5 V and a transconductance (gm) of 620 μS/μm at a drain voltage of 1.0 V alongside a contact resistance (Rc) of 164.5 Ω·μm with positive threshold voltage (Vth). Reliability degradation is effectively suppressed, with bias-temperature instability (BTI) down to 8 mV even at extremely scaled contact length (Lc) of 50 nm. Leveraging these optimized devices, we further demonstrated a scaled two-transistor-zero-capacitor (2T0C) DRAM capable of up to 6-bit per cell, long data retention over 4000 s, and write time down to 10 ns. We proposed an M3D-DRAM architecture with vertically stacked multilayer embedded memory for artificial intelligence (AI) accelerators, achieving 77× faster weight loading and 9.6× lower energy consumption compared with mature high-bandwidth memory (HBM) counterpart, while maintaining graphics processing units (GPU)-equivalent inference accuracy of 92.25%. This work demonstrates an effective approach for the co-optimization of performance and reliability in ultrascaled IGZO FETs, providing critical foundation for next-generation DRAM and M3D applications.
n2d216eedd750: This study demonstrates proximity-induced ferroelectric switching in a stacked ferroelectric film composed of fluorite-structured HfZrO2 (HZO) and wurtzite-structured AlN, which are grown by thermal atomic layer deposition (ALD) and plasma-enhanced ALD (PEALD), respectively. The stacked film shows remanent polarization close to that of HZO but with a much higher coercive field, desirable for enhancing the memory window of ferroelectric thin-film transistors (FeTFTs) for storage applications. The FeTFT with a 5 nm-thick amorphous In–Ga–Zn–O (a-IGZO) channel layer, also grown by ALD, shows a memory window of ∼6.1 V, and data retention over 10 years. It also shows stable endurance cycles of ∼104. These enhancements over the single-layer HZO or stacked HZO/Al2O3 films, which show a minimal memory window of ∼0.3 V and ∼−0.3 V, respectively, are ascribed to the proximity ferroelectric effects between the soft ferroelectric HZO and hard ferroelectric AlN. These results, together with the conformal deposition of the HZO/AlN stack in high-aspect-ratio structures, demonstrate the feasibility of extending the ALD/PEALD-based Prox-FE materials platform toward three-dimensional (3D) process integration.
n41f0bb639e16: High‐capacity optical multiplexing is crucial for next‐generation intelligent information systems, spanning high‐speed communications, optical computing, and immersive displays. A fundamental challenge is to maximize the number of independent channels while maintaining high fidelity, compact footprint, and low structural complexity, constraints that severely limit existing diffractive optical elements. Here, we overcome these long‐standing trade‐offs by introducing a multi‐dimensional reconfigurable diffractive neural network (MRDNN) that enables high‐capacity, high‐fidelity optical multiplexing within an exceptionally compact and simple architecture through the co‐design of predictive neural optimization and multi‐physical‐dimension multiplexing. Experimentally, a dual‐layer MRDNN realizes 24 independent channels for distinct functionalities, including focusing, beam steering, and holographic image reconstruction. Owing to its excellent scalability, only four metasurface layers comprising a minimal library of 2002 meta‐atoms achieve 120 distinct optical channels with low crosstalk and high fidelity (measured mean structural similarity index measure of over 0.8), representing a record experimental multiplexing capacity with one of the smallest normalized footprints and simplest structural configurations in a metasurface‐enabled system. This work establishes a scalable and efficient paradigm for extreme optical multiplexing in multifunctional and reconfigurable photonics systems.
n6f4008eead9e: Electrocatalytic ammonia oxidation reaction (AOR) offers a green route to nitrite (NO2 −) synthesis while coupling hydrogen evolution reaction. However, maintaining NO2 − selectivity at high current density remains challenging due to the narrow thermodynamic windows for NO2 − and nitrate (NO3 −) formation and competition of oxygen evolution reaction at high anodic potentials. Herein, we report a Cu2S/NiOOH heterojunction that sustains high NO2 − selectivity over a wide oxidative window at industrially relevant current densities. Operando Raman spectroscopy, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations reveal that the heterointerface induces interfacial electronic redistribution within the Ni–O framework, strengthens NH3 adsorption, and rebalances AOR energetics, favoring NO2 − release over oxidation. Consequently, in a membrane electrode assembly-based flow cell, Cu2S/NiOOH delivers a Faradaic efficiency for NO2 − (FE(NO2 −)) exceeding 90% at 800 mA cm− 2 with a high production rate of 383.2 mg cm−2 h−1. These results highlight the potential of Cu2S/NiOOH for NO2 − electrosynthesis at industrial production rate.
nc257691975f8: Physical reservoir computing (PRC) has emerged as a highly energy‐efficient paradigm for processing high‐dimensional spatiotemporal data in edge‐intelligent systems. However, the deployment of PRC is often limited by the quantization mismatch between continuous input signals and the finite dynamic range of hardware substrates. Conventional binary time‐multiplexing ensures high noise immunity but necessitates protracted pulse sequences that induce high latency and premature physical saturation. Conversely, multi‐valued analog encoding enhances information density but frequently induces state overlap, operating devoid of physical quantization boundaries. To resolve this physical‐information trade‐off, we propose a saturation‐constrained information capacity (SCIC) framework. This framework considers task‐specific encoding variables and substrate‐intrinsic constraints, enabling device‐informed optimization of input mapping. We experimentally demonstrate this framework on a highly uniform, selector‐free 32 × 32 crossbar array, utilizing the volatile dynamics of memristors. Under the experimentally selected encoding conditions, the SCIC‐guided RC achieves exceptional performance in temporal prediction (NRMSE of 0.019), speech recognition (free‐spoken digit dataset (FSDD) subset accuracy of ∼94.5%), and real‐time obstacle avoidance. Our approach links encoding constraints to solid‐state device physics, providing a device‐informed method for PRC parameterization at the edge.
n9ed377baf34e: Achieving effective and economical hemostats requires a robust clot‐wound interface constructed by spatiotemporally coordinated coagulation. However, accumulated interfacial blood causes delayed clotting in adhesion‐reliant dense hemostats, and rapid but off‐site coagulation in absorptive porous materials. Here, we present MAGIC (Micromesh‐At‐Grid Integrated Cotton) gauze, which leverages a reversible transition between dense and porous states to precisely coordinate the spatial and temporal dynamics of coagulation. This transition is achieved by a pressure‐responsive micromesh composed of supramolecular procoagulant microparticles. Spatially, blood‐derived ions trigger the gelation of these procoagulant particles on the gauze surface, laterally repelling interfacial blood to ensure on‐site coagulation. Temporally, applied pressure induces micromesh dissociation to re‐expose the gauze macropores for wicking residual fluid, followed by the rapid co‐assembly of sol‐state procoagulant particles with blood components. This tightly synchronized process seals the cleared wound with a robust clot. Consequently, a single MAGIC pad arrested lethal porcine femoral artery hemorrhage within 30 s. Compared to standard gauze, it reduced blood loss by 98%, cotton consumption by 96%, treatment costs by 83%, and lifecycle CO2 emissions by 84%. Collectively, MAGIC gauze delivers exceptional preclinical first aid efficacy while pioneering a viable pathway for the decarbonization of surgical consumables.
n26215435948b: Ultrasound (US)‐triggered sonodynamic therapy (SDT) combined with immunotherapy shows considerable promise, yet its therapeutic efficacy remains constrained by insufficient intratumoral drug activation and limited immunogenicity. Herein, we report a self‐amplifying US‐responsive nanoplatform (PMB@R848) for synergistic sonodynamic immunotherapy. The nanotherapeutic was constructed by conjugating the sonosensitizer methylene blue (MB) to polylysine through US‐labile urea‐based linkages, providing a stable framework for efficient complexation of immunostimulant R848. Under physiological conditions, PMB@R848 exhibited excellent colloidal stability and biocompatibility. Upon US irradiation, the generated reactive oxygen species (ROS) initiated selective cleavage of urea bonds, exposing protonatable amino groups that enhanced intraparticle electrostatic repulsion under mildly acidic tumor microenvironment. This cascade process further accelerated nanoparticle destabilization and established a self‐amplified release behavior, enabling synchronized liberation of both MB and R848. The released MB markedly enhanced ROS generation, inducing robust immunogenic cell death and tumor antigen release, while R848 further amplified dendritic cell maturation and systemic antitumor immunity. Benefiting from the synergistic integration of self‐amplified SDT and immune activation, PMB@R848 achieved potent inhibition of primary tumors, effectively suppressed recurrence, and established durable immune memory in multiple murine tumor models. This work presents a self‐amplifying, US‐activatable nanoplatform for precision sonodynamic immunotherapy.
n15ffdb3f683f: The explosive advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has driven vast amounts of unstructured data that directly emerges at sensory interaction interfaces. Memristors with superior computing ability are among the most promising computing blocks. However, conventional vertical Metal/Resistive layer/Metal (V‐MRM) memristors tend to generate intense electric fields, suffer from limited sensory response, inflexible, and rigid functional modes, as well as long‐standing variability and overshoot issues. Here, we present an unconventional two‐terminal quasi‐vertical (QV) van der Waals heterostructure (vdWH) memristor as opto‐reconfigurable hardware. Unlike the V‐MRM memristor with a strong, rigid vertical electric field, this QV‐vdWH memristor realizes a significantly softened, tunable electric field, enabling parametric configurable and wavelength‐dependent reconfigurable modes across nonvolatile/volatile memory, neurons, synapses, and optical perception. Moreover, the light‐memristive switching‐vdWH coupling triggers a super‐additive synergistic enhancement of memristive performance (> 100‐fold) and photoresponse (> 3000‐fold). Meanwhile, the long‐standing variability and overshoot issues are overcome, yielding ultra‐uniform memristive behavior with even a single‐valued distribution. Leveraging the opto‐reconfigurability, high‐accuracy object tracking, and human motion recognition (∼96.8%) are successfully performed. Breaking through the inherent functional limitation of the conventional V‐MRM memristive structure, the QV‐vdWH memristor provides a flexible, opto‐reconfigurable hardware platform for emerging computing paradigms, and AI applications.
ne5f1e113778e: Diamondoid Cu3SbSe4 is an earth‐abundant thermoelectric material with strong potential for near‐room to mid‐temperature applications. However, its performance has been limited by intrinsically low carrier mobility. Here, we report the first successful growth of large‐sized Cu3SbSe4 crystals, achieving a fivefold enhancement in carrier mobility, and demonstrate the first Cu3SbSe4‐based thermoelectric cooling device. We show that Ag substitution reduces both the effective mass and deformation potential through strengthened bond covalency, yielding a high carrier mobility of ∼150 cm2 V−1 s−1. This leads to a remarkable power factor of ∼23 µW cm−1 K−2 at 300 K, a maximum ZT of ∼1.6 at 700 K and an average ZT of ∼0.85 over 300–700 K, representing state‐of‐the‐art performance among Cu‐based thermoelectric materials in this temperature range. A 7‐pair device based on Cu3SbSe4 crystal achieves a cooling temperature difference of ∼25 K at room temperature, and reaching a maximum of ∼34 K at 343 K. Additionally, the optimized sample demonstrates a single‐leg power‐generation efficiency of ∼7% at ΔT = 350 K. These results highlight crystal‐growth as a powerful strategy to unlock high‐performance refrigeration in previously limited materials, establishing diamondoid Cu3SbSe4 crystals as a viable, low‐cost and environmentally benign platform for practical thermoelectric applications.
nfdbdab68904a: Periodontitis, the sixth most prevalent global disease, causes tooth loss and systemic disorders, imposing a significant global burden. Functional regeneration of the periodontium remains a major challenge due to the hierarchical soft‐hard tissue interface and complex spatiotemporal functional demands. An anti‐delamination interface is engineered via polymer chain topological entanglement and dynamic boronate ester and ionic networks, while precise complex viscosity matching enables synchronized microscale laminar co‐extrusion. Concurrently, the hydrogel maintains wet adhesion, especially to moist root and bone surfaces. Spatiotemporal biofunctionalization is achieved by loading microRNA‐26a liposomes in the PCAC layer to activate Wnt/β‐catenin signaling for osteogenesis, and covalently tethering a PDGF‐BB mimetic peptide within the PCMC layer to trigger PI3K/Akt‐LOX signaling for fibroblast recruitment and functional collagen formation. In vivo, the Bio‐Fun bilayer hydrogel achieves integrated regeneration of alveolar bone and aligned periodontal ligament fibers, forming Sharpey's fiber‐like structures with firm bone‐ligament attachment. Meanwhile, the modular and injectable design might provide broad reference for the reconstruction of periodontal, osteochondral, and other soft‐hard tissue interfaces.
n4cd242b40c4c: Wound infections represent a major clinical concern due to their high incidence and subtle early manifestations, often resulting in prolonged healing and increased risk of complications. While wearable bioelectronics facilitate real‐time diagnostics and therapeutic interventions, their widespread clinical translation remains constrained by the complexity, power demands, and high cost of current systems. Here, a wearable platform that integrates colorimetric sensors with a wireless optoelectronic microneedle patch was presented for in situ wound infection status detection and on‐demand photodynamic therapy (PDT). This wireless colorimetric optoelectronic microneedle (COMN) patch enables rapid (15 min) and reliable detection of typical wound infection biomarkers with minor interference. By integrating microneedles and wireless light‐emitting diodes (LEDs), this system supports concurrent delivery of photosensitizers and light into deeper wound tissues, achieving > 99.9% eradication of drug‐resistant bacteria through penetration‐enhanced PDT. In a murine full‐thickness wound infection model, this system promptly assessed the infection status of the wound and then triggered PDT, resulting in > 3 log reduction in bacterial burden and accelerated healing, with > 80% wound closure observed by day 14. This work demonstrates a flexible and adaptive bioelectronic platform based on colorimetric analysis and optoelectronic microneedle therapy, offering an accessible strategy for precision wound care.
nf1e7304c8b96: Solid‐state metal hydrides offer high volumetric hydrogen density and intrinsic safety for hydrogen storage, yet their practical application is severely hindered by poor room‐temperature thermodynamics, sluggish kinetics, impurity gas poisoning, difficult activation, and cycling degradation. Multi‐principal element alloys (MPEAs) have recently emerged as promising candidates to overcome these bottlenecks through their vast compositional space, severe lattice distortion, and synergistic cocktail effect. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in MPEAs for solid‐state hydrogen storage, bridging atomic‐scale design to system‐level performance. A unified composition‐process‐structure‐property framework is established that integrates engineering‐driven design rules, post‐processing techniques, multi‐scale computations, machine learning (ML), and high‐throughput experiments. Using advanced in situ and ex situ characterization, the atomic‐scale origins and cross‐scale evolution of surface poisoning, hydrogen‐induced amorphization (HIA), disproportionation, pulverization, and defect accumulation. A theoretical framework linking electronic structure to heat and mass transport is further developed, and hydrogen storage bed design, device integration, fuel‐cell coupling, manufacturing scalability, and cost analysis are discussed. Finally, key scientific and engineering challenges and future research directions are outlined. This review provides scientific guidance for designing MPEA‐based solid‐state hydrogen storage systems with high capacity, long cycle life, high poisoning tolerance, fast de‐/hydrogenation kinetics, and low cost.
n32750dd51e1c: Electrocatalytic reactions occur at a dynamic, ion‐regulated electrochemical interface, rather than at a static electrode boundary. In electrocatalytic processes such as hydrogen evolution/oxidation and CO2 reduction, which operate at potentials below the electrode's potential of zero charge, electrolyte cations are not mere spectators but active participants that shape reaction behavior. Their size, charge density, solvation structure, and spatial organization within the electric double layer (EDL) govern interfacial energetics, transition states, and reaction activity and selectivity, giving rise to pronounced, system‐dependent cation effects. Furthermore, cation accumulation dynamically modifies the interfacial electric field, reorganizes water structure, and alters local pH, thereby coupling electrostatics, solvation, and mass transport in a highly nonlinear manner. These intertwined effects complicate mechanistic interpretation and have contributed to ongoing debates and seemingly contradictory conclusions across experimental and theoretical studies. Here, we synthesize the current understanding of cation effects at electrochemical interfaces, highlight emerging interfacial molecular structures revealed by in situ and operando studies that challenge classical EDL models, identify key unresolved debates, and outline pathways toward a quantitative, molecular‐level description of cation–interface–reactivity relationships.
n04110bd9915f: Electrocatalytic seawater hydrogen evolution is fundamentally limited by the rigidity of interfacial water structures and static electron distributions at catalyst surfaces. Here, we report a bias‐responsive S‐scheme heterojunction that dynamically couples nonequilibrium electron redistribution with interfacial water activation during operation. Using a MoN/NiCoN model system, in situ x‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) reveals a cathodic‐bias‐induced reversal of interfacial electron transfer relative to the equilibrium state, leading to progressive electron enrichment at the catalytic interface. In situ infrared spectroscopy reveals potential‐dependent restructuring of the interfacial water environment associated with this electronic redistribution, transforming strongly and intermediately hydrogen‐bonded water into catalytically active free or weakly hydrogen‐bonded species. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations further reveal accelerated hydrogen‐bond exchange kinetics, shortened hydrogen‐bond lifetimes, and a more adaptive dipole orientation at the MoN/NiCoN interface, providing molecular‐level evidence for dynamic water‐network reorganization. Ionic‐liquid‐based experiments further demonstrate that this restructuring originates from electronically driven interfacial activation rather than bulk water availability. Consequently, water dissociation and hydrogen evolution kinetics are synergistically accelerated, enabling ultralow overpotentials in real seawater and high solar‐to‐hydrogen (STH) conversion efficiency. This work establishes dynamic S‐scheme heterojunctions as a general strategy for electronically programmable interfacial reaction environments in electrocatalysis.
nc4c24af78598: High‐temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells (HT‐PEMFCs) offer compelling advantages for energy conversion, including simplified water and thermal management and high tolerance to fuel impurities. In these systems, phosphoric acid (PA) serves as the primary proton conductor, enabling anhydrous proton transport. However, cathode performance and durability remain constrained by sluggish oxygen reduction kinetics and the challenge of controlling PA distribution and retention. Uneven acid distribution, manifesting as local flooding that blocks gas pathways and covers active sites or local depletion that disrupts proton‐conducting networks, causes severe mass‐transport losses and performance decay. Concurrently, gradual PA migration and loss during operation progressively degrade proton conduction pathways, accelerating voltage decay. Recent studies have established cathode binder engineering as an effective strategy to regulate both PA distribution and retention. This review systematically examines the design of cathode binder systems—encompassing polymer binder optimization and functional additive integration—and the characterization and diagnostic frameworks for evaluating their efficacy in PA management. We further integrate advanced PA characterization techniques with a comprehensive electrochemical performance evaluation framework. By establishing explicit connections among binder design, PA distribution and retention behavior, and device‐level performance assessment, this review provides an instructive guide for the rational development of high‐performance, durable HT‐PEMFC cathodes.
n190ad3cf54e0: Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn─I2) batteries are attractive for large‐scale energy storage yet remain limited by two coupled failure mechanisms: unstable zinc interface at the anode and polyiodide shuttling at the cathode. L‐Carnosine (LC) emerged as a unique candidate exhibiting both the highest dipole moment and a moderate LUMO energy across the screened library. Experimentally, LC's zwitterionic, multicenter charge distribution drives persistent multidentate adsorption at the zinc interface, suppressing HER, directing (101)‐oriented crystallographic deposition through facet‐selective passivation, and enabling formation of a vertically graded organic‐inorganic hybrid solid electrolyte interphase. Concurrently, the electron‐rich imidazole group rapidly quenches polyiodide intermediates through a rapid redox reaction. This synergistic regulation enables Zn||Zn symmetric cells to operate stably for 4980 h, Zn||Cu cells to achieve 99.76% average Coulombic efficiency (CE) over 1400 cycles, and Zn||I2 full cells to sustain over 18 000 cycles with nearly 100% capacity retention. Furthermore, the practical viability is demonstrated in Ah‐level pouch cells with 85% capacity retention after 500 cycles. This work establishes a unique molecular transformation strategy for stabilizing high‐energy aqueous energy systems.
n6cd95c8b5031: Protective materials for harsh environments should dissipate transient impact energy while maintaining mechanical reliability under thermal fluctuations. This structural–molecular coupling provides efficient impact protection, delivering a low energy transfer rate of 7.38% under high‐strain‐rate compression and reducing the residual impact force from 20°C to 100°C. The carbon‐nanotube‐containing framework further provides photothermal responsiveness, allowing reversible stifhefness modulation, adaptive force buffering, and shape recovery after localized high‐speed impacts. Together, these results establish a bioinspired twisted brick–mortar design strategy for adaptive thermo‐mechanical impact protection.

nc9d2b13c1bf1: A Pd-catalyzed atroposelective ring-opening coupling of cyclic tetracoordinate borons affords tetrasubstituted axially chiral alkenyl silanes while retaining the boron moiety. The reaction integrates boron and silicon within a configurationally stable chiral framework and exhibits broad functional-group tolerance. More broadly, this strategy expands the reactivity of tetracoordinate borons beyond conventional migration pathways and provides a distinct approach to tetrasubstituted axially chiral molecules.
nbdfc15a2b905: Complex, dynamically heterogeneous environments such as lipid membranes, electrocatalytic interfaces, soft polymer matrices, crowded biological media, and phase-separated assemblies are characterized by spatially distinct microenvironments, multiscale structural dynamics, and short-range interactions. Microscopic interactions are poorly captured by bulk descriptors. In this article, we review how ultrafast two-dimensional infrared (2D IR) spectroscopy and related vibrational methods provide direct access to these complex molecular landscapes by resolving inhomogeneous ensembles, picosecond environmental fluctuations, and exchange between local states. When combined with vibrational probes and modern molecular simulation, these spectroscopic observables reveal how local interactions, such as electrostatics, hydrogen bonding (H-bonding), and ion pairing and aggregation generate microscopic heterogeneity and govern multiscale dynamics. We organize discussions around representative classes of complex environments, including hydration and electrostatics in lipid membranes, molecular environments and dynamics in biomolecular condensates, confinement and crowding in self-assembled and interfacial systems, including electrochemical interfaces, polymers/gels and soft matter, electrolytes and ion-specific effects, and aqueous cosolvent mixtures relevant to solvation and cryopreservation. Looking ahead, ongoing advancements in vibrational probe design, multidimensional spectroscopy, and molecular simulation are expected to enable more quantitative and predictive analyses of heterogeneous molecular environments across chemistry, materials science, and biology.

n538e88554fe1: Two atomically precise sulfide-templated Cu14 nanoclusters (NCs), [S@Cu14(4MBT)12(PPh3)6] (S@Cu14-4MBT) and [S@Cu14(3MBT)12(PPh3)6] (S@Cu14-3MBT), were synthesized and structurally characterized to investigate the influence of ligand engineering on the stability and electrocatalytic performance of Cu NCs during the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR). ndcfcdee41585: Boron carbide (B4C) is a ceramic of considerable interest due to its high hardness, elevated melting point, excellent thermal stability, low density, and chemical inertness. ROMP of the cyclooctenyldecaborane monomer enabled controllable molecular weight and produced a series of polymers with molecular weights up to 35 kg/mol and dispersities (D̵) in the range of 1.3-1.6. Thermogravimetric analysis coupled with infrared spectroscopy and mass spectrometry (TGA-IR and TGA-MS, respectively) of PCD revealed the evolution of small hydrocarbon species following an initial release of hydrogen at low decomposition temperatures around 250 °C, which is in stark contrast to the decomposition profile of unfunctionalized poly(cyclooctadiene) (PCOD) that transitions into volatile hydrocarbon species at approximately 450 °C. MD simulations indicate that the release of H2 results in the exothermic formation of boron clusters, which promote the thermal decomposition of the hydrocarbon polymer backbone. These findings indicate that decaborane plays an active role in the polymer-to-ceramic conversion rather than serving solely as a boron source, providing mechanistic insight that will enable the rational design of next-generation PCPs with enhanced ceramic yields and tunable compositions.
na86b19af39ba: Vapor−liquid−solid (VLS) growth has delivered a level of synthetic control in group IV and III−V semiconductor nanowires that remains unmatched in any other class of one-dimensional materials. For Si, Ge, and GaAs, decades of mechanistic study have made diameter, growth direction, crystal phase, and axial composition into design parameters. For oxides, carbides, and chalcogenides, including emerging van der Waals materials, which we refer to collectively as non-conventional nanowires, one-dimensional structures have been reported in abundance, but comparable deterministic control has not been achieved despite their predicted functional properties and broad application potential. This review examines where and why the two groups diverge. We survey and categorize the literature on VLS and VLS-related synthesis of non-conventional nanowires, following the sequence of the growth process itself, namely, precursor creation and delivery, seed particle formation and evolution, and nucleation and growth of one-dimensional structures. Each step is compared against the group IV and III−V baseline to locate shared behavior and genuine differences. From this comparison, we identify seed particles, spanning the choice of seed material, the chemical composition of the seed during and after growth, and its dynamics, as the principal bottleneck restricting deterministic synthesis, with precursor creation and delivery acting as an upstream constraint that narrows the accessible seed design space. We discuss potential solutions, including new precursor chemistries, improved reactor designs, and in situ characterization of growth, that would deepen the mechanistic understanding of nanowires already demonstrated by VLS and extend seeded growth to emerging quantum and functional materials, ultimately paving the way for deterministic synthesis and integration of complex one-dimensional nanomaterials.

nf16a976f4b1f: Transforming plastic waste into valuable organosulfur chemicals, this work presents a solar-driven, continuous-flow photoelectrochemical platform. n28c1f913945c: Li-rich layered oxides access high capacity through transition-metal and oxygen redox, but oxygen loss and structural reconstruction cause large first-cycle irreversibility. Here, we examine Li1.2Ni0.13Co0.13Mn0.54O2 at four states of the first charge–discharge cycle using atomic-resolution STEM, nanobeam electron diffraction with electron pair distribution function (NBED-ePDF) analysis, electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS), image simulations, and DFT. Up to 4.3 V, Li extraction is dominated by interlayer sites and the slab framework remains largely preserved. At 4.8 V, changes in Li/O contrast and O K-edge features coincide with a short ePDF correlation near 1.57 Å. Seeded DFT relaxations stabilize short O–O pairs near vacancies in the transition-metal slab. After discharge, incomplete spectroscopic recovery accompanies near-surface reconstruction and oxygen-related contrast changes consistent with oxygen depletion. Together, the results implicate Li depletion from the transition-metal slab in high-voltage oxygen rearrangement and suggest that controlling this site occupancy may improve oxygen-redox reversibility.
na5d68d45a0e0: Spin-based multivalued logic offers compelling advantages for next-generation computing. Thus far, only binary systems─exploiting domain walls, skyrmions, and vortices─have been realized. Here, we demonstrate the implementation of ternary logic operations using a one-dimensional vortex chain, via the co-manipulation of both the chirality and polarity of magnetic vortices. We show that ternary AND logic functionality can be achieved via dipole-mediated chirality modulation and domain-wall-assisted polarity reversal in the vortex chain, with operation times on the nanosecond scale. Our work establishes a viable and scalable platform for multivalue magnetic logic, thereby paving the way for next-generation spintronic logic applications.
n22cbeb01c9c5: The modular assembly of protein nanoparticles has enabled the design of highly immunogenic and cross-protective viral vaccines. However, downstream translation is hampered by labor-intensive purification methods that lack the resolution needed to efficiently sort molecular assemblies. Here, we report an affinity tag-free nanoparticle sorting platform that exploits electro-viscoelastic microfluidic (EVM) migration for the high-fidelity, continuous-flow isolation of virus-like particle (VLP) assemblies. This migration mechanism can overcome Brownian fluctuations, which are typically dominant on the nanoscale, confining the target assemblies to central streamlines for selective collection. In a single pass, the system segregates 40 nm VLPs from 6 nm excess antigen monomers, increasing the VLP purity by 20.2%. A sacrificial electrode outlet directs undesired electrohydrodynamic effects to the waste, preserving the VLP-rich product stream. Our results offer an alternative downstream framework for the rapid purification and quality control of complex bionanomaterials, establishing a scalable pathway for precision nanomedicine processing.
n065c87963aaa: Breaking reciprocity in thermal radiation opens opportunities for energy harvesting, sensing, and thermal management. Traditional nonreciprocal radiative semiconductor devices need an external magnetic field. In this work, we predict a series of magnetic topological materials for magnetic-field-free nonreciprocal thermal radiation in the infrared regime by combining first-principles calculations with Maxwell electrodynamics. We find strong and broadband nonreciprocity in magnetic Weyl semimetals (e.g., Co3Sn2S2), outperforming conventional semiconductor InAs. Furthermore, we propose material design recipes. Strong nonreciprocity requires a large anomalous Hall response relative to the optical loss, whereas the broadband response favors a large optical loss and small dielectric dispersion. Our work establishes a predictive material discovery framework and quantitative design rules for next-generation magnet-free nonreciprocal thermal devices.
n26648c93b2ae: Fe(Te,Se) is a prototypical iron-based superconductor and a promising platform for exploring topological superconductivity. However, growing high-quality ultrathin Fe(Te,Se) films on magnetic substrates remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate epitaxial growth of monolayer-to-trilayer Fe(Te,Se) on the van der Waals itinerant ferromagnet Fe3GeTe2 (FGT) via direct selenization of the substrate, without external Fe or Te deposition. Combined scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS), low-energy electron diffraction (LEED), scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM), and energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) characterizations reveal large-area, atomically flat tetragonal films with well-defined rotational alignment to the hexagonal FGT lattice. Cross-sectional STEM-EDS confirms Se incorporation and interfacial elemental redistribution. Thickness-dependent spectroscopy reveals evolving electronic structures and progressive decoupling from the ferromagnetic substrate. Measurements across lateral monolayer–bilayer interfaces further uncover asymmetric band bending and charge redistribution driven by Fermi-level equilibration. These findings establish substrate-mediated selenization as a versatile route to ultrathin superconducting heterostructures and magnetic quantum platforms.
n56005a3d50fa: Emulating frequency-dependent synaptic plasticity requires artificial devices capable of integrating temporal inputs and adapting their responses. Here, we demonstrate electroelasticity-regulated vacancy diffusion in MoSe2 memristors as a physical mechanism for frequency-adaptive synaptic dynamics. An applied electric field induces lattice deformation that lowers the vacancy diffusion barrier, whereas poststimulus electroelastic relaxation progressively restores the barrier, creating a dynamically evolving diffusion landscape. This coupled electroelastic–ionic process gives rise to intrinsic second-order memristive dynamics and enables frequency- and history-dependent plasticity, including pair- and triplet-spike-timing-dependent plasticity and Bienenstock–Cooper–Munro-type learning with a sliding modification threshold. Leveraging these dynamics, memristor-based spiking neural networks realize adaptive neuromorphic functions spanning composite color–direction perception and autonomous drone control. These results establish electroelastic regulation of vacancy diffusion as a materials-level mechanism for translating temporal input statistics into adaptive synaptic responses, providing a pathway toward neuromorphic systems with frequency-adaptive perception and control.
nf134ce4e6292: Dielectric nanoparticles can be engineered to scatter light predominantly in the transverse direction, perpendicular to the incident plane wave’s propagation direction, a phenomenon known as the transverse Kerker effect. Although complete cancellation of forward scattering from a single object is forbidden by the optical theorem, we show that a single photonic mode can provide an ideal transverse Kerker effect. When combining several nanoparticles to form a metasurface, the mode evolves into an accidental bound state in the continuum. This enables polarization-independent quasi bound states in the continuum whose quality factors are tunable without symmetry breaking. We experimentally demonstrate our concept in the visible, achieving the first polarization-independent bound state in the continuum without Brillouin-zone folding. These modes maintain large quality factors over a broader region of momentum space than conventional bound states in the continuum. Our results establish a platform for realizing ultranarrow resonances free of conventional design constraints.
nf0fb92ae1f37: Alkali metals are promising materials for low-loss plasmonics, because of their intrinsically weak optical damping and favorable free-electron response. However, their high chemical reactivity and weak optical absorption make their ultrafast carrier dynamics difficult to access conventionally. Here, we investigate the long-lived carrier relaxation in potassium using a mode-engineered concave metasurface as a resonantly enhanced optical readout. A strongly confined hybrid mode with a high quality-factor-to-mode-volume ratio (Q/V) greatly enhances the sensitivity to pump-induced dielectric perturbations. Transient-reflectance spectroscopy resolves two characteristic relaxation times of ∼0.5 ps and ∼8 ps due to the electronic redistribution and electron–phonon-mediated energy relaxation, respectively. Two-temperature-model analysis yields a record-low electron–phonon coupling factor, consistent with weak electron-to-lattice energy transfer in potassium. These results demonstrate high-Q/V mode engineering as an effective strategy for accessing weak nonequilibrium carrier dynamics in low-loss plasmonic materials and for exploring light–matter interactions in minimally dissipative plasmonic environments.
n92b2564c8b39: Operating sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries (SSBs) at high voltages increases energy density but induces O2 release from cathode materials, degrading battery performance. To elucidate this early stage degradation, SSBs were fabricated using LiNi0.5Co0.2Mn0.3O2 (NCM523) particles with distinct grain-boundary (GB) densities: single-crystalline (SC) or polycrystalline (PC). Gas analysis of SSBs during charging up to 5.0 V (vs Li/Li+) reveals that the PC-cell produces 27 times more O2 than the SC-cell despite having identical total surface areas. STEM-EELS analysis reveals 2–5 nm thick rock-salt phase formation across particle surfaces and along GBs regardless of the crystallinity, indicating that O2 evolution in the PC-cell occurs mainly along GBs of NCM523 particles. Because surface coating on the PC substantially suppresses O2 evolution, oxygen-vacancy formation initiated at the particle surface propagates O2 release along the GBs. Consequently, suppressing surface oxygen-vacancy formation represents a critical strategy for improving the long-term stability of high-voltage SSBs.

na765e5d6c329: Polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) synthases share similar architectures, yet produce distinct PUFAs.
