These insights inform rational engineering.
n763a13f11dfa: Carboxylic acids are attractive precursors to boronic esters, but redox requirements of decarboxylation are poorly matched to diboron reagents. Juliá-Hernández and coworkers report an iron ligand-to-metal charge transfer strategy activating coordinated carboxylates through photoinduced electron transfer. Free acids, from acetic acid to drug molecules, give boronic esters in one step.
n5eec01b94f9e: Following Wender’s pioneering studies, the total synthesis of Euphorbia diterpenoids has undergone a remarkable renaissance over the past decade. This resurgence has been driven by the emergence of unified synthetic platforms, radical-based coupling strategies, and strategic cycloaddition reactions. These developments have not only enabled the concise and scalable synthesis of flagship molecules such as phorbol, prostratin, resiniferatoxin, and pedrolide, but also provided chemical probes for exploring their promising biological activities. This review summarizes the total syntheses of these four molecules, with a particular emphasis on the strategic innovations and emerging trends across the different synthetic routes developed for each, aiming to provide timely guidance for future synthetic efforts.
nb4b7f87fda11: The O-dealkylation of alkyl ethers—or the removal of small alkyl protecting groups (PGs)—remains a significant challenge in organic synthesis. While traditional chemical methods require harsh reaction conditions and lack sufficient selectivity, biocatalytic approaches represent valuable alternatives. However, enzymes facilitating the desired O-dealkylation reactions are scarce. In this work, we applied a sequence similarity network (SSN)-guided approach to identify cytochrome P450 monooxygenases (CYPs) with O-dealkylation activity within the growing sequence diversity found in public databases. We investigated six CYPs, three of which exhibited significant activity toward structurally diverse ethers bearing methyl, ethyl, propyl, or allyl groups. While P450ThcB and P450Terp enabled the deprotection of aromatic and aliphatic primary and secondary ethers, P450Sca2-mut complemented the substrate scope by effectively deprotecting sterically demanding tertiary ethers. In particular, P450ThcB and P450Terp exhibited high regioselectivity, preferentially cleaving phenolic over benzylic ethers. Furthermore, P450ThcB enabled the regioselective deprotection of veratryl alcohol. Preparative scale reactions of three substrates yielded up to 74% of the isolated and (regioselectively) cleaved alcohol product. Together, these findings substantially expand the enzymatic toolbox for the selective removal of alkyl PGs and highlight the suitability of SSN-guided database mining approaches for the identification of biocatalysts with the desired function.
n2918c82c5505: Precise control of catalytic active centers and their interfacial strain is central to accelerating heterogeneous reactions, yet systematic regulation of strain at subnanometer metal–oxide interfaces remains challenging. Here, we report a class of 3d metal/heavy rare-earth metal oxide oligoatomic catalysts, in which finite metal ensembles are anchored on oxide surfaces to form nuclearity-dependent, strain-coupled metal–oxide interfaces. By varying the metal species, oxide support, and, most critically, the average number of metal atoms in each ensemble, we show that interfacial strain can be systematically tuned across diverse 3d metal/oxide combinations. In the Ni/Y2O3 system, an optimal nuclearity range of approximately 4–6 Ni atoms maximizes both compressive Ni–Ni strain and tensile Y–O distortion, creating a strained Ni–O–Y interface that balances CH4 oxidation and CO2 reduction during dry reforming of CH4. The resulting catalyst sustains near-equilibrium CH4 and CO2 conversion for over 1200 h without coke accumulation or detectable active-site collapse and remains stable under natural-gas reforming conditions. Theory and in situ spectroscopy reveal that nuclearity-regulated interfacial strain redirects carbon-containing intermediates away from deep dehydrogenation and toward continuous oxidation, thereby establishing a dynamic carbon balance. These findings position oligoatomic catalysts within the structural regime situated between single-/dual-atom and nanoparticle catalysts and highlight ensemble nuclearity as a tunable parameter for modulating interfacial strain in demanding catalytic reactions.
nc3c7a5169471: The active site of the classical Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 (CZA) catalyst for CO2 hydrogenation remains elusive as its surface structures undergo dynamic change under reaction conditions. Here, we combine neural network interatomic potential molecular dynamics simulations and grand-canonical density functional theory calculations to investigate the evolution of the representative CuZn alloy and inverse ZnO/Cu surface phases, and we consistently observe drastic restructuring under hydrogenation conditions, forming fragmented Zn-based ensembles at Cu support. Among the pathways examined, CO2 hydrogenation on these ensembles preferentially proceeds through the HCOO pathway, with different ensemble compositions being thermodynamically favored for the intermediates formed at different reaction stages. Importantly, these Zn-based ensembles are highly dynamic on Cu, allowing the inert HCOO within the ensembles to access highly active Cu/Zn interfacial sites, thereby making its hydrogenation kinetically accessible. The formation of ensembles and their dynamic behavior may be related to a suitable Cu–Zn interaction, which stabilizes Zn on Cu while preserving its mobility. Overall, these findings identify dynamic Zn-based ensembles as potential operando active sites in the Cu–Zn component of CZA and show that catalyst restructuring not only changes surface morphology but also couples directly to the reaction mechanism.
nba9787d58afa: Cyclopropane fatty acid synthase (CFAS) enzymes catalyze the formation of cyclopropane rings within bacterial membrane lipids, a transformation implicated in membrane homeostasis, stress adaptation, and antimicrobial resistance. Despite decades of biochemical investigation, the molecular determinants governing CFAS regioselectivity, stereoselectivity, chain specificity, and substrate scope remain poorly understood. Here, we systematically investigate how enzyme orthology, lipid structure, and membrane environment shape CFAS selectivity. Comparative analysis of CFAS orthologues from Escherichia coli, Lactobacillus acidophilus, and Streptococcus thermophilus reveals that the extent of mono- versus di-cyclopropanation, regioselectivity, and stereochemical outcome are not conserved properties but diverge substantially across the enzyme family. A simple two-carbon variation in phospholipid acyl chain length (C16 versus C18) reverses the absolute configuration of the cyclopropane product, revealing an unrecognized structural determinant of stereochemical outcome. Furthermore, we demonstrate that CFAS catalysis extends beyond native phospholipids to synthetic pseudo-phospholipids bearing non-phosphate anionic headgroups and to fatty acids embedded within lipid vesicles, substantially expanding the substrate scope of this enzyme family. Together, these findings provide insight into the molecular basis of CFAS selectivity, advance the understanding of bacterial lipid cyclopropanation, and broaden the synthetic potential of these enzymes for the stereoselective preparation of non-natural cyclopropyl lipids.
na44d8c686724: Hybrid perovskites are emerging as promising piezoelectric materials, yet the use of high-quality single crystals in flexible ultrasound sensing remains largely unexplored. Here, we report intrinsically noncentrosymmetric chiral two-dimensional perovskite single crystals, (S/R-NEA)2PbBr4, that exhibit strong piezoelectricity arising from chirality-induced symmetry breaking and enhanced lattice polarizability. By integrating these crystals into a polymer matrix, we realize flexible piezoelectric nanogenerators delivering high output (∼8 V) under ultrasonic excitation. The devices enable reliable detection and clear resolution of 50 kHz ultrasound signals, along with excellent mechanical durability and environmental stability. This work establishes a single-crystal strategy for flexible piezoelectric devices and highlights chiral 2D perovskites as a compelling platform for high-sensitivity ultrasound detection and energy harvesting.
n484feb4ee38e: Bicarbonate electrolysis offers a direct route for converting captured CO2 into high-value chemicals without energy-intensive CO2 regeneration and compression. However, multiphase transport within liquid-fed porous cathodes remains poorly understood. We found carbon paper and carbon cloth yielded drastically different performance, and further analysis revealed gas retention, i.e., localized and temporary entrapment of internally generated gas within the pore network, as an important transport limitation. Flow pulse and recovery experiments under galvanostatic operations showed largely reversible performance losses, while operando X-ray imaging directly visualized gas retention. Gas retention intensifies with denser electrodes, lower catholyte flow rates, and higher current densities. Guided by these observations, an interdigitated flow field was employed to enhance through-plane convection and gas removal, increasing the maximum formate partial current density to 304 mA cm–2 and enabling 120 h of stable operation. These findings establish gas management as a critical design criterion for bicarbonate electrolyzers.
naa8c055efc37: The performance and lifetime of energy‐storage devices are determined at the interfaces between electrodes, electrolytes, and separators, where ion and charge transfer, parasitic reactions, and mechanical degradation originate within nanometers of the surface. Atomic layer deposition (ALD) and molecular layer deposition (MLD) enable precise engineering of these interfaces through self‐limiting surface reactions that produce conformal coatings with controlled thickness and composition, even on porous electrodes. Although ALD surface chemistry is well established on ideal oxide surfaces, energy‐storage materials present chemically and structurally complex surfaces, on which reaction mechanisms, growth per cycle, and coating function can differ. This Review develops a chemistry–process–structure–function framework that connects surface chemistry, precursor reaction pathways, and nucleation behavior with film structure, ionic transport, charge‐transfer kinetics, redox stability, and mechanical response. We examine growth on oxide, sulfide, metal, polymer, and carbon substrates and relate the films to their functions at cathodes, anodes, solid electrolytes, and separators in Li‐based and beyond‐Li batteries. We further assess process scalability in terms of precursor utilization, throughput, and energy consumption, and discuss in situ monitoring, post‐deposition characterization, and full‐cell test conditions needed to validate coating performance. These relationships are summarized as six design rules presented as a decision flow.
n90eece73f86a: The sluggish dynamic equilibration of ions in ionic liquid electrolytes, particularly under high viscosity conditions, originates from strong interionic interactions and inefficient utilization of charge carrier species. Here, we present a strategic electrolyte design that reconfigures the interionic interaction network and accelerates the dynamic equilibration of charge carriers in AlCl3/EMIC ionic liquid electrolyte. By incorporating an optimized moderator with low polarity and small molecular size, the dynamic redistribution and re-equilibration of charge carriers during cycling are significantly accelerated, while the continuous depletion of effective charge carriers is suppressed. Guided by this principle, the dichloroethane-enabled electrolyte exhibits rapid chloroaluminate equilibration and improved electrode-electrolyte stability. In situ Raman spectroscopy confirms that the moderator promotes reversible AlCl4 − /Al2Cl7 − conversion. As a result, the reorganized AlCl3/EMIC electrolyte suppresses dendrite growth and achieves unprecedented Al anode stability in symmetric cells. Matched with flake graphite cathodes, the full battery capacity increased by 120.7% from 92 to 203 mAh g−1 at 200 mA g−1 after 7000 cycles. This work establishes a dynamic speciation regulation principle for designing ionic liquid electrolytes with fast ion equilibration and provides a pathway toward long-life aluminum-ion batteries.
n3ac0471aeefc: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) is among the most promising techniques to provide hydrogen as both energy carrier and feedstock for the chemical industry, due to its compatibility with intermittent renewable electricity sources. However, a major bottleneck in scaling up PEMWE is the limited supply of the anode catalyst Ir. This work shows a novel approach to tailoring ionomer‐free catalyst layers based on custom‐made microporous substrates and two different atomic layer deposition (ALD) processes, both using Ir(EtCp)(CHD) precursor. Thermal ALD using O3${\rm O}_3$ as counter‐reactant yields mostly metallic Ir/IrOx${\rm IrO}_x$ and an electrode Ir loading of 0.21 mg·cm−2${\rm mg}\cdot{\rm cm}^{-2}$. The PEMWE cell‐level performance is comparable to a commercial catalyst‐coated membrane anode despite 7×$7\times$ lower loading, and is maintained over an accelerated durability test equivalent to 600 h of intermittent operation. Moreover, using a low‐loading ALD‐made cathode, the total platinum group metal loading is only 0.24 mg·cm−2${\rm mg}\cdot{\rm cm}^{-2}$. Plasma‐enhanced ALD reduces the Ir loading to 0.04 mg·cm−2${\rm mg}\cdot{\rm cm}^{-2}$ by tailoring the catalyst distribution, however, yields lower‐activity IrO2${\rm IrO}_2$. Finally, direct ALD catalyst deposition needs no ionomer‐bearing ink. The anodes are therefore compatible with various membrane materials, as demonstrated in a CO2${\rm CO}_2$ electrolysis experiment with an anion exchange membrane.
na1555fbe0b71: Aqueous proton batteries are promising alternatives to lithium‐ion batteries owing to their intrinsic safety, low cost, and fast proton transport. However, the small size, high charge density, and strong protonating ability of H+ often perturb host frameworks during repeated insertion/extraction, causing phase transformations, lattice strain, and rapid capacity decay. Herein, we synthesis we report a non‐stoichiometric tunnel‐structured molybdenum oxide, Mo5O14, as a highly reversible proton‐storage electrode. The interconnected tunnel framework enables direct and reversible H3O+ intercalation without phase transition, pronounced structural distortion, or significant volume variation, thereby ensuring excellent structural stability and rapid ion transport. As a result, Mo5O14 delivers a high capacity of 271 mAh g−1 at 1.5 A g−1 (∼5C) and retains 142.2 mAh g−1 even at 300 A g−1 (∼1000C) and sustains stable operation for over 310 000 cycles. When paired with a VHCF cathode, the full cell achieves 73.3 Wh kg−1 and maximum power density of 43.4 kW kg−1, and over 60 000 stable cycles. Furthermore, a flexible interdigital proton micro‐cell array demonstrates rapid‐charge capability, powering a red light‐emitting diode for over 5 min after only 10 s of high‐rate charging.
nd441043fe459: Battery safety remains a critical challenge in the large‐scale deployment of lithium‐ion batteries. While thermal runaway is typically attributed to exothermic reactions involving electrode materials and electrolytes, the contribution of current collectors has been largely overlooked. Here, we demonstrate that the conventionally presumed inert aluminum (Al) current collector engages in intense exothermic reactions with various cathode materials at temperatures exceeding 600°C. This reactivity is catalyzed by fluorides, which disrupt the Al passivation layer, resembling combustion mechanisms observed in Al‐based rocket propellants. The specific heat release from Al oxidation (−22 to −33 kJ g−1) is nearly twice that of the electrolyte (−12 to −16 kJ g−1). Considering that the Al mass is approximately half that of the electrolyte, its theoretical thermal contribution during thermal runaway is comparable to that of the electrolyte. Employing fluorine‐free electrolytes can suppress the propellant‐like reaction. Together with flame‐retardant strategies, the total heat release during thermal runaway can be further reduced, with the measured peak temperatures around pouch cells being effectively suppressed below 400°C. This work uncovers a pervasive yet previously underappreciated high‐energy reaction in batteries and offers new design strategies for improving thermal safety.
n502380544241: Solid‐state MgH2 holds immense promise for high‐capacity hydrogen storage, yet its practical deployment is severely hindered by extreme atmospheric susceptibility and an elusive activated dehydrogenation mechanism. Herein, we report a armor like architectural design featuring asymmetric Ni‐N3 sites and nanoparticles (NPs) co‐decorated within a flexible nitrogen‐doped graphene (NG). Driven by the electronic synergy between the Ni‐N3 sites and the highly active Ni NPs, the NG achieves robust encapsulation of MgH2, providing a rigid size‐exclusion barrier against ambient O2/H2O infiltration. Concurrently, strong electronic interactions between MgH2 and Ni species optimize the MgH2 electronic structure, which further reduces its reactivity toward O2/H2O, enabling the MgH2 to preserve its full capacity even after a 28‐day cumulative air exposure. Furthermore, the encapsulated Ni NPs undergo an in situ reaction to form Mg2Ni nanorivets, which serve as high‐flux interfacial hydrogen pumps, while creating a vital spatial buffer during dynamic cycling, thereby achieving 95% capacity retention over 360 cycles at 300°C. Density functional theory calculations confirm that the electronic hybridization induced by the asymmetric Ni‐N3 sites, Ni NPs, and Mg2Ni nanorivets destabilizes Mg‐H bonds. This multi‐scale engineering of environmental isolation, electronic modulation, and structural riveting presents a robust blueprint for air‐tolerant, fast‐kinetics solid‐state hydrogen storage.
ncafcaf34fab4: All‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) with Li‐metal or Li‐metal‐free anodes enable high energy density, yet high‐loading cathodes induce severe mechanical instability, leading to rapid cell failure. Herein, we identify stress accumulation caused by repetitive Li plating/stripping as a critical degradation origin in ASSBs and propose a mechanically adaptive Ag–carbon/carbon nanofiber (CNF) hybrid anode to address this challenge. Operando pressure analysis and mechanical modeling reveal that increasing cathode areal capacity substantially amplifies pressure fluctuations and dynamic mechanical instability, leading to interfacial disruption and short‐circuiting. To mitigate this behavior, the Ag–C interlayer and porous CNF framework were independently customized to provide complementary electrochemical regulation and mechanical buffering functions. The Ag–C layer promotes uniform Li nucleation through Ag–Li alloy‐assisted interfacial regulation, while the porous CNF host accommodates volumetric changes and dissipates stress. Phase‐field modeling and microstructural analyses reveal sequential Ag–Li alloying within the Ag–C interlayer, CNF lithiation and pore filling, and controlled interfacial Li deposition, thereby spatially redistributing volumetric expansion. Consequently, the Ag–C/CNF architecture significantly reduces pressure fluctuation and enables stable cycling over 250 cycles under high‐loading conditions (∼5 mAh cm−2). Furthermore, stable pouch‐cell operation is demonstrated under practical stack pressures of 1 and 2 MPa, highlighting a viable strategy for mechanically robust high‐energy‐density ASSBs.
n82f7cf236446: Lithium–metal batteries are widely regarded as a key direction for next-generation energy storage systems due to high energy density. However, LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2||Li battery systems face severe challenges in practical application, including lithium dendrite growth, interfacial side reactions and structural degradation of high-nickel cathodes. Here, we proposed a versatile modification strategy combining in-situ interfacial transformation with polymer phase regulation to fabricate self-healing solid polymer electrolyte with fast ion transport and stable interface. This strategy not only constructs fast ion channels and suppresses hydrofluoric acid production by in-situ converting Li2CO3 on the Li6.4La3Zr1.4Ta0.6O12 surface into Li2PO3F interfacial layer, but also induces the transition of PVDF from α-phase to high polarity β-phase using ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid to promote lithium salt dissolution and reduce Li+ migration resistance. The as-prepared electrolyte exhibits extended electrochemical voltage windows (5.13 V), high room-temperature ionic conductivity (1.694 mS cm− 1), excellent thermal stability (200°C), high elongation at break (422.6%), and superior cycling stability (89.4% retention after 500 cycles at 1 C). A non-destructive monitoring method based on dp/|dQ| and dT/|dQ| differential signals has been developed to track electrochemical-mechanical-thermal responses during battery operation. This work provides an effective strategy for designing solid polymer electrolytes with high ionic conductivity and interfacial stability.
n7078bb7dc390: Dual electrode‐free (DEF) Zn─MnO2 batteries based on dissolution‐deposition chemistry are promising candidates for large‐scale energy storage due to their lightweight architecture and high theoretical capacity (616 mAh g−1). However, poor interfacial reversibility and the accumulation of “dead manganese” significantly limit their lifespan. Here, we demonstrate a stable DEF battery enabled by an anion‐regulation strategy using a hybrid electrolyte (E‐OA) comprising trifluoromethanesulfonate (OTf−) and acetate (Ac−) ions. At the anode, OTf− facilitates the formation of a fluoride‐rich solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI), effectively suppressing dendrite growth and the hydrogen evolution reaction. At the cathode, the synergistic anionic environment elevates the MnO2 nucleation overpotential, shifting the electrocrystallization pathway to an instantaneous nucleation mode. The kinetically driven growth process traps abundant structural defects, identified as proton‐compensated manganese vacancies (Ruetschi defects). These vacancies lower the thermodynamic energy barrier for Mn─O bond cleavage, thereby ensuring highly reversible dissolution. Consequently, the E‐OA‐based DEF battery achieves exceptional stability for over 7500 cycles at 0.5 mAh cm−2 and sustains 600 cycles at 2 mAh cm−2 (10 mA cm−2), demonstrating superior rate capability and versatility in both flow and gel battery configurations. This work provides a transformative strategy for high‐energy aqueous batteries via tailored anion chemistry and kinetics‐driven defect engineering.
nd19116b8c808: Alkaline seawater electrolysis is a promising route for sustainable hydrogen production, yet its practical implementation is severely constrained by chloride‐induced corrosion and limited anode durability during the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Here, we develop synergistic fluoride‐management, defect‐engineering, and polymer‐interfacial‐protection strategy for NiFe‐LDH anodes, enabling kilo‐hour‐scale operation at ampere‐level current densities in natural seawater. A custom‐designed microwave‐assisted method produces fluoride‐protected NiFe layered double hydroxide on nickel foam (F‑NiFe‑LDHMW/NF). The electrode is subsequently tailored through controlled Zn depletion to generate an evolving cation‐deficient environment, followed by electropolymerization of calmagite to construct a multifunctional poly(calmagite) (poly(CM)) interfacial layer. The optimized F‑NiFeZnvac‑LDHMW@CM/NF anode delivered exceptional stable operation for 1000 h in simulated seawater and 1650 h in natural seawater at a commercial‐scale current density of 1000 mA cm−2. Mechanistic analyses combining stage‐resolved characterization, electrolyte analysis, and DFT reveal complementary intrinsic and extrinsic stabilization mechanisms: F− regulation and the evolving cation‐defect environment modify the structural and electronic state of NiFe‐LDH, while poly(CM) suppresses Cl− access and adsorption and delays interfacial corrosion. During prolonged electrolysis, F− undergoes dynamic redistribution and gradual leaching, accompanied by controlled catalyst reconstruction rather than catastrophic structural degradation. This multilevel stabilization strategy can be a step forward toward practical seawater electrolysis.
na22b2c2f9f6a: Modulating the electronic structure and interfacial wettability of cathode catalysts is crucial for enhancing intrinsic activity and broadening triple‐phase interfaces for oxygen reduction reactions (ORR) in zinc−air batteries (ZABs), yet achieving their synergistic regulation faces a big challenge. Herein, an N/F source modulation strategy is proposed to synthesize porous carbon nanofibers anchored with MnF2 nanocrystals and N/F heteroatoms (MnF2/NF−CNF). The unique interconnected fibrous and hierarchical porous architecture, together with tailored MnF2 embedding and N/F doping, achieves an optimal balance between activity and wettability regulation. Excellent ORR performance with a high half‐wave potential of 0.87 V vs. RHE and limiting current density of 6.34 mA cm−2 is achieved, outperforming Pt/C and most previously reported Mn‐based/heteroatom‐doped systems. Theoretical and experimental analyses reveal surface N dopants as active sites, with MnF2 modulating p‐orbital configuration, refining ORR pathways. Meanwhile, surface F dopants, in synergy with the porous architecture, regulate wettability, equilibrate electrolyte/oxygen transport, and substantially extend triple‐phase reaction interfaces. The assembled ZAB delivers an exceptional peak power density of 181.5 mW cm−2 with high specific capacity, rate capability, and cycling stability. This work deciphers the regulatory mechanism balancing catalytic activity and interfacial wettability, proving a versatile strategy for developing advanced ORR electrocatalysts in ZABs.
ncb86ebd59219: Lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) are central to modern energy storage, yet evaluating their internal states under extreme thermal fluctuations remains a critical challenge. Here we present a non‐destructive evaluation framework that leverages the quasi‐static component (QSC) of nonlinear ultrasonic guided waves. By integrating an operando electro‐acoustic‐thermal platform, we isolate temperature‐induced artefacts from intrinsic acoustic signals. This statistical compensation enables the precise, simultaneous prediction of state of charge (SOC) and state of charge relative to nominal capacity (SOCN) across a wide temperature span (−10°C to 40°C). Furthermore, in situ multidimensional characterization maps these ultrasonic signatures to temperature‐dependent mechanics and irreversible capacity fade mechanisms. Ultimately, this unified framework provides a scalable, quantitative diagnostic tool for reliable energy systems operating under extreme environments.
n70d8fc3949b3: Magnesium‐based hydrogen storage materials exhibit great application potential, but high operating temperature and slow kinetics hinder their large‐scale utilization. Here, the amorphous‐carbon‐stabilized Mg particles decorated with sub‐2 nm ZrO2 nanoclusters are reported, which were in situ fabricated via ball milling of commercial Mg powder, acetone (ACE), and zirconium acetylacetonate (Zr(acac)4). The optimized Mg‐ACE‐1 wt.% Zr composite achieves rapid hydrogen absorption of 4.25 wt.% at 30°C within 60 min and exhibits high cycling stability with nearly no H2 capacity fading after 40 cycles at 300°C under 30 bar H2. Notably, the Mg‐ACE‐1 wt.% Zr sample enables reversible hydrogenation at room temperature and dehydrogenation at high temperature, achieving better energy efficiency than conventional thermally driven MgH2 and showing promise for coupling with renewable hydrogen production. Interfacial characterizations and DFT calculations confirm that the in situ formed ZrO2/Mg interface accelerates H2 adsorption, dissociation, and diffusion.

n135044a524a6: CO 2 shifts the redox balance of Mo–V catalysts: mixed oxides undergo reduction and deactivate, whereas supported VO x /MoO 3 shows greater redox stability and less coke. Stability depends on the reduction-reoxidation balance.
n3ac0cef0c6fe: As an efficient catalyst for the C-2 epimerization of aldoses, molybdenum oxide is hindered by surface instability, which adversely affect catalytic kinetics and product selectivity. In this work, a γ-Al2O3-supported...
n356cc0f85f48: A chemistry-centered framework for Ga-based liquid metal biomimetics, linking multiscale material design and interfacial reactions to matter simulation, energy conversion, information processing and cross-habitat adaptation.
ne4cd050b1ff3: A step-resolved framework explains how catalytic environments regulate adsorption, dehydrogenation, chemical conversion, C–C cleavage and desorption to shape glycerol electrooxidation selectivity, activity and stability.
n8da6a96460eb: Solid-state batteries pairing lithium metal anodes with inorganic solid electrolytes promise a step change in energy density, but during charging at practical rates lithium dendrites penetrate the solid electrolyte, short-circuiting the cell. Our current understanding of dendrite propagation derives largely from symmetric Li−Li cells with millimetre-thick electrolyte pellets, whereas practical cells will employ solid electrolyte separators less than 100 μm in thickness. In this work, we use in situ synchrotron X-ray computed tomography to show that dendrites in a thin Li6PS5Cl separator, which generally propagate from the lithium anode to the cathode, can be made to propagate laterally by the cathode. Volume contraction of the NMC cathode during charge places the thin separator under lateral compressive stress, deflecting dendritic cracks to propagate laterally (parallel to the electrodes) rather than transversely (across the separator). The result is that the cell resists short circuit even after passing 3 mA h cm−2 capacity at a rate of 3 mA cm−2. Replacing NMC with zero-volume-change pre-lithiated Li4Ti5O12 removes this compressive stress, and the cell rapidly fails by transverse cracking. Chemomechanical modelling rationalises both behaviours, with cathode volume change emerging as a design parameter that can suppress or accelerate failure, with direct implications for cathode selection and cathode/separator interface engineering in practical solid-state batteries.
n2216855ec587: Rare-earth hybrid nitrate double perovskites (REHNDPs) have recently emerged as an intriguing subclass of functional materials, combining structural diversity with rich intrinsic optoelectronic, magnetic, piezoelectric, and ferroelectric properties. Although notable progress has been made in three-dimensional (3D) and 2D REHNDPs, 1D counterparts have yet to be discovered. Herein, by introducing the bulky organic cation 1-adamantyltrimethylammonium (TMAA+), we report a family of 1D REHNDPs with the general formula (TMAA)2LnCs(NO3)6 (Ln = La3+, Ce3+, Pr3+, Nd3+, Sm3+, and Eu3+). Distinct from the μ2-κ3(O,O′,O″) mode characteristic of 2D and 3D REHNDPs, the bridging NO3− ligands adopt a μ2-κ3(O,O′) coordination mode in 1D counterparts. Strikingly, (TMAA)2SmCs(NO3)6 possesses a step-like high-temperature dielectric switch at 431.7 K. (TMAA)2EuCs(NO3)6 shows brilliant photoluminescence with a quantum yield of 65.46% and a lifetime of 5.21 ms. The X-ray detector based on (TMAA)2EuCs(NO3)6 demonstrates high X-ray sensitivity of 560 μC Gyair−1 cm−2 and a low detection limit of 153 nGyair s−1 under a bias of 25 V. This work bridges a critical dimensional gap and significantly expands the structural and functional portfolio of the REHNDPs.
n986a0e2cfb8f: Rechargeable Zn−air batteries (ZABs) have attracted considerable attention as promising energy storage systems owing to their high theoretical energy density and environmental compatibility. However, their practical application is hindered by the sluggish ORR/OER kinetics at the air cathode. This study investigates low Pt-modified Fe- and Ni-doped hexagonal perovskites (BaTi0.8M0.2O3−δ, M = Fe and Ni) as robust bifunctional oxygen electrocatalysts, focusing on the modulation of their participating metal and electronic structures. Structural analysis confirms the formation of stable hexagonal phases, while Pt deposition induces distinct electronic reconstruction depending on the dopant species. With a higher ORR catalytic behavior than the Pt/BTO-Ni catalyst, the Pt/BTO-Fe catalyst demonstrates remarkable bifunctionality driven through dopant-dependent surface interaction modulation by Pt with optimized surface/lattice oxygen distribution. Notably, in full-cell ZAB tests, the optimized Pt/BTO-Fe catalyst achieved a comparable peak power density of 124.8 mW cm−2 with a remarkably low round-trip efficiency decay rate of 0.41%/h under stable operation for 60 h, compared to the commercial IrO2 + Pt/C benchmark (125.2 mW cm−2 and 1.39%/h) even at lower Pt content. These findings highlight the critical role of Pt2+-mediated interfacial interactions in governing catalytic durability, providing a rational strategy for designing highly durable bifunctional electrocatalysts for next-generation energy storage systems.
n774c976db3fb: The number of possible crystal structures vastly exceeds the number realized among thermodynamically stable inorganic materials, suggesting that experimentally accessible structure space is organized around a limited set of preferred structural frameworks. Analysis of 23,160 structures on the thermodynamic convex hull identifies 6820 distinct structural frameworks, of which 2382 recur across multiple chemically distinct materials and are therefore classified as structural prototypes. Within a filtered dataset, metallic systems exhibit particularly strong structural recurrence, with 6270 materials grouped into 535 frameworks and 327 prototypes, while 5557 ionic compounds occupy 1704 frameworks and 696 prototypes. These results demonstrate that stable inorganic materials naturally coalesce into recurrent structural prototypes and do not require any a priori definition through manual curation. The resulting recurrence-based catalog also provides an empirical measure of framework prevalence, enabling the relative likelihood of structural frameworks in future materials to be estimated from their recurrence among known compounds.
n70e42d8e642f: To understand the nature of multicenter interactions in periodic solids and their associated materials (transport) properties, we investigate and quantify multicenter bonding on the basis of the underlying wave function, namely by a combination of quantum-chemical tools for a diverse series of functional materials. First, we probe all compounds by projected force constants based on plane-wave phonon calculations, followed by a projection from plane waves onto a local-orbital framework and its thorough quantum-chemical analysis. While the three-center crystal orbital bond index is used to quantify multicenter bonding between atomic orbitals, the linear combination of fragment orbitals provides a molecular-orbital lens. Eventually, both approaches are fused into the molecular orbital contribution index that directly attributes the contributions of a single molecular orbital to a multicenter bond.
n185e0085945e: SAPO-34 is an excellent catalyst for methanol-to-olefins (MTO) reaction. Simultaneously alleviating the diffusion limitations and optimizing the acidity of SAPO-34 is extremely challenging. Herein, a three-dimensional hollow square array SAPO-34 (SAPO-34-HSA) with a sinusoidal-like distribution of silicon was synthesized in a simple way. The role of triethylamine (TEA) switches between the etchant and structure-directing agent according to the reaction temperature. In the heating stage, the seed with high silicon content was etched by TEA; during the crystallization process, TEA guides the epitaxial growth of raw materials on the seed crystal, forming a hollow core−shell structure; after crystallization, the shell was partly leached to form a hollow square array structure. The sinusoidal-like distribution of silicon is conducive to promoting olefin cycling in the hydrocarbon pool mechanism and significantly improving the selectivity of ethylene. So the SAPO-34-HSA catalyst exhibits 70%−400% longer catalytic lifetime in MTO reaction compared with the seed under different reaction conditions.
na923104221b9: Amid escalating energy demand and severe environmental effects, green hydrogen production via water electrolysis has emerged as a cornerstone technology. Conventional alkaline water electrolysis (AWE) generally suffers from low hydrogen purity and current density, while proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) relies on high-cost noble-metal catalysts and harsh acidic conditions. To mitigate these limitations, researchers have turned to anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) as a promising alternative, offering an intermediate pathway that pairs the non-noble metal-based catalysts of AWE with the high purity and compact architecture of PEMWE. However, AEMWE technology remains comparatively underdeveloped. Herein, we have summarized transition metal chalcogenides (TMCs) as a low-cost catalyst platform for AEMWE devices. The current review focuses on a comparative analysis across the chalcogen family and discusses how variations in their physicochemical properties influence the overall catalytic performance of anion exchange membrane devices. In addition, the underlying mechanisms of AEMWE, the membrane-electrode assembly, and cell configurations have also been explored in detail. The review critically examines the intrinsic activity of the transition metal chalcogenide-based catalyst layer against device-level performance metrics and further highlights emerging future directions. The review aims to provide a clear roadmap toward the development of highly efficient and commercially competitive AEMWE systems for next-generation green hydrogen production.
n09b6b63883fd: Seawater electrolysis for green hydrogen production urgently demands high-performance electrocatalysts that simultaneously deliver fast reaction kinetics with robust chloride ion (Cl−) resistance. Herein, we report an ultralow Pt-loaded (<1 wt %) Pt/Fe2O3 catalyst rich in Pt−Fe atomic pairs synthesized via a photoreduction synthetic strategy. Photogenerated electrons drive the selective reduction of Pt precursors at low-coordinate Fe3+ sites on α-Fe2O3 (012) facets, constructing Pt−Fe pair interfaces that enable directional electron transfer from Fe-dz2 to Pt-dz2 orbitals. This electronic modulation optimizes the Gibbs free energy of hydrogen adsorption, weakens the intrinsic affinity of active sites toward Cl−, and accelerates water dissociation. The as-synthesized catalyst achieves ultralow overpotentials of 9 and 51 mV at 10 and 100 mA cm−2 respectively in alkaline simulated seawater, with a slight potential decay of only 0.08 mV h−1 over 1000 h of continuous operation, outperforming most state-of-the-art electrocatalysts. When integrated into an anion exchange membrane electrolyzer, it delivers a low cell voltage of 2.0 V at 500 mA cm−2 and maintains stable operation for 200 h at 100 mA cm−2.
n15bde14f6444: Introducing homologous acceptors into PM6:L8-BO tailors aggregation kinetics during film formation, extending the crystal-growth window to ∼100 ms and reducing excited-state energetic disorder, enabling ternary devices to achieve efficiencies >20%.
n884ee42aebac: All-solid-state sodium batteries (ASSBs) offer high energy density and safety, but conventional solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layers suffer from low efficiency and severe side reactions. This work proposes a novel strategy based on a borate-enriched SEI that effectively suppresses side reactions and enables dendrite-free Na plating/stripping, providing valuable mechanistic insights and a feasible pathway toward high-performance ASSBs.
n06a787ecfdfe: Antiferromagnetic spintronics promises ultrafast device performance, yet the essential Néel vector reversal is hindered by its intrinsic immunity to external magnetic fields. Here, we propose a mechanism for deterministic Néel vector reversal in 2D van der Waals antiferromagnets enabled by ultrafast laser pulses. The core physics involves light-induced asymmetric interlayer demagnetization, which drives the antiferromagnet into a transient ferrimagnetic state with a finite net moment. This transient symmetry breaking allows the Néel vector to be controlled by an external magnetic field. We identify that the intrinsic structural and electronic asymmetries and spin–orbit-coupling mediated spin flips are essential for this process. Using first-principles calculations and real-time time-dependent density functional theory, we further demonstrate this mechanism in bilayer NiICl and YI2. Our work establishes a general strategy for the optical manipulation of 2D antiferromagnetic order.
n413ba0ff9ef0: TADF-sensitized fluorescence (TSF), also known as hyperfluorescence, combines efficient triplet exciton harvesting with the narrowband emission of fluorescent emitters. Yet, its performance depends on the interplay between exciton conversion, energy transfer, and molecular organization across different length scales. Herein, we review recent progress in nanoscale exciton-transfer engineering for TSF, with emphasis on molecular excited-state dynamics, sensitizer-dopant spatial control, diversified energy-transfer pathways, and interlayer sensitization. These approaches regulate exciton conversion and lifetime, balance Förster and Dexter energy transfer, and control exciton distribution within emissive layers and across interfaces. We also discuss emerging directions including kinetic matching, spatial organization, and multiscale modeling for understanding the links between molecular structure, energy-transfer dynamics, and device performance. This Mini-Review provides profound insights into transforming random blend systems into controllable nanoscale exciton-transfer networks, paving the way for efficient narrowband TSF OLEDs.
n031a74c37fd9: Structural colors generated by photonic crystals (PCs) have attracted interest in optical sensing. However, the sensing behavior of porous PCs is commonly tailored through material composition, pore structure, or surface chemistry. Here, we show that the spatial configuration of sequence-switchable MOF-on-MOF Bragg stacks regulates molecular access and adsorption while preserving the constituent metal–organic frameworks (MOFs). The reflection wavelength is continuously tuned across the visible spectrum by controlling layer thickness and refractive-index contrast, producing blue-to-red structural colors with a peak reflectance of approximately 90%. Reversing the layer sequence generates distinct optical response amplitudes and kinetics toward volatile organic compounds (VOCs). Combined optical analysis and molecular dynamics simulations further show that the sensing responses depend not only on molecular uptake but also on spatial adsorption distribution and framework–guest interactions. These findings establish molecular transport pathway control through spatial configuration as an additional strategy for regulating the sensing behavior of porous photonic materials.
n9818df8af9b2: Binuclear metalloenzymes remain underexplored for new-to-nature biocatalytic reactions. Now binuclear copper enzymes, particularly a Bacillus megaterium tyrosinase, are used as a catalytic platform for stereoselective radical azidation, bromination, chlorination and isothiocyanation reactions, expanding metalloenzyme catalysis beyond mononuclear systems.
n77d71dfc8d8a: Aptamers have generally been understood as nucleic acids that recognize a specific ligand. Now it has been shown that secondary aptamers can recognize the ligand-bound conformation of a primary aptamer, enabling recognition of molecules that lack multiple binding sites for sandwich assays. This mechanism can be integrated into lateral flow assays for targets, including serotonin.
n9e927aacd0ea: Adapt-ring networks consisting of dense, reconfigurable α-cyclodextrin crystalline domains and sparsely crosslinked polyethylene glycol form adaptive polymer materials that remodel and strengthen in response to mechanical stress.
n56772df9d20d: Predictive human-relevant model systems are outlined in a Review by integrating engineered materials and microenvironments, human tissue and organ models, computational approaches, and closed-loop strategies. Controlling the boundary conditions, biological organization, measurements and model calibration can improve mechanistic insight, reproducibility and translational relevance across applications.
n6f423c8acb1b: Scanning tunnelling luminescence resolves exciton emission from individual defects in monolayer MoS2 and identifies carbon–hydrogen complexes as the source of a ubiquitous defect emission band.
n0e748516d9b0: Harnessing viral mimicry mechanisms enhances cancer vaccination by improving long-range antigen presentation and T cell activation.
n6d96b4689465: Engineered dendritic-cell vesicles enrich antigen-presentation ligands and viral-mimicry programmes to drive T cell immunity and melanoma control.
n280d12d67af2: Low-energy photoredox catalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for promoting mild, chemoselective transformations through radical intermediates. While various red-light-absorbing photocatalysts, including molecular porphyrins, have enabled diverse synthetic transformations, these processes operate almost exclusively under homogeneous conditions in organic solvents. Here, we demonstrate that integrating a photoactive porphyrin as the organic linker in a metal–organic framework (MOF) affords an air- and aqueous-compatible, heterogeneous photoredox catalyst. Using porphyrinic zirconium MOFs such as PCN-224, we enable a range of bond-forming reactions, including Giese additions, C(sp2)–H alkylations, C(sp2)–H arylations, formal cycloadditions, and radical polymerizations under mild red-light irradiation. While preserving the intrinsic reactivity of molecular porphyrins, heterogenization provides practical advantages including efficient photocatalysis independent of catalyst solubility and reaction medium, structural tunability, high turnover number (TON), and easy catalyst recovery and reuse. Mechanistic studies indicate that radical generation occurs predominantly within the framework pores.
n7a5744b31780: Nickel oxyhydroxide (NiO(OH)) is the catalytically active species during electrochemical alcohol oxidation at nickel electrodes. Herein, we demonstrate that the adopted phase structure of NiO(OH) (β- and γ-NiO(OH)) can dramatically influence the catalytic properties of nickel electrodes. We show that β-NiO(OH) oxidizes aliphatic alcohols preferentially to aldehydes and that carboxylates are formed at γ-NiO(OH). By combining the effect of the NiO(OH) phase with reagent effects (electrolyte pH, alcohol concentration, and trace amounts of Fe), we achieve aldehyde formation with ∼90% selectivity or carboxylate formation with ∼85% selectivity. Furthermore, we perform an in situ Raman spectroelectrochemical study to elucidate the reaction conditions that favor the formation of β- and γ-NiO(OH) phases, respectively. Freshly deposited nickel electrodes form γ-NiO(OH) phases upon oxidation, whereas an electrochemical conditioning protocol can be employed to transform γ- to β-NiO(OH). Finally, we show that the efficiency of this transformation depends on the precise reaction conditions and the precursor used. Hence, we showcase that the exact surface structure of the phase formed in situ on top of transition metal (oxides) affects the product distribution of electrochemical reactions. Moreover, we highlight how the “history” of these catalysts affects their performance via an intricate interplay among the reaction environment, pre-treatment, and surface structure.
n8e2faa9f89d5: Cyclic α-halo ketones and vicinal halohydrins serve as essential synthetic intermediates or structural motifs for a variety of pharmaceuticals. Ketoreductase-catalyzed dynamic reductive kinetic resolution (DYRKR) of cyclic α-halo ketones is an attractive strategy for the synthesis of chiral cyclic vicinal halohydrins. However, we found that the spontaneous racemization of the α-halo groups of 3-bromo-chroman-4-ones and 2-bromo-1-tetralones was less efficient than the ketoreductase-catalyzed reduction of the more reactive enantiomers, resulting in a low conversion and poor (dia)stereoselectivity. To address this challenge, two classes of racemization catalysts were identified: prolinol-derived organocatalysts and racemase-based biocatalysts, both of which could accelerate the racemization of cyclic α-halo ketones. Consequently, combining these catalysts with ketoreductases improved both the conversion and product (dia)stereoselectivity of the DYRKR. Based on the discovery of racemization catalysts, this work provides an efficient strategy for biocatalytic dynamic kinetic resolution and an operationally simple route for the synthesis of chiral cyclic vicinal halohydrins.
n0c7be96d28db: Developing practicable layered oxide cathodes remains a critical challenge for sodium-ion batteries. Here, by systematically varying Cu contents to tune TM–O covalency in Nay[CuxFe3/9Mn(6/9–x)]O2, we show that an optimal degree of covalency simultaneously boosts energy density and structural resilience. The optimized Na7/9[Cu2/9Fe3/9Mn4/9]O2 delivers 131.6 mAh g–1 at 0.1 C and retains 80% capacity after 500 cycles at 0.5 C. Mechanistically, the enhanced Cu–O covalency converts trivalent Cu from a conventional d8 to a heavily mixed d9L configuration, delocalizing holes across the extended TM–O network, enlarging polaron size, and “flattening the ripple” of local lattice distortions. Side-by-side comparison with an ionic Ni analogue confirms the suppressed cation migration and polarization. Crucially, the covalency-driven stabilization is not unbounded–excessive covalency rigidifies the lattice, defining a covalency threshold for optimal performance. These findings establish covalency modulation within a defined threshold as a predictive design principle for durable layered oxide cathodes.
n1519c51a3729: Extracting uranyl ions (UO22+) from uranium mining leachates can enhance national uranium security and mitigate the environmental impact of nuclear energy. Conventional techniques such as ion exchange and iron-based reductive precipitation have notable limitations. This study reports that the uvanite (U2V6O21) electrode, a layered uranium-vanadium oxide, enables potentiodynamic decoupling of UO22+ and proton intercalation/deintercalation, as well as proton-induced UO22+/UO3 precipitation and dissolution reactions. Building on a comprehensive understanding of charge-transfer and transport mechanisms, we found that potentiodynamic modulation enables selective capture of uranium species using a uvanite electrode. By allowing competing cations to deintercalate at lower potentials and preventing proton deintercalation, UO3 dissolution is inhibited, achieving a high UO3 recovery capacity of 515 mg/g at 10 times the competing cation concentration. The new electrochemistry of the uvanite electrode helps develop cost-effective, sustainable battery electrodes for critical ion extraction from water.
n6f24301ad204: The development of an efficient and reversible hydrogen storage and transport system is crucial for a sustainable hydrogen economy. Liquid organic hydrogen carriers (LOHCs) offer a potential solution due to their high hydrogen storage density and ease of transport, but conventional thermal approaches for the hydrogenation and dehydrogenation of LOHCs remain heavily reliant on harsh operating conditions. Here, we demonstrate a plasmonic photocatalysis approach for toluene hydrogenation to methylcyclohexane and methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation to toluene under substantially milder conditions. We observe changes in reaction orders and substantial reductions in activation barriers by 0.34 and 1.11 eV for toluene hydrogenation and methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation, respectively, as compared to thermocatalysis due to the role of hot carriers. Both reactions exhibit high activity, stability (>70 h), and excellent selectivity (>95%), offering a sustainable pathway for on-demand hydrogen storage and release.
ndae8349a2031: During the start‐up/shut‐down (SU/SD) processes of proton‐exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), anode reversal generates an excessively high voltage that accelerates corrosion of the cathode Pt/C catalyst. Conventional approaches focus on blocking the delivery of oxygen or electrons to the anode, but fail to address the intrinsic activity coupling of Pt/C for both hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR) and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Here, we report a strategy that can selectively tailor the catalytic function of Pt nanoparticles. We used phosphorus to modulate the electronic structure of low‐loading Pt clusters on a carbon support, forming a Pt/P‐BP catalyst. The P‐coordination downshifts the d‐band center of Pt cluster, as evidenced by in situ ATR‑FTIR spectroscopy and DFT calculations, thereby widening the activity gap between HOR and ORR. Specifically, compared to Pt/C, Pt/P‐BP enhances HOR mass activity by fivefold while substantially suppressing ORR, transforming Pt from a bifunctional catalyst into a highly selective HOR catalyst. Consequently, Pt/P‐BP achieves a 10.8‐fold higher HOR/ORR selectivity than Pt/C. In SU/SD experiments, the Pt/P‐BP anode significantly reduces carbon corrosion of the cathode catalyst layer, maintaining the fuel cell performance better than Pt/C. This work paves a new avenue toward durable PEMFCs and inspires the selectivity design for electrocatalysts.
nab686dda6fe4: Earth-abundant Cu and Co are attractive electrocatalysts for nitrate reduction to ammonia (NO3 −RR); however, conventional solid-solution alloys with single-phase active sites lack effective intermediate spillover, impeding the hydrogenation of multiple reaction intermediates and limiting NH3 selectivity under dilute nitrate conditions. Here we report phase-separated yet electronically coupled Janus–CuCo alloys synthesized via a time–charge regulated electrochemical reduction strategy, forming metallic Cu/Co domains with a well-defined interphase electronic structure. This Janus architecture enables relay catalysis, in which Cu domains activate NO3 −, intermediates migrate to Cu−Co interfaces for hydrogenation, and adjacent Co domains promote subsequent NH3 formation. In situ characterizations reveal pronounced Cu–Co synergy, where Co sites regulate *H-mediated hydrogenation while the balanced surface coverage of *H and *NO3 − optimizes NH3 selectivity and yield. Consequently, the optimized Janus Cu−Co catalyst, Janus–Cu70Co30/NOMC, achieves a peak NH3 Faradaic efficiency (FENH3) of 95.5% at −500 mA cm−2 and delivers a FENH3 of 93.1% with an NH3 yield rate of 4.2 mg h−1 mgcat −1 at −0.4 V vs RHE in an MEA flow cell under low nitrate concentrations. These findings establish phase separation with electronic coupling, enabled by electrochemical time–charge control, as an effective design principle for efficient multistep NO3 −RR electrocatalysis.
ne5813f627e66: Ethylene oligomerization is pivotal in the petrochemical industry to produce olefins and polymers. In this work, we conduct density functional theory (DFT) calculations to investigate ethylene oligomerization catalyzed by a...
naf17cd83b56e: Pd/TiO 2 catalysts enable mild reductive amination of aromatic and bio-based aldehydes. Particle size control and SMSI enhance amine selectivity, boost turnover frequency nearly 200-fold, and support reuse.
ndd2015aa7900: Intramolecular cross-electrophile coupling (iXEC) offers a unified strategy for building semisaturated rings directly from simple dielectrophiles. This work establishes conditions that generate persistent nickel intermediates capable of rapid radical capture through solvent-controlled activation of aryl and alkyl electrophiles. The approach enables efficient access to heteroaromatic, spirocyclic, and macrocyclic compounds under mild conditions, thus providing a broadly applicable platform for pharmaceuticals and natural products where arrays of diverse ring systems can be synthesized from a single core.
nbfcf0cc0b1a8: Atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP) combines increasingly sustainable polymerization processes with precise macromolecular engineering to create materials with extended lifetimes, improved circularity, and advanced functions for energy technologies. This perspective discusses recent advances and future opportunities for greener, scalable ATRP processes and the design of high-performance polymeric materials that integrate functionality and sustainability.
n865b42e4fa17: Combining quantitative live-cell imaging, electrophysiology, and atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, we establish a mechanism by which CPP additives drive the direct translocation of proteins across cellular membranes through membrane potential-dependent water pores. This framework provides a basis for intracellular delivery of protein therapeutics to expand access to intracellular, previously undruggable targets.
neb9bf52fa7d4: Zhou et al. develop an oxygen-independent photocatalytic strategy that converts glutathione to its oxidized form while generating hydrogen in cancer cells, thereby disrupting the intracellular redox balance. This catalytic redox remodeling induces ferroptosis and antitumor immune activation, establishing an oxygen-independent mode of photocatalytic cancer therapy.
n44a90ab06014: A battery stability prediction model covering LIBs, SIBs, and ZIBs has been proposed. The electron-ion transport mismatch is identified as a key determinant of battery stability. A linear correlation between the battery stability and the electron-ion transport mismatch has been revealed: the closer the transport rates of electrons and ions, the more stable the battery. The battery stability could be predicted rapidly from the electron-ion mismatch, with no need for time-consuming long-term cycling.
n660917528ddd: Hollandite-type α-MnO2 is a prototypical tunnel-structured host for rechargeable batteries, yet the atomic-scale mechanisms governing multivalent-ion insertion remain poorly understood. Here, we reveal how guest-ion species dictate electrochemical reaction pathways through distinct occupation modes within the one-dimensional tunnels of α-MnO2. By combining electrochemical analyses, atomic-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy, and soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy, we directly correlate reaction kinetics with guest-ion configurations and the accompanying structural and electronic responses of the host framework. Electrochemical measurements reveal substantial diffusion-controlled contributions for both Na+ and Mg2+, whereas Ca2+ exhibits predominantly surface-controlled behavior. Atomic-resolution imaging demonstrates that, despite their comparable macroscopic kinetic contributions, Na+ and Mg2+ exhibit distinctly different microscopic insertion modes: Na+ homogeneously occupies the tunnel-center sites throughout the particles, whereas Mg2+ occupies both tunnel-center and off-center sites, with pronounced near-surface enrichment accompanied by local tunnel distortion. In contrast, the Ca2+ reaction is largely confined to the near-surface region, with no clearly detectable occupation of the internal tunnel sites. Soft X-ray absorption spectroscopy further reveals spatially heterogeneous Mn reduction, with more pronounced reduction near the structurally less constrained particle surface. These results establish a direct relationship between guest-ion occupation modes, electrochemical reaction pathways, and the resulting structural evolution, providing an atomic-scale design principle for engineering tunnel-type host materials for multivalent-ion insertion.
n16c95d1fb977: Multielectron redox in Li2FeS2 involves both cation and anion contributions. While prior studies have investigated this process experimentally, questions remain about the Fe-to-S redox transition, persulfide formation, and incomplete delithiation. Here, we revisit the electrochemistry of Li2FeS2 using density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Initial Fe oxidation is shown to proceed via increased Fe−S covalency driven by ligand-to-metal rehybridization. This accounts for only ∼60% of the Fe capacity, after which phase separation into Li1.5FeS2 and Li0.5FeS2 induces a shift to S oxidation. We identify nonbonding S 3p orbitals as redox-active centers. To track their evolution during delithiation, we isolate the localized nonbonding states by subtracting the bonding and antibonding contributions from the total electronic densities of states. These orbitals undergo S-to-Fe rehybridization, progressive oxidation, and eventual reorganization into persulfide bonds. At high states of charge, Li vacancies enable FeS4 tilting and facilitate S−S bond formation. Further delithiation beyond Li0.5FeS2 would require unstable S hole formation or conversion to pyrite FeS2, explaining why it is challenging to fully delithiate this material. These findings offer insights into the interplay of cation and anion redox, guiding the design of high-capacity sulfide cathodes.
n251675295ae6: Diabetic wound healing is severely impaired by persistent inflammation, bacterial infection, impaired angiogenesis, and especially disrupted bioelectrical signaling. Conductive hydrogels can help restore local bioelectrical signal transmission and provide an attractive strategy for intractable wound healing by modulating the behaviors of bioelectrically responsive skin-resident cells. Here, we developed a glucose/pH-responsive polyaniline− gelatin conductive hydrogel (HGP@D) based on double dynamic covalent crosslinking of the imine bond and boronic ester bond for promoting the Staphylococcus aureus-infected full-thickness diabetic wound healing. The HGP@D hydrogel had strong mechanical property, great tissue adhesive strength, glucose/pH dual-responsive drug release behavior, alongside robust broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, and potent intracellular antioxidation. The HGP@D hydrogel restored local bioelectrical signaling and created an anti-inflammatory wound microenvironment, thereby modulating the behaviors of skin-resident cells involved in diabetic wound repair, including fibroblast migration, macrophage M2-like polarization, and endothelial angiogenic activity. Mechanistic analyses suggested that the HGP@D hydrogel promoted infected diabetic wound healing through two Ca2+-associated regulatory axes: the Ca2+/CaMKKβ/AMPK/NF-κB axis for inflammatory regulation and the Ca2+/PI3K/Akt/mTOR/HIF-1α/VEGF axis for angiogenesis and tissue reconstruction. Overall, HGP@D provides a promising clinical therapeutic strategy for the advanced healing of diabetic wounds and other non-healing wounds by integrating glucose/pH-responsive microenvironment regulation with bioelectrical modulation.
n64c3bde4a1d7: Neutral-pH aqueous organic redox flow batteries (AORFBs) based on TEMPO catholytes and viologen anolytes have emerged as one of the most intensively developed molecular pairings for safe, scalable, long-duration energy...
n99799621e51a: Molecular-level energetic fluctuations in organic semiconductors remain a critical challenge for achieving efficient organic solar cells (OSCs). However, how molecular organization regulates dynamic energetic disorder remains largely unexplored. Here, we...
n9f6bd4657bfc: Sulfur can remain physically present in a lithium-sulfur pouch cell while becoming electrochemically inaccessible. This perspective links local electrolyte availability and the transport of lithium ions and soluble sulfur species to sulfur conversion, lithium-metal degradation, and variations in pressure and temperature. Two qualitative diagnostic questions and a staged validation protocol guide regional failure analysis and the translation of laboratory strategies into practical cells.
n3dc4dc4ec6d2: Metal halide perovskites (MHPs) have attracted significant interest in the field of X-ray detection due to their unique semiconducting properties. However, the self-powered detection capabilities of almost all of these materials rely on their inherent ferroelectricity or heterojunction structures, yet the structure design and fabrication still pose significant challenges. By incorporating a polymer into a centrosymmetric MHP, we successfully prepared (PEA)2(FA)Pb2I7/PVDF composite flexible films (PEA = β-phenylethylamine, FA = formamidine, PVDF = poly(vinylidene fluoride)) and obtained self-powered X-ray responses in a nonpolar perovskite. Notably, the photodetector based on thin films exhibits excellent self-powered X-ray detection performance with a high sensitivity (559.11 μC Gyair–1 cm–2), a low detection limit (29.09 nGyair s–1), and excellent radiation stability. Our work offers a new strategy for self-driven devices without relying on ferroelectricity or heterojunctions, expanding halide perovskites in flexible film applications.
n46da2d92e80a: In a combined experimental and theoretical study, we demonstrate anisotropic polariton transport on the nanoscale in the van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr. While effective cavity-polariton formation emerges via the self-hybridization of ultrahigh oscillator strength excitons with a thin slab photonic mode, the absence of external mirrors facilitates spectroscopic investigation of these polaritons via cathodoluminescence (CL) on length scales inaccessible to optical excitation. This direct access allows us to precisely chart the polariton landscape with nanometric resolution, and probe polariton interference phenomena. Our finding highlights that coherent polariton transport follows the C2v symmetry of CrSBr, highly directional transport along the a-axis, while no coherent features are found along the b-axis. By extending CL spectroscopy to strongly anisotropic cavity polaritons, our work establishes this technique as a powerful tool to probe highly directional expansion and relaxation phenomena on the nanoscale, paving the way for investigating complex polaritonic landscapes in asymmetric systems.
nd9663515a541: Li-rich layered oxides (LLOs) are promising high-energy cathodes but suffer from irreversible oxygen redox and structural degradation associated with Li2MnO3 domains. Recently, disorder engineering has emerged as an effective strategy to regulate the local coordination environment and stabilize the oxygen redox of LLOs. Herein, we confirm the existence of intrinsic intralayer Li/Mn disorder within the Li2MnO3 domains, which can be classified into local Li-excess and TM-excess configurations derived from the initial Li-rich framework. Furthermore, DFT calculations suggest complementary local roles for the different disordered configurations: Li-excess domains promote oxygen redox activity, whereas TM-excess domains reinforce TM–O bonding and stabilize the framework against irreversible degradation. Consequently, M-LLO containing the coupled disordered configurations promotes more reversible anionic redox, suppresses irreversible oxygen release and transition-metal migration, and thereby delivers improved electrochemical stability. This work provides new insights into the role of intrinsic disorder regulation in Li-rich layered cathodes.
n13215fd0c13b: Negative supercoiling (underwinding) of DNA plays a vital role in regulating genome organization and gene expression. These processes often depend on the DNA structure, yet the influence of ionic strength on supercoiled DNA structure is still not well understood. Here, we develop an approach to extract detailed insight into the mechanical properties of underwound DNA from force–distance measurements. Using this approach, we demonstrate that low concentrations (2 mM) of divalent cations are sufficient to induce substantial increases in DNA persistence length at high superhelical densities. This is consistent with the formation of Z-DNA, a rigid, left-handed conformation, and suggests that Z-DNA-like structures can be more readily formed than is often assumed. We also show that divalent cations can induce extensive sawtooth-like behavior in force–extension curves of underwound DNA, revealing unexpectedly strong stabilization of secondary structures. Together, these findings demonstrate how divalent salt can sensitively modulate the stability of different underwound structures.
na9aa2fcefca1: High-performance single-photon sources at telecom C-band wavelengths are key building blocks for applications in long-distance quantum communication. Here, we report the generation of highly indistinguishable single photons at a clock rate of 2.5 GHz. This is achieved by coherently driving the biexciton transition (T1XX=64(1) ps) of a semiconductor quantum dot embedded in a microcavity with strong asymmetric Purcell enhancement. Employing pulsed two-photon resonant excitation, strong multiphoton suppression with g(2)(0) < 4% and high two-photon-interference visibility of Vraw > 85% are observed. The observed photon indistinguishability is close to the theoretical limit expected for the photonically engineered radiative cascade and matches values obtained at lower repetition rates. Our results show a substantial advancement toward interference-based quantum information protocols at unprecedented data rates in the telecom C-band.
n790488ef26bb: Applications of plasmonic nanopores for molecular sequencing remain limited by poorly controlled translocation dynamics and predominantly single-pass readout. Here, we propose an in-plane heterostructure architecture that integrates molecular transport, confinement, and surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) readout to enable deterministic and repeated interrogation of individual biomolecules. Using all-atom molecular dynamics coupled with nanoplasmonic simulations, we show that the heterostructure can actively guide molecules into and through a localized sensing region while constraining their conformational and translational dynamics. Simulated SERS signatures discriminate single-stranded DNA sequences with resolution approaching the single-nucleobase scale and further suggest the feasibility of distinguishing polyglutamine tracts of different lengths. Importantly, the in-plane geometry allows molecules to be controllably transported back and forth across the sensing region, providing a route to repeated measurements of the same molecule rather than relying on stochastic single-pass translocation. These results suggest a strategy for improving the accuracy and reproducibility of nanopore-based biomolecular sensing.
n1d15a7c24786: While additives direct Zn electrocrystallization and impact battery performance, the mechanism remains disputed. Now it has been shown that facet-dependent work function modulation upon additive adsorption governs Fermi-level equilibration and Zn crystallographic texture across 29 additives with 93.1% accuracy, providing an interfacial electronic descriptor for additive screening towards favourable Zn electrodeposition.
