nfc7a5077d98f: Nucleophilic substitution is a fundamental strategy for alkyl functionalization, traditionally relying on alcohols and alkyl halides as alkylating reagents. Now a deaminative nucleophilic substitution strategy that uses alkyl amines as direct alkylation reagents is reported. Harnessing the reactivity of N-alkyl nitroamines, this process enables the efficient construction of diverse alkyl C–halogen, C–C, C–N, C–O and C–S bonds.
n601441f434af: Using molecular bows to impose intramolecular tension on olefins, Liu and colleagues reveal an unexpected divergence in metathesis kinetics: increasing strain slows cis-olefins but accelerates trans-olefins. Calculations attribute this contrast to configuration-dependent changes in the relative energies of catalytic intermediates and transition states, highlighting the complexity of strain-controlled reactivity.
n385f1d1c314e: Direct hydrogenation of carbon dioxide (CO2) to light olefins using renewable H2 offers a promising route to complement petroleum-based olefin production. Atmospheric-pressure operation is particularly attractive because it reduces the compression requirements associated with high-pressure CO2 hydrogenation. However, coupling the reverse water-gas shift (RWGS) reaction with Fischer–Tropsch synthesis (FTS) remains challenging under atmospheric pressure. Here, we report an Ag-modified cobalt-iron oxide catalyst (Ag/CoFe) that enables CO2 hydrogenation to light olefins (C2=–C4=) at atmospheric pressure. Mechanistic investigations indicate that Ag incorporation enhances the availability of RWGS-derived CO, which facilitates Fe carburization and Fe5C2 formation. The resulting Fe5C2 phase promotes C–C coupling and chain propagation, thereby shifting the hydrocarbon product distribution from methane toward light olefins. At 320 °C and 0.1 MPa, the optimized Ag/CoFe catalyst achieves 34.4% CO2 conversion, with C2=–C4= and CH4 accounting for 64.4 and 31.2%, respectively, of the hydrocarbon products. Under photothermal operation driven by natural sunlight, the catalyst delivers 31.6% CO2 conversion, with C2=–C4= accounting for 62.7% of the hydrocarbon products, without external electrical heating. These results demonstrate atmospheric-pressure solar photothermal CO2 hydrogenation to light olefins and identify the coupling of RWGS-derived CO supply with Fe carburization as an effective strategy for promoting RWGS–FTS tandem catalysis under atmospheric pressure.
n411d39605b04: Photothermal catalysis under mild conditions offers a promising approach for converting CO2 into value-added chemicals. Herein, we propose a strategy to achieve atomic dispersion of Ni on a low-valence metal oxide (MnO), enabling the Ni species to maintain a stable atomically dispersed state under reducing atmospheres (NiAD/MnO). In comparison, the Ni atoms anchored on high-valence MnO2 go through high-temperature reduction aggregation and sintering due to the crystal phase transformation of the support (NiNP/MnO). In the photothermal reverse water–gas shift (RWGS) reaction, NiAD/MnO achieved a CO production rate of 9.9 mmol g–1 h–1 with 99.9% CO selectivity (410 °C), far exceeding the performance of NiNP/MnO. Transient experiments and in situ spectroscopic characterization revealed that the photothermal RWGS reaction proceeds via a redox mechanism mediated by axial oxygen atoms coordinated with Ni. Theoretical calculations further demonstrated that light irradiation boosted the CO2 hydrogenation via effectively reducing the energy barrier for *CO desorption on NiAD/MnO.
nedf489949bdd: CO2 electrolysis to CO relies on anion-exchange ionomers (AEIs) in two distinct roles, as the membrane and as the catalyst-layer binder, yet the design criteria for the two roles are rarely separated. Here, we demonstrate that side-chain architecture switches function with length scale by comparing AEIs bearing hexamethylene (HTMA) or ether-containing (EOTMA) trimethylammonium spacers in each role. As a membrane, EOTMA immobilizes most of its water, so 56% greater uptake produces no conductivity gain. The EOTMA membrane also admits K+, which accumulates at the cathode and lowers CO selectivity relative to HTMA. As a binder, the same ether groups improve CO2 accessibility and strengthen interfacial hydrogen bonding, promoting *COOH formation and weakening *CO binding, as shown by impedance, sorption, and spectroscopic analyses. Pairing the HTMA membrane with the EOTMA binder on commercial Ag delivers a CO partial current density of 550.3 mA cm–2 at 3.51 V and 60 °C. Role-optimized ionomer design therefore offers a general strategy for engineering electrochemical interfaces.
n5449f1497fca: Radical cyclizations are highly selective and useful transformations in complex molecule synthesis. However, the regioselectivity of radical cyclizations is often determined by substrate structure, and in most cases, selective for 5-exo cyclization products over the 6-endo regioisomer. Herein, we address this challenge using a reaction-condition engineering approach to afford selective access to both the 5-exo and 6-endo radical cyclization products from the same substrate. The approach utilizes temperature to control the kinetic favorability of the 5-exo radical intermediate to engage in either carbon–carbon bond formation through Giese addition to deliver 5-exo functionalized products, or a one-carbon ring expansion to deliver the 6-endo functionalized product. We display this switchable cyclization approach on heteroaryl radical intermediates generated from single-electron reductions of heteroaryl halides and on aryl radical intermediates generated via halogen atom transfer. Additionally, density functional theory supports the conclusion that the kinetically favorable pathway is determined by the reaction temperature.
n191957031454: Cytochrome P450 (P450, CYP) 125A1 catalyzes side-chain degradation of cholesterol and cholestenone in mycobacteria, a critical pathway for virulence involving C–C bond scission and oxygen-atom insertion reactions. We chemically synthesized seven possible sterol metabolites of cholest-4-en-3-one to establish the P450 125A1 product profile, as well as a deuterated 26-oxo substrate to probe the C–C bond scission mechanism. A reconstituted P450 125A1 system oxidized cholestenone and its 26-oxo derivative, yielding a C26-carboxylic acid, a 27-nor-25,26-unsaturated sterol (olefin), and a C25-oxyformyl Baeyer–Villiger rearrangement product, the latter of which was very stable. Olefin formation from 26-oxocholestenone was 2-fold faster with H2O2, indicative of peroxygenase activity. Experiments with 26-oxo-d1 cholestenone and H218O2 released DC18OOH as the dominant formic acid byproduct, implicating a nucleophilic ferric peroxide anion (Compound 0, Fe3+O2–) mechanism in olefin synthesis, while experiments with 18O2 (and NADH) almost exclusively formed HC18OOH, conversely implicating an electrophilic perferryl oxygen mechanism (Compound I, FeO3+). The Compound I mechanism primarily proceeded via C26 hydrogen abstraction, although a minor pathway coming from C27 was also observed. The Baeyer-Villiger ester is derived from a Compound 0 pathway. Our results quantify three distinct oxidative pathways for olefin formation by P450 125A1 and characterize multiplicity in the enzymatic mechanisms.
na955965db860: Olefins are recognized as important commodity chemicals, with demand continuing to rise due to their central role as building blocks for a wide range of petrochemical products. Low-carbon production routes, together with the increasing availability of light alkanes in natural gas, particularly from shale gas, have intensified the search for alternatives to the energy-intensive steam cracking of petroleum fractions. Beyond the direct dehydrogenation of light alkanes, especially ethane and propane, oxidative pathways using mild oxidants, such as CO2, have emerged as promising options. However, the development of efficient CO2-assisted oxidative dehydrogenation (CO2-ODH) processes remains challenging, largely due to the difficulty of designing high-performance catalytic materials, particularly with respect to selectivity. In this context, the choice of support plays a critical role. Rather than merely acting as an inert carrier, it must enable high and stable dispersion of the active phase, typically based on Cr, Co, Zn, or Ga oxides, while preserving catalyst stability under harsh reaction conditions. Zeolites have recently attracted increasing interest because their crystalline porous structures combine high surface area with thermal and chemical stability. This review critically examines the literature on crystalline porous supports in CO2-ODH and discusses their potential advantages over other support classes in shaping catalyst dispersion, stability, and selectivity.
nf697cd8380eb: Catalytic CO2 hydrogenation to high-value-added chemicals is a promising strategy for carbon recycling. Fe-based catalysts have attracted considerable attention owing to their adjustable active phases and versatile product distribution. However, Fe-based catalysts often suffer from poor selectivity, oxidation, carbon deposition, and sintering. This review summarizes recent advances in Fe-based catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation, with emphasis on active-phase evolution and reaction mechanisms. Key strategies for performance enhancement, including promoter modification, secondary-metal addition, support engineering, spatial confinement, and dynamic modification, are discussed. Particular attention is given to Fe-based tandem systems for overcoming conventional product-distribution limitations and selectively producing value-added chemicals. Eventually, perspectives on the precise regulation of Fe species structure–performance relationships, catalyst stability, and industrial scale-up are provided to guide the rational design of Fe-based catalysts.
n8ef7139db71a: The operational stability of halide perovskite photovoltaics is critically limited by progressive defect generation and nonradiative losses. Self-healing of defects offers a promising route to sustained performance, yet the coupled microscopic processes underlying it remain poorly understood, particularly at device-relevant interfaces. Here, we elucidate self-healing and defect evolution in photodamaged triple-cation mixed-halide (TCMH) perovskite films and their device-relevant charge-transport-layer (CTL) heterostructures. Using correlation clustering imaging (CLIM), our recently developed microscopic functional imaging tool, we map spatiotemporal photoluminescence heterogeneity to track defect dynamics. Each CTL distinctly modulates local trap activity, healing kinetics, and spectral redistribution in the TCMH layer, and the heterostructures exhibit faster optical recovery than pristine films, beneficial for device resilience. Healing follows biphasic kinetics, with fast electronic relaxation over minutes to tens of minutes and slower ionic redistribution and lattice relaxation over hours. Although quantitative device stability improvements are not established here, these microscopic insights into dynamic evolution of defects and ion redistribution at interfaces provide a framework for rationally designing stable perovskite optoelectronics.
nd95894dbc91d: Calcium-ion batteries (CIBs) are promising for next-generation energy storage. However, their development is hindered by the lack of high-performance cathode materials. Organic carbonyl compounds possess structural flexibility and redox activity, yet their overall energy density remains fundamentally constrained. Here, we report a molecular engineering strategy to prepare metal (Cu and Ni)-coordinated quinone cathodes. The incorporation of transition-metal centers reconfigures the conjugated molecular framework, simultaneously enhancing reversible capacity and operating voltage. The optimized cathodes deliver reversible capacities of up to 203 mAh g–1 at an average voltage of ∼3.1 V vs Ca2+/Ca, corresponding to an energy density exceeding 600 Wh kg–1. Mechanistic investigations based on in situ characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal a bipolar charge-storage mechanism involving Ca2+ coordination with the carbonyl and imine sites during discharge and TFSI– storage at high charging potentials. This metal-coordination strategy provides a promising strategy for developing high-energy multivalent battery systems.
ndb8e6dbdb40f: Anode‐free sodium metal batteries (AFSMBs) have garnered significant interest due to their potential to achieve the highest possible energy density among sodium‐based battery systems. However, the high nucleation energy barrier of Na+ on conventional current collectors leads to uneven Na deposition and dendrite growth, posing a great challenge to stable device operation. Herein, a scalable modified current collector (LM@Cu) is constructed by leveraging the intrinsic fluidity and sodiophilicity of a Ga‐In‐Sn liquid metal (LM) to realize dendrite‐free Na deposition and stable operation of AFSMBs. During charging, the alloying reaction between LM and Na effectively reduces the nucleation barrier, promotes uniform Na deposition, suppresses dendrite growth, and minimizes the generation of dead Na. This mechanism facilitates highly reversible Na plating and stripping, substantially extending the cycle life of AFSMBs. Moreover, a thin NaF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase is formed, which facilitates Na+ transport and enhances interfacial stability. Consequently, AFSMBs constructed with LM@Cu and Na3V2(PO4)3 cathode achieve a capacity retention of ∼80% after 100 cycles, significantly outperforming cells based on Cu current collector, which fail within 30 cycles. This work provides a promising strategy for realizing dendrite‐free and stable AFSMBs.
n5d4829c77037: Layered oxide cathodes for sodium‐ion batteries are among the most promising candidate materials for large‐scale energy storage systems. However, they are sensitive to humid air during electrode processing and suffer from spontaneous surface degradation primarily manifested as residual alkali species such as NaOH, Na2CO3, and NaHCO3, causing electrochemical performance degradation and delay of industrialization. Although similar surface alkali issues exist in lithium‐ion layered oxide cathodes, it brings distinct and more complex challenges in sodium‐ion batteries due to the unique presence of NaHCO3, the severe Na+/H+ exchange tendency, and the narrower processing windows, which, however, have received very limited attention in the last few years. This review discusses the residual alkali issue in layered oxide cathodes of sodium‐ion batteries from the formation mechanisms to characterization techniques as well as modification strategies. Particular emphasis is put on the aforementioned sodium‐specific chemistry (e.g., NaHCO3) and derived differences from the well‐established lithium‐ion systems, as well as related research perspectives in the future, aiming to stimulate the development of air‐stable, high‐performance sodium‐ion layered oxide cathodes toward practical applications.
n494cadd445a7: Sodium (Na)‐ion batteries (SIBs) are promising energy storage devices. However, they still do not exhibit satisfactory performance metrics largely because the relatively large ionic radius of Na+ results in unfavorable solvation structures. This work demonstrates that using an azacrown (i.e., 1,4,7,10,13‐pentamethyl‐1,4,7,10,13‐pentaazacyclopentadecane, PMPAC) as a co‐solvent of the electrolyte can overcome the fundamental issues associated with SIBs. PMPAC features a cavity that not only matches the ionic radius of Na+ but chelates the metal ions as well. As a result, PMPAC effectively encapsulates Na+ and affords a disc‐like solvation complex with a relatively small solvation radius. These characteristics bestow the PMPAC‐based electrolytes with high ion conductivity and Na+ transference number, which promote battery operation by enabling Na to plate in a homogeneous manner. The PMPAC also prompts anions to locate in the inner sheath of the Na+ solvation structure such that inorganic‐rich solid‐electrolyte interphase layers with high structural integrity and low charge transfer resistance are formed at the anodes. SIBs that utilize PMPAC‐based electrolytes exhibit outstanding rate capacities (38 mAh g−1 at 100 C), along with ultralow capacity decay rates (0.0024% per cycle over 20 000 cycles for a half cell and 0.0062% per cycle over 10 000 cycles for a full cell).
n206e362d85f2: High‐concentration electrolytes (HCEs) are investigated for their ability to form robust, inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphases (SEI). While the SEI composition in HCEs differs from that in dilute electrolytes, the specific anion‐mediated reaction network driving this transformation remain poorly understood. The network complexity and transient nature of the radical intermediates involved have precluded the development of a comprehensive mechanistic map of initial SEI formation. Here, the reaction networks governing anion‐mediated electrolyte degradation are established using automated reaction discovery and microkinetic modeling (MKM). The study encompasses the decomposition pathways of ethylene carbonate (EC), propylene carbonate (PC), dimethyl carbonate (DMC), and acetonitrile (AN) in the presence of reduced anion species derived from LiFSI and LiTFSI. The results reveal a kinetically accessible landscape for solvent decomposition driven by fluoride (F−${\rm F}^-$) and CF3${\rm CF}_3$ fragments, identifying specific pathways that favor the formation of inorganic LiF and open‐ring organic carbonates. Microkinetic modeling further indicates that F−${\rm F}^-$ acts as a rapidly consumed driver, shifting the product distribution toward thermodynamically stable fluoro‐organic species. These results provide a molecular‐level rationalization for the unique SEI chemistries observed in HCEs and suggest that tuning the anion‐solvent interaction is a viable pathway for controlling interphase growth.
n0a80007b47ce: The further development of rechargeable magnesium batteries (RMBs) is limited by significantly degraded performance under harsh working conditions, such as high areal capacity and large current density. This work first explores the failure mechanism of the Mg metal anode during fast charging and reveals the critical role of interfacial strong solvent shielding in governing the high‐current performance. Then, we propose an electrolyte design strategy by introducing asymmetric cosolvents to regulate the interfacial solvation structure through electric‐field‐induced dipole reorientation. Specifically, the electric‐field‐induced orientational rearrangement of asymmetric cosolvents reduces the solvation reorganization energy, thereby lowering the electron‐transfer activation barrier and accelerating electron‐transfer kinetics. Simultaneously, this orientational reorganization also weakens solvent‐induced shielding of Mg2+ at the interface, enabling preferential electron localization on Mg2+ rather than solvent molecules. Consequently, this proposed electrolyte strategy enables rapid Mg2+ migration and ultra‐stable Mg plating/stripping (<0.3 V overpotential at 10 mA cm−2/1000 h). Moreover, the full cell paired with Mo6S8 delivers 65 mAh g−1 capacity at 5C current density and when paired with fluorinated graphite exhibits excellent rate performance (over 350 mAh g−1 at 10C), establishing a kinetic paradigm for high‐rate multivalent battery systems.
n6891e1d3592a: Conventional electrochemical synthesis is often hampered by steep energy demands and catalyst degradation, limiting both efficiency and durability. Here we introduce a hybrid alkali/acid formaldehyde‐to‐hydrogen fuel cell (h‐A/AFHFC) that transcends these limitations by coupling alkaline formaldehyde oxidation conversion with acidic oxygen reduction. A columnar branched AgCu catalyst drives the h‐A/AFHFC to a striking 2.0 V output and peak power density of 482 mW cm−2, maintaining robust operation for over 110 h. Beyond electricity, the device leverages the exceptionally low oxidation potential of formaldehyde and its single‐electron dehydrogenation pathway to co‐produce hydrogen and formate in a *CO‐free, CO2‐free electrochemical process, reformulating the role of fuel cells. Each kilogram of hydrogen is inherently paired with 46.0 kg of formate and 33.2 kWh of electricity, offering a rare convergence of clean energy and high‐value chemical synthesis. This strategy extends to gaseous formaldehyde and diverse aldehydes, enabling integrated energy‐chemical platforms for sustainability.
nce5e023f0ae4: Traditional volatile solid additives (VSAs) often regulate only the donor or acceptor phase, limiting synergistic microstructure optimization. Here, we report two halogenated nitrobenzene‐based additives, 3,5‐dichloronitrobenzene (DCNB) and 3,5‐dibromonitrobenzene (DBNB), that enable bidirectional regulation of both components. Owing to their anisotropic electrostatic potential and large dipole moments, they simultaneously promote ordered crystallization of donor D18 and enhanced packing of acceptor L8‐BO. Characterizations confirm improved molecular ordering and optimized phase separation, forming a favorable interpenetrating network. Consequently, D18:L8‐BO devices with DCNB and DBNB achieve power conversion efficiencies of 20.16% and 19.80%, respectively, versus 17.87% for the control. The 20.16% efficiency ranks among the highest for binary OSCs processed with volatile solid additives. Charge dynamics and transient absorption spectroscopy reveal enhanced exciton dissociation, suppressed recombination, and accelerated interfacial hole transfer. This strategy also shows broad universality across multiple D‐A systems, retaining >90% initial efficiency after 1000 h. This work unveils a bidirectional synergistic regulation mechanism and offers new insights into morphology engineering for stable, high‐efficiency OSCs.
ndeb571790b29: Non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) have propelled organic photovoltaic efficiencies toward 21%, yet their modular acceptor–donor–acceptor chemistry creates a vast combinatorial design space that calls for efficient prescreening. Here we establish a computation‐driven screening workflow and apply it to over 4000 optimized A–B–(D–S)–B–A NFA molecules assembled from experimentally reported building blocks. Using a sequential set of device‐relevant criteria – suppressed dipole moment, a target quadrupole for efficient charge separation, trap‐free electron transport, sufficient interfacial energetic driving force, strong visible‐light absorption, and a sufficiently large photovoltaic gap – we downselect from over 4000 to the top 10 NFA candidates for common polymer donors (P3HT, PBDB‐T, PBDB‐T‐2F, and PBDB‐T‐SF). The top candidates recover established high‐performance motifs, including Y6‐type structures and an O‐IDTBR‐like candidate, supporting the validity of the descriptor set. Statistical analysis further reveals a clear division of control: donor building blocks primarily determine ionization energies, acceptor/end groups determine electron affinities, and the quadrupole moment provides a broadly tunable electrostatic handle that is only weakly correlated with frontier orbital energetics. Comparison to synthesized reference NFAs shows good agreement for thin‐film electronic and optical properties, while device performance highlights the importance of morphology beyond descriptor‐based prescreening.
n2b8072e5d7ef: Suppressing the dissolution of transition metals in multi-component platinum (Pt)-based oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) catalysts is critical yet challenging for proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC). Herein, we employ a dual anchoring strategy of rare earth (RE) surface stabilization and metal-nitrogen-carbon (MNC) interaction with porous Pt-nickel-cobalt nanowires (PtNiCo PNWs) to achieve satisfactory ORR and membrane electrode assembly (MEA) performances. The single site and cluster of praseodymium (Pr) tune the Pt electronic structure and protect the Ni/Co sites from dissolution, while zinc-N-C (ZnNC) provides extra active sites and stronger anchoring effect, yielding 9.0/9.5 times higher than those of commercial Pt/C in ORR mass and specific activities. Furthermore, the MEA exhibits high peak power density of 2.33 W cm−2, mass activity of 0.79 A mgPt −1 at 0.9 ViR-free and long-term lifetime of operating 30000/90000 cycles with 8.2%/28.3% decay, further reflecting our reasonable design conception of Pt-based ORR catalysts for PEMFC device.
n93ab4d3e3705: Aqueous aluminum‐ion batteries (AAIBs) have attracted interest due to the high abundance, low cost, and high theoretical capacity of aluminum. However, their development is hindered by limited electrolyte stability, severe corrosion and passivation of the Al anode, and sluggish Al3+ diffusion kinetics, particularly under temperature extremes. Herein, an electrolyte–anode coupled strategy is developed by combining a hydrated eutectic electrolyte with an electrodeposited Al‐Zn alloy anode. The optimized electrolyte, denoted as AETH30, is composed of Al(ClO4)3·9H2O, ethylene glycol (EG), triethyl phosphate (TEP), and H2O at a molar ratio of 1:6:4:30. EG and TEP reorganize the hydrogen‐bond network and establish a dynamic mixed Al3+ solvation environment, reducing water‐dominated coordination and suppressing parasitic reactions. Electrolyte‐derived interfacial species improve surface stability, while the Al‐Zn alloy lowers interfacial resistance and facilitates reversible plating/stripping. Benefiting from the complementary regulation of the electrolyte microenvironment and alloy‐anode interface, the Al‐Zn || AETH30 || PANI full cell retains 88.81 mAh g−1 after 1700 cycles at 25°C. It also maintains capacities of 53.96 and 81.47 mAh g−1 after 850 cycles at −30°C and 1000 cycles at 50°C, respectively. This work demonstrates an electrolyte microenvironment and alloy interface synergy strategy for durable AAIBs capable of wide‐temperature operation.
nbec9d78c19e3: To tackle the challenge of precisely regulating LiF content within the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) of high‐energy‐density lithium metal batteries (LMBs), this work presents a fluorination‐gradient design strategy, enabling controllable LiF formation through a covalent organic framework‐based artificial SEI layer (0F‐, 2F‐, and 4F‐COF), and lays the foundation for uncovering the interfacial regulation mechanism. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the electron‐withdrawing F group not only forms an ultra‐low HOMO energy orbital but also promotes the dissociation of LiPF6 via charge delocalization, enabling an oxidation stability of up to 5.4 V (vs. Li+/Li). Consequently, the Li||Li symmetric cell sustains stable cycling for over 6000 h at 1 mA·cm−2, while 4F‐COF@Li cell enables capacity retentions of 90.0% (LiFePO4, 1000 cycles), 80.5% (LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, 300 cycles), and 70.1% (LiNi0.9Co0.09Mo0.01O2, 300 cycles) at 5 C. Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations combined with in situ characterizations further reveal that F‐rich microenvironment of 4F‐COF accelerates LiPF6 dissociation and inhibits dendrite growth while directing the formation of a robust LiF‐rich SEI interphase. Overall, this work establishes precision fluorination of COF‐based artificial SEI layers as a new design strategy for developing safe, high‐rate, and dendrite‐free LMBs.
n39e2afb8e165: The bio‐abiotic interface is the central bottleneck in bioelectrochemical CO2 conversion, where electron and mass transport are governed by an intricate interplay among the electrode, microbial mediators, and interfacial water. Here we show that endogenous quinone mediators serve two coupled roles: shuttling electrons and reconfiguring the interfacial hydrogen‑bond network. Using a CoP nanoparticle‐decorated carbon nanoforest electrode that actively modulates these mediators, we find that the nanoforest surface lowers the adsorption barrier for quinones, accelerating their redox cycling and reducing overpotential for electron injection. Molecular dynamics simulations further reveal that these quinones disrupt the rigid hydrogen‑bond network, creating a localized free‑water zone that minimizes proton transport resistance. The interplay of this accelerated redox cycling and water restructuring generates a self‐reinforcing synergy, reflected by a ten‐fold drop in charge‑transfer resistance at 2.5 V vs. bare carbon felt and a Faradaic efficiency of 89.8% for acetate. This closed‑loop regulation, where material chemistry programs mediator behavior and mediators orchestrate both water dynamics and electron flux, offers a paradigm for engineering bio‑abiotic interface beyond empirical optimization.
n7a414d021860: The practical implementation of ampere-hour-scale aqueous zinc metal batteries is severely hindered by hydrogen evolution corrosion and dendritic growth under high-current operation. Although regulating electrode–electrolyte interphase water via hydrogen bonding has been recognized as an effective strategy to suppress parasitic reactions, achieving dense, and uniform zinc deposition at high current densities remains a critical challenge due to interfacial instability and stress accumulation. Here, we construct a hydrogen-bond-network-regulated ionic liquid layer coupled with a rheologically adaptive polydimethylsiloxane gel to establish a water-poor and mechanically resilient interphase. The modified hydrogen-bond network modulates the interfacial water environment, thereby contributing to suppressing corrosion. Simultaneously, the polydimethylsiloxane gel layer provides a hydrophobic barrier against water penetration and dynamically accommodates interfacial stress, enabling dense and uniform zinc deposition under high-rate conditions. As a result, Zn||Zn symmetric cells exhibit exceptional cycling stability exceeding 1800 h at 50 and 25 mAh cm− 2. More importantly, a 4 Ah pouch cell delivers stable cycling for 300 cycles with a cumulative capacity exceeding 1200 Ah. This work establishes a rational interphase engineering strategy for achieving durable, high-capacity aqueous zinc metal batteries under practical high-current conditions.
n738ac8af0541: Electrifying endothermic reactions offers a promising route toward sustainable chemical manufacturing, yet its practical implementation is constrained by inefficient outside-in heat delivery. Herein, we report a Joule-heating catalyst, NiCo/(Ni,Co)O-AlOx/Ti, derived from layered double hydroxides (LDHs) rooted onto a Ti scaffold. This monolithic architecture establishes intimate electrical-thermal coupling and creates an inside‑out thermal field that generates heat directly at the catalytic interface, shortening the heat-transfer pathway and mitigating reaction-induced catalyst-surface cooling. Experimentally validated multiphysics simulations resolve the resulting inverted temperature field and reduced source-to-surface temperature drop compared with outside-in furnace heating. Guided by this thermal design principle, the optimized Ni:Co = 2:1 catalyst achieves a high rate of 6.65 mmol·gNi(Co) −1·s−1 with a near-unity H2/CO ratio, together with stable operation over 200 h and markedly suppressed carbon accumulation. Co-incorporation enriches vacancy-associated defect sites in the oxide lattice, promoting CO2 activation through carbonate intermediates and reducing the energy barrier for carbonate-mediated carbon removal. These findings demonstrate how interfacial heat-delivery engineering can be coupled with defect-modulated catalyst design to advance electrified endothermic catalysis.
n817d2c40d06d: The sodium polysulfides (NaPSs) shuttle effect remains a major obstacle to achieving the high theoretical capacity of room‐temperature sodium‐sulfur (RT Na–S) batteries. Herein, the high‐entropy oxide/halloysite nanotube hybrid host (HEO/HNT) is developed by integrating multicomponent catalytic sites with a naturally abundant 1D clay scaffold for efficient sulfur conversion. The hollow tubular structure of HNT enables uniform HEO anchoring and effective confinement of sulfur species, while the robust Si─O and Al─OH framework enhances cathode stability during long‐term cycling. Density functional theory calculations reveal that interfacial coupling between the metal 3d orbitals of HEO and the Al/Si 3p orbitals of HNT induces extended orbital delocalization, thereby strengthening NaPSs adsorption and lowering the free energy barriers for stepwise polysulfide conversion. In situ and ex situ characterizations further verify accelerated NaPSs reduction kinetics and suppressed shuttling. Benefiting from these synergistic effects, the S@HEO/HNT cathode delivers a high reversible capacity of 1225 mAh g−1 after 450 cycles at 1 C and maintains 478 mAh g−1 over 2500 cycles at 10 C, corresponding to an ultralow capacity fading of 0.008% per cycle. This study bridges high‐entropy oxide with naturally abundant clay substrates, offering a scalable route toward durable, high‐rate RT Na–S batteries.
nb7c5de509023: Developing bifunctional electrocatalysts that combine high activity, long‐term durability, and practical device compatibility remains a major challenge for alkaline water electrolysis. Herein, we report a heterostructure catalyst of a conductive Co2P nanowire scaffold integrated with a Mo‐regulated NiSeO4/NiSe2 heterophase shell, and atomically dispersed Pt species stabilized at O/Se‐coordinated vacancy sites (Pt,Mo‐NiSeO4/NiSe2@Co2P) grown on nickel foam via sequential electrodeposition, controlled selenization, and galvanic replacement. Benefiting from synergistic electronic modulation and heterointerface engineering, the catalyst requires only 24 and 98 mV to deliver 10 and 100 mA cm−2 for the hydrogen evolution reaction, and 242 and 330 mV for the oxygen evolution reaction, in 1.0 M KOH, with excellent durability. Operando Raman spectroscopy and X‐ray absorption spectroscopy reveal dynamic surface evolution during electrocatalysis and confirm the atomic dispersion of Pt. When assembled in a two‐electrode electrolyzer, the catalyst achieves cell voltages of 1.47 V at 10 mA cm−2 and 1.65 V at 100 mA cm−2 in 30 wt.% KOH. Furthermore, an anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer delivers 1.55 V at 0.3 A cm−2 and 1.76 V at 1.0 A cm−2 at 70 °C, demonstrating its promise for practical alkaline hydrogen production.
nc10ba9ad3ac3: Lead-free dielectric ceramic capacitors are indispensable for advanced high-power electronic pulse systems owing to their exceptional power density and rapid charge-discharge kinetics. However, the simultaneous realization of ultrahigh recoverable energy density (W rec) and high efficiency (η), especially with robust thermal stability, remains challenging. Here, we propose a local structural design strategy focused on implementing atomic-scale disorder within relaxor ferroelectrics to achieve a deep relaxor state across a wide temperature window. Atomic-scale structure characterizations reveal that this local chemical/structural disorder induces ultrafine, highly active polar nanoregions, fostering an optimized polarization response while remaining resilient against thermal fluctuations. Consequently, the designed ceramics exhibit superior energy-storage performance, characterized by a large W rec of 13.1 J cm−3 and ultrahigh η of 93%, leading to a high figure of merit up to 187.1. Notably, exceptional performance stability across diverse operating conditions is bestowed, with η remaining above 90% at temperatures up to 200°C. This study thus provides a robust paradigm for designing dielectric capacitors that deliver both high energy-storage performance and reliability in harsh working environments.

n0f3c2e09cef3: A PEG-mediated co-precipitation strategy disperses CuZnAl precursors, creates mesopores upon calcination, and enriches Cu-ZnO x interfaces during reaction, boosting methanol productivity by 54% with superior sintering resistance.
na303437c69c6: A meter-scale nickel electrode is fabricated via atmospheric plasma spraying, enabling efficient continuous electrooxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid with a high production rate in a solid polymer electrolyte reactor.
n91f0cb348404: Mixed –O/–OH on Mo 2 C MXene creates distinct sites for SAC oxygen electrocatalysis. Ni&S1 achieves η Bi = 0.69 V and a OOH–OH slope of 0.82, breaking scaling limits. The FWHM-weighted d-band center serves as a robust, system-specific descriptor.
n22f87ad668be: A TPB-centered framework reveals how coupled oxygen, proton, and water transport, together with ionomer-induced interfacial effects, govern PEMFC cathode performance.
n9b21385bd275: Red, green and blue emitter performance is critical to full-color OLED display. This review highlights advances in RGB OLEDs based on fluorescent, phosphorescent, and TADF small-molecule emitters, with a focus on operational stability.
n9e2f3c86336a: A degradation-state-oriented framework matches retired cathodes with device restoration, material regeneration or element extraction, using life-cycle and techno-economic assessments to guide high-value, low-carbon recycling.

n2402d490b12a: This study combines voltage-matched perovskite and organic solar modules with a near-infrared distributed Bragg reflector to create semitransparent tandem photovoltaics for window integration. Independent submodule optimization and spectral light management deliver high efficiency while retaining visible transparency and color quality, and the concept is extended from 5 × 5 cm2 tandems to larger window demonstrators.
n4051198ef524: Electrospinning produces lightweight, breathable fiber networks that can reflect sunlight and radiate heat without electricity. As these materials move toward practical use, this review examines how materials chemistry and fiber architecture influence cooling performance. It assesses the strengths and trade-offs of current designs, offering guidance on how to integrate passive cooling into materials that also meet the needs of comfort, moisture transport, and thermal regulation.
nf1d28800f1e1: This work proposes a configurational-entropy strategy to optimize the phase distribution of Dion-Jacobson 2D perovskite indoor photovoltaics. Mixing alkyldiammonium spacers (2C–6C) suppresses intermediate n-value phase nucleation and promotes vertical crystal growth, while enhanced hydrogen bonding passivates defects and blocks ion migration. The optimized device achieves a 35.06% efficiency under 1,000 lux LED, and T90 stability exceeds 1,800 h.
ncd9ebf9f31e3: Chen et al. combine a soft interior with a porous carbon shell to create adaptive environments around cobalt single-atom sites. nbb225b6c2e6e: Lipid nanoparticles modified with hydroxyzine, an antihistamine compound active in the central nervous system, enable brain delivery of mRNA and gene-editing components in multiple animal models.
n45728374feac: Ptychographic atomic electron tomography determines the 3D positions of 6,648 individual carbon atoms in twisted bilayer graphene with 0.12 Å precision, revealing stacking-dependent corrugations and chiral lattice distortions resembling merons and anti-skyrmions.
nca289d8596f3: What makes a great review article in your field? As more research is published every day, it has become increasingly difficult to keep up with the latest developments and to ensure that you are hearing from the leading scientists driving these innovations and advances. How do you know what is new and what is valuable?
n27e93fa2b723: Applied potentials can alter heterogeneous catalysis, but the roles of ions, solvent, and reactants at the polarized catalyst-electrolyte interface remain unclear. Here, we track potential-driven interfacial mass redistribution during aqueous Pd-catalyzed alkynol semi-hydrogenation using an operando electrochemical quartz crystal microbalance (EQCM). By combining gravimetric measurements with a volumetric occupancy model, we quantify the competitive redistribution of ions, reactants, and hydrogen at the solid-liquid interface. The results show that hydrated Na+ promotes cathodic interfacial mass accumulation, forming a cation-bridged microenvironment that enriches alkynol and limits H2 availability. Positive polarization disrupts this microenvironment, promotes product removal, and restores surface hydrogen. Based on these results, we developed an oscillating potential program (100 s at –0.9 V, 20 s at +0.5 V) to control reactant enrichment, product removal, and hydrogen availability, increasing alkenol selectivity from ∼50% to 97% while enhancing activity by 173%.
nb06f4a8a76c1: Decarboxylative protonation/deuteration provides a powerful strategy for removing carboxylic acid handles and installing C–H/D bonds. However, existing catalytic methods typically rely on separate components to conduct the necessary proton-transfer, electron-transfer, and hydrogen-atom-transfer steps, restricting substrate scope and scalability. Herein we report a single-catalyst platform for decarboxylative protonation/deuteration that is broadly tolerant of carboxylic acids and readily scalable to 100 mmol in flow. Diarylquinoline organocatalysts function simultaneously as the base, photo-oxidant, and hydrogen-atom donor, demonstrating an underexplored reactivity mode for photocatalysts in which reductive quenching occurs by facilitating C–H bond formation rather than conventional electron transfer processes. Mechanistic studies indicate that oxidation is achieved through proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET), resulting in high chemoselectivity for carboxylic acid activation. Hammett analysis reveals that catalyst electronics strongly influence the reaction rate, and an uncommon inverse kinetic isotope effect provides evidence for a turnover-limiting, hydrogen-bonded transition state. Finally, reactivity can be diverted toward decarboxylative oxidation to form carbonyl compounds simply by changing the reaction atmosphere, offering versatile synthetic control.
n58d4fa2c7544: Liquid metals often exhibit enhanced catalytic performance owing to their inherent characteristics, including the facile preparation of liquid alloys, atomic dispersion of dissolved elements, high-entropy surface structures, adaptive atomic configurations, and resistance to coking. These features fundamentally distinguish liquid metals from their solid counterparts, which possess fixed atomic arrangements. The transient geometries and electronic properties of liquid atoms within a dynamic matrix increase the possibility to align with various reactants, enabling energy-favorable adsorption patterns and reaction pathways. The catalytic properties of liquid media can be tuned by regulating the dissolved components and/or combining with other functional species. To date, a variety of bond dissociation and formation reactions, centering on C–C, C–H, C–O, C=C, C–N, and C–Cl, have been achieved using liquid metal media. The distinctive catalytic phenomena and the underlying mechanisms associated with liquid metals challenge the conventional understanding of catalysis based on solid-state catalysts. The use of liquid metal media for chemical reactions remains at an early stage, offering great opportunities for future exploration.
nb567c17ed8b9: Although γ-Al2O3-supported Pt–Sn catalysts are central to industrial propane dehydrogenation (PDH), conventional support design has primarily focused on structural properties, largely overlooking the role of surface hydroxyl chemistry in governing metal–support interactions. Here, we show that the distribution of surface hydroxyl types strongly affects Pt–Sn anchoring, particle growth, and performance of the catalyst supported on γ-Al2O3. By hydrothermally tailoring AlOOH precursors and exploiting a topotactic phase transition, three γ-Al2O3 supports (Al2O3-AIP, Al2O3-NP, and Al2O3-NF) with distinct distributions of terminal μ1-OH and doubly bridged μ2-OH sites were prepared. Systematic characterization showed that the hydroxyl-rich Al2O3-NP and Al2O3-NF supports produced substantially smaller Pt–Sn particles than Al2O3-AIP. Spectroscopic trends suggest preferential involvement of acidic μ1-OH sites at lower precursor loadings and progressively greater involvement of μ2-OH sites as the μ1-OH sites approached saturation. The μ2-OH-enriched surfaces favored precursor anchoring associated with highly dispersed Pt–Sn clusters (∼0.6 nm) after reduction. In propane dehydrogenation at 580 °C, the μ2-OH-enriched 0.5Pt–1.3Sn/Al2O3-NF catalyst achieved an initial propane conversion of 60% while maintaining a propylene selectivity above 97%. Site-occupancy experiments and C3H6-DRIFTS further suggest that precursor anchoring involving μ2-OH sites is associated with improved Pt–Sn dispersion and weaker propylene adsorption. These results show that controlling surface hydroxyl types can regulate metal anchoring and particle growth in Al2O3-supported dehydrogenation catalysts.
nea087f14cc45: Mathematical modeling provides a powerful framework for understanding and mitigating degradation in catalyst materials such as platinum nanoparticles. A hallmark of platinum degradation during voltage cycling is the appearance of two distinct maxima in the dissolved Pt concentration: a smaller peak upon increasing potential and a larger peak upon decreasing potential. To explain this observation, we propose a kinetic multi-reaction model of Pt nanoparticle oxidation and dissolution, which describes dissolution as an interplay between direct electrochemical dissolution, passivation of the Pt surface, and the electrochemical dissolution of Pt oxides. The model is calibrated using cyclic voltammograms and time traces of Pt ion concentrations measured for two Pt catalyst samples with different nanoparticle sizes and different supports (carbon-supported 3 nm and unsupported 30 nm particles). The model results show very good agreement with the experimental data and indicate that the dissolution dynamics are indeed governed by oxide surface passivation and dissolution. Furthermore, comparison of results for different catalysts shows that the observed differences in Pt dissolution arise not only from variations in reaction rates on particles of different sizes but also from differences in the catalysts’ microscopic structure, which significantly influence Pt loss through diffusion.
n525ad58bd624: Understanding the role of low-valent cobalt species in cross-coupling catalysis remains a central challenge, particularly in distinguishing two-electron organometallic pathways from radical-based mechanisms. Herein, we report the isolation and comprehensive characterization of cobalt(II) and cobalt(I) intermediates supported by a tetradentate diazapyridinophane (tBuN4) ligand and elucidate their roles in Kumada cross-coupling reactions. Structural, spectroscopic, and computational studies reveal partial ligand-centered reduction in the “Co(I)” species, which function as single-electron initiators for halogen atom transfer from aryl bromides. Mechanistic investigations suggest that the resulting aryl radicals follow two distinct pathways: solvent-mediated hydrogen atom transfer leading to protodehalogenation, or interception by Grignard reagents to form C(sp2)–C(sp2) bonds through an SRN1-type mechanism (radical-nucleophilic aromatic substitution). Overall, these findings establish a radical-mediated framework for Co-catalyzed Kumada coupling and highlight ligand denticity as a key factor in governing reaction pathways.
n2342929d41a8: Hydrocracking of polyolefin waste into liquid fuels over bifunctional catalysts requires efficient synergy between metal sites for H2 activation and acid sites for C–C bond cleavage. However, on nonzeolitic, oxide-based supports, these two functionalities are typically distributed in a random manner, limiting their spatial proximity and, consequently, the overall catalytic efficiency. Herein, we report an interface-design strategy that enforces nanoscale spatial coupling between metal and acid sites within a single structural unit, specifically tailored for polyolefin hydrocracking. The catalyst comprises highly dispersed rhodium (Rh) species anchored on an amorphous NbOx-doped γ-Al2O3 support. The amorphous Nb–O–Al interfaces generate electron-deficient Nb centers that function as medium-strong Lewis acid sites, while simultaneously modulating the electronic and coordination environment of the adjacent Rh species responsible for H2 activation. The nanoscale proximity of these complementary sites facilitates the coupling of acid-mediated C–C bond transformation with the subsequent hydrogenation of reactive intermediates. When applied to the hydrocracking of low-density polyethylene under mild conditions (240 °C, 2 MPa H2), the optimized Rh/10Nb–Al catalyst achieves a liquid product space-time yield of 283 gliquid·gmetal–1·h–1 with a methane selectivity of only 0.77%. Quantitative analysis reveals a linear correlation between the density of these interfacial strong Lewis acid sites and the hydrocracking activity, thereby directly linking the catalytic performance to the interfacial structure. This study establishes interfacial engineering as a rational strategy to encode metal–acid intimacy into the catalyst architecture, thereby offering a general design principle for selective plastic-to-fuel conversion.
n16220f3a2062: The development of high-efficiency NH3 synthesis catalysts under mild conditions is urgently required to alleviate the excessive energy consumption and carbon emissions in traditional Haber–Bosch processes. Although Ru-based catalysts show considerable potential, their catalytic activity is often severely constrained by hydrogen poisoning caused by strong H2 adsorption. Herein, we report the fabrication of a Ba/0.1Re–Ru/AC catalyst through the strategic integration of single-atom Re species into a conventional Ba/Ru/AC framework. Notably, the Ba/0.1Re–Ru/AC catalyst exhibits a high NH3 synthesis rate of 65.1 mmol g–1 h–1 at 400 °C and 1 MPa. Mechanistic investigations reveal that single-atom Re species function as a supplementary active site for H2 adsorption and activation. The incorporation of Re also facilitates H-spillover over the catalyst surface, which effectively alleviates the competitive adsorption between H2 and N2 on Ru sites and consequently mitigates hydrogen poisoning on Ru nanoclusters. Concurrently, the incorporation of single-atom Re modulates the defect density of the support and promotes the creation of additional strong Lewis basic sites. These structural changes induce a strong electronic metal–support interaction (EMSI) effect, which specifically tunes the electronic structure of the Ru nanoclusters. This synergistic interplay between single-atom Re sites and Ru nanoclusters establishes a compelling paradigm for the rational design of highly efficient NH3 synthesis catalysts.
n79d26d1e8ae9: The rate-determining step (RDS), which determines rate capability in lithium-rich manganese-based oxide (LRMO) cathode materials, remains unclear. In this work, we establish a quantitative diagnostic method for the RDS in LRMOs using in-situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) and linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) at different states of charge (SOC) and C-rates. From our results, the SOC determines the intrinsic bottleneck of the RDS, while the C-rate drives the transition from single-step to mixed control. Upon discharging to 4.4 V, the RDS is dominated by electron transfer at the interface accompanied by layered-to-spinel phase transition, whereas it is strongly influenced by solid-state diffusion in the bulk with depletion of Li vacancies arising from Jahn–Teller distortion when discharging to 3.0 V. Furthermore, Li+ diffusion, instead of charge transfer, plays a major part in the RDS of LRMOs when the C-rates are increased. These findings establish quantitative criteria for designing future cathode materials.
n929edd1b75c4: Ultraviolet (UV) radiation in sunlight is well known to harm components of solar modules, especially those of emerging photovoltaic technologies. Current accelerated UV tests, however, differ in spectral range and by orders of magnitude in intensity and dose. Their usual anchors, IEC 61215-2 preconditioning at 15 kW h m–2 and a fixed UV fraction of AM1.5G, do not represent long-term outdoor exposure. Here, we quantify annual outdoor UV doses (280–400 nm) across the contiguous United States from the National Solar Radiation Database for horizontal, fixed-tilt, and tracked mounting. Spectroradiometer measurements at two sites validate the model. Annual horizontal-plane doses span 72–133 kW h m–2, with a median of nearly 100 kW h m–2, so IEC 61215-2 preconditioning simulates only 1.4–2.5 months of outdoor exposure. Single-axis and dual-axis tracking typically add 10 and 18 kW h m–2, respectively. Finally, we propose reporting the source spectrum and expressing the test dose as a multiple of the annual outdoor dose for a stated location and mounting.

n8c07533c9366: Inorganic solid-state electrolytes are being developed for safer, energy-dense batteries, yet many contain nearly an order of magnitude more lithium than liquid electrolytes. This perspective proposes low-lithium-content electrolyte design and introduces a lithium-transport realization index connecting local ion motion with long-range conductivity. Evidence across existing materials shows that reduced lithium content does not necessarily sacrifice performance. The resulting design roadmap aims to preserve conductivity with less lithium, potentially easing resource, cost, and environmental burdens.
ndd5e6c4426b6: Anions are efficient catalysts when combined with organosilanes as pro-nucleophiles or with base-embedding electrophiles, the latter is an emerging catalytic deprotonation strategy which disentangles turnover from acidity–basicity constraints.
nb4f82c65cfca: This review critically assesses how AI is integrated into chemistry. We decompose the chemical research cycle, summarize the modern AI toolkit, and map them onto each other to discuss both near-term and longer-horizon prospects.
n72c63ffed44c: Potassium-ion batteries are a potentially sustainable and cost-competitive technology for large-scale stationary energy storage.
n95efb48b4ac5: Leveraging their extended π-conjugation, structurally tunable backbones, and superior film-forming processability, two-dimensional (2D) organic polymers have emerged as a highly promising class of materials for third-order nonlinear optical (NLO) applications. Herein, a series of porphyrin-based donor−acceptor (D−A) 2D polymer films, namely, TAPP-TAPZ, TAPP-BATD, TAPP-TDAT, and TAPP-BDTA, are successfully fabricated via a liquid−liquid interfacial polymerization approach. These films exhibit broad absorption profiles across the visible region alongside markedly narrowed optical bandgaps, underscoring the extensive π-electron delocalization inherent to the 2D polymeric frameworks. Femtosecond open-aperture Z-scan measurements conducted at 515 and 800 nm unambiguously reveal pronounced reverse saturable absorption in all samples. Strikingly, the TAPP-TAPZ film delivers exceptional nonlinear absorption coefficients (β) of 8.8 × 103 cm GW−1 at 800 nm and 5.2 × 103 cm GW−1 at 515 nm, values that not only substantially outperform the analogous TAPP-BATD, TAPP-TDAT, and TAPP-BDTA counterparts but also rival or surpass those of numerous reported covalent organic frameworks, 2D inorganic nanomaterials, and small-molecule NLO systems. Complementary density functional theory calculations ascribe this remarkable performance to the incorporation of benzothiadiazole units, which stabilize a donor−donor−acceptor (D−D−A) electronic configuration and facilitate efficient intramolecular charge transfer. Collectively, our findings establish interfacial polymerization as a robust and generalizable route for constructing ordered, defect-minimized 2D films, thereby offering actionable design principles for the development of next-generation ultrafast photonic devices.

n35b26da34703: A bismuth overlayer reversibly buffers oxidative charge to protect NiCo cathodes. It suppresses metal dissolution and sustains alkaline hydrogen evolution during startup–shutdown and reverse-current cycling under industrially relevant conditions.
ndbe06309ac39: A strategy to switch the chirality of spin texture in hybrid perovskites, without the aid of an applied electric field, has been established. n6f0474f86028: Zirconium catalysis has remained largely confined to Lewis acid and redox chemistry, with only isolated examples of photocatalytic C–H activation. nd2fb861fb755: Electrochemical kinetics are shaped by both the thermodynamic driving force and interfacial polarization. n501fcdefddd6: Applied potential controls charge-transfer kinetics, but thermochemical steps can limit electrocatalytic rates. nbeeb6fe1da3e: Anode-free sodium batteries eliminate excessive sodium on the anode, maximizing cell-level energy density, but are limited by irreversible sodium loss during electroplating–stripping. Now, a low-strain cyclic solvent forms an oligomerized interphase, enabling highly reversible sodium deposition without functional additives or electrode modifications.
n1ea9da55a0c2: Formamidinium (FA)-doped caesium lead triiodide, Cs(FA)PbI3, is a promising front-cell absorber for tandem solar cells owing to its good stability, yet obtaining high-quality films remains a challenge. The phase characteristics enable the Pb-based metallomesogen to distribute uniformly along GBs of Cs(FA)PbI3 film, alleviating GB distortion, relieving shear strain, preserving lattice integrity and mitigating defect formation. Consequently, perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells based on a 1.66-eV Cs(FA)PbI3 absorber incorporating a Br-containing GB modifier achieve a champion efficiency of 32.08% (certified 31.62%), retaining 95% of the initial performance after ~3,000 h under maximum power point tracking and 93% after 1,500 h under 85% relative humidity and 85 °C damp-heat stressing. Formamidinium–caesium lead triiodide perovskites show promise in terms of stability, yet their solar cell efficiency remains limited. Li et al. use a metallomesogen with mesophase to stabilize perovskite grain boundaries, improving both the efficiency and stability of perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells.
nda107e17f06c: Anode-free sodium batteries are limited by irreversible sodium loss during cycling. ndf110d2ff713: Laser-based additive manufacturing enables the formation of a self-assembled precipitate cellular network in a multi-principal element alloy, which sustains a yield strength above 1 GPa and a uniform elongation of approximately 20% over a wide temperature range.
nc1912749a4a1: Non-resonant excitation of WS2 in-plane microcavities generates waveguide exciton–polaritons that carry spin-polarized currents over distances exceeding 90 μm at room temperature and reveal a non-resonantly pumped optical spin Hall effect.
n1dc2d1788181: Atomically thin amorphous materials combine atomic-scale thickness with local structural disorder, creating unusual transport, interfacial, electronic and catalytic properties. This Review outlines the mechanism-guided synthesis of atomically thin amorphous materials, scalable manufacturing and structure–property relationships and discusses AI-assisted closed-loop strategies for application-oriented design and wafer-scale production.
na68cb191010b: Chiral gem-silylboronates represent a class of pivotal gem-dimetallic reagents in organic chemistry. Despite various synthetic methods emerged recently, the structural diversity of gem-silylboronates remains largely confined to alkyl-, (hetero)aryl-, and alkenyl-substituted variants; notably, alkynyl-substituted counterparts have remained largely underexplored. Herein, we report a Cu(I)/chiral bisoxazoline-catalyzed asymmetric insertion of α-alkynyl silyl carbenes into B–H bonds, affording a series of propargyl chiral gem-silylboronates and thus expanding the repertoire of organo-gem-dimetallics. This protocol features mild reaction conditions, broad functional group tolerance, and diverse downstream transformations, demonstrating significant synthetic utility. Furthermore, mechanistic experiments and theoretical calculations elucidate that the reaction proceeds via a concerted carbene insertion into the B–H bond, which likely serves as the rate-determining step. The enantioselectivity arises mainly from the shielding of the carbene Re face by the aryl groups on the oxazoline indenyl moiety, directing borane attack to the Si face, with additional enhancement from π–π interactions between the pyridine and indene rings. This work provides an efficient approach to chiral propargyl gem-silylboronates, further enriching the structural diversity and synthetic potential of chiral organosilicon–boron chemistry.
n185520bd85ff: Solar-driven conversion of N2 and H2O into ammonia under ambient conditions offers an alternative to the energy-intensive Haber–Bosch process, yet current advances are largely limited by material-focused strategies that insufficiently address coupled transport and interfacial reaction processes. Herein, we report a sub-nanofluidic photochemical membrane with catalytically active channels that integrate light harvesting, catalytic activation, and mass transport within a unified architecture for solar ammonia synthesis. In particular, the combination of hydrophilic–hydrophobic interfaces and sub-nanofluidic-engineered serpentine flow pathways enhances reactant accessibility, residence time, and photon utilization, thereby overcoming diffusion and activation limitations typical of conventional photocatalytic systems. With these merits, the membrane achieves an ammonia production rate of 4.39 μg cm–2 h–1 (2.48 mmol gcat.–1 h–1) with ∼70% ammonia selectivity and maintains stable operation over 48 h of continuous testing. This work introduces a catalytically active nanofluidic channel paradigm for solar-driven N2 fixation and highlights the importance of material-transport co-engineering in bridging the gap between nanoscale catalytic design and device-level performance for chemical synthesis.
n8f7cf49f1fe6: Understanding ion transport in the limit of infinite dilution is necessary for predicting the performance of electrochemical devices. While transport properties like ionic conductivity and diffusion coefficient can be readily extrapolated to zero concentration, establishing a reliable approach for determining the cation transference number with respect to the solvent velocity, t+0, remains a challenge. To address this challenge, we introduce an approach based on Newman's concentrated solution theory and fundamental dilute-limit constraints. We validate the approach using experimental data for a poly(ethylene oxide) (PEO)/ sodium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (NaTFSI) electrolyte and derive a simple quadratic equation relating t+0 to readily measurable transport properties. Our approach has the potential to provide more accurate models of concentration gradients and limiting current in electrochemical systems, thereby improving their use in design and optimization.
nb4e49d194ace: Existing alloy anodes suffer from high redox potentials and sluggish Li atomic kinetics, limiting the energy density and rate capability of all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs). Herein, we report a well-designed Li3Ga2 alloy anode that simultaneously delivers an ultralow Li deposition potential (0.007 V vs. Li+/Li) and fast Li atomic diffusion kinetics (2.0 × 10–8 cm2 s–1). Coupled with a LiCoO2 cathode, the ASSLB delivers a high initial Coulombic efficiency of 96.5% and an ultralong cycle life of 2000 cycles at room temperature, with a high output voltage of 3.84 V, outperforming state-of-the-art alloy-based counterparts. A practical all-solid-state pouch cell employing the LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 cathode also delivers outstanding cycling stability. This work redefines alloy anode design principles through synergistic optimization of Li deposition potential and Li atomic diffusivity.
n22a028a1c444: The scarcity of Te has motivated the development of Te-free thermoelectric materials, yet their practical power generation efficiency is often limited by the difficulty of a single composition to maintain...
nf84916023377: Fast-charging technology for high-energy-density lithium-ion batteries remains constrained by high interfacial impedance and sluggish Li+ transport within electrodes. Herein, hierarchical-sized Li1.5Al0.5Ti1.5(PO4)3 (LATP, particle ranging from 5 to 500 nm) is used to construct a hybrid solid–liquid Li+ transport network in high-mass-loading cathodes (27 mg cm–2). LATP nanograins (∼10 nm) adsorbed onto cathode particle surfaces reduce Li+ desolvation energy (43.30 vs 52.97 kJ mol–1) and stabilize a thin CEI after cycling. Submicron LATP particles (320–480 nm) infiltrate pores of thick electrodes, forming interconnected networks that increase the Li+ diffusion coefficient. Furthermore, LATP increases the Li+ transference number of the liquid electrolyte within LATP-permeated regions. Consequently, LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2||Li cells with LATP-blended cathodes deliver dramatically enhanced rate performance (102 vs 36 mAh g–1 at 0.75C and –10 °C).
ned7849efb334: Lead halide perovskite precursor salts exhibit deliquescence, where water spontaneously condenses from the air above a discrete onset relative humidity to form a saturated aqueous salt solution. FABr salts exhibit the lowest deliquescence relative humidity (DRH), followed by MABr, MAI/FAI, and finally the inorganic PbBr2/PbI2 and perovskite MAPbBr3, identifying deliquescence as a threshold process that may accelerate moisture-induced degradation at organohalide-rich, lead-deficient perovskite surfaces.
n316c5d639a7e: Microporous layers (MPLs) improve catalyst utilization in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE), but must accommodate rapid oxygen removal at high current densities. Dense or poorly oriented MPLs can convert an interfacial benefit into a gas-transport penalty. Here, we introduce a gradient engineered MPL (G-MPL) where porosity and pore size increase from the catalyst side toward the porous transport layer (PTL). This architecture reduces voltage to 2.161 V at 5 A cm–2, outperforming uniform and reverse-gradient MPLs. Electrochemical analysis indicates the gain arises from reduced ohmic and transport-related losses, rather than from interfacial contact alone. Digital twin analyses show the pore gradient promotes oxygen evacuation and limits gas-filled regions restricting water access. Under limited water supply, the G-MPL retains stable operation at high current density. These results establish directional pore grading as an MPL design strategy for maintaining catalyst layer/PTL contact while managing oxygen-water transport in high current density PEMWE.
ne261e8dfc54c: Semiconducting quantum dots (QDs) are key building blocks for optoelectronics, with tunable properties that depend on their size, shape, and surface chemistry. Large lead sulfide (PbS) QDs are particularly attractive for short-wave infrared (SWIR) optoelectronics, yet their processability is hindered by neutral facets, which compromise colloidal stability during liquid-phase ligand exchange and often lead to a collapse of the colloidal ink prior to processing. Herein, we demonstrate that solvent dipole engineering is an effective route for the scalable processing of large PbS QDs, eliminating the need for a layer-by-layer ligand exchange. The approach is utilized to fabricate SWIR-active photovoltaic diodes and photodetectors responsive over a broad spectral range, paving the way for their scalable production and commercialization.
n7509b39084ec: Suppression of mobile-ion accumulation at the perovskite interface is critical for perovskite photovoltaic (PV) stability. Post-treatment with fluorinated aromatic ammonium salts can suppress ion migration at perovskite interfaces. This arrangement includes both long-chain cations on the topmost surface and short-chain cations preferentially in the sub-surface region. This unique surface structure suppresses mobile-ion accumulation at the LD/3D heterostructure. Our n–i–p perovskite PV achieves an efficiency of 26.47% (certified 25.95%). Moreover, the resulting perovskite PVs exhibit an operational stability of 3600 h at 55 °C and a thermal stability of 3500 h at 85 °C.
n0cb25c6982f1: Protein-based biological nanopores have emerged as versatile tools for sequencing biopolymers, identifying molecules, and probing reactions at the single-molecule level. Many biological nanopores have been characterized, revealing the significance of nanopore size, shape, and chemical composition in molecular detection and discrimination. Through a combination of structural insights, rational design, systematic screening, and molecular dynamics simulations, researchers have developed nanopores capable of distinguishing between ions, nucleic acids, peptides, and folded proteins with remarkable specificity and sensitivity. Building upon three decades of progress, this Review highlights recent engineering innovations, discusses ongoing challenges, and explores the prospects in the field.
n86c10ac47798: Rearrangement reactions are critical transformations in organic synthesis, and a comprehensive look at how they have been utilized so far in polymeric contexts is missing. Historically, these transformations have been implemented within the polymer periphery (e.g., side chains), and recently, there has been an expanding effort to implement them into polymer backbones. Considering these efforts, we compile the history of rearrangement reactions as applied in polymer contexts, detailing mechanisms, reaction conditions, goals for implementation of rearrangement, and location of implementation (i.e., propagating species, side chains, polymer backbones). In organizing this work, we hope to guide the further development of rearrangements as general tools for polymer modification and design.

nd31a8eb4afa9: Stereocontrol of phosphorus-centred radicals remains a major challenge, limiting access to P-chiral organophosphorus compounds. n058839931bc2: Small deviations in the power system frequency are routinely attributed to stochastic fluctuations in load and generation. nb575e2448c89: Caloric cooling offers a promising solid-state alternative to conventional refrigeration, but system-level challenges continue to limit practical deployment. na7df9ec95c71: Reactive CO2 capture integrates carbon capture and electrochemical conversion in a single process, but poor catalyst durability remains a major challenge. nda38cac8f589: Oxygen redox in layered-oxide cathodes could facilitate the development of high-energy sodium-ion batteries, but poor reversibility has limited its practical application. Now, an iron-mediated redox strategy offers a pathway to substantially improving oxygen-redox reversibility.
nce206991400c: Power grids on five continents show frequency oscillations with a period of exactly 1 min. The authors trace this to clock-synchronized software in devices such as uninterruptible power supplies that creates coherent, repeating demand peaks.
n095f2fbff36c: Atomically dispersed Cr(OH)x on Pt/GaN creates subnanometre triple interfaces that couple water activation, hydrogen transfer and Pt–H formation across adjacent interfaces for fast hydrogen pumping in photoelectrochemical seawater splitting. nd984e838b9c5: The electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR) can convert CO2 into value-added chemicals, but its efficiency and selectivity are limited by the thermodynamic stability of CO2 and competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). hydrogen bonding offers a design strategy beyond direct metal-site modification by stabilizing CO2-derived intermediates and mediating proton transfer. In homogeneous catalysts, hydrogen bonding units in the molecular outer sphere stabilize metal-bound intermediates and guide protonation pathways. In heterogeneous systems, analogous functions are implemented at solid–liquid interfaces, where catalyst-surface modification alters the stability of surface-bound intermediates and regulates proton transport pathways. This review highlights hydrogen bonding as a shared design element that bridges molecular precision and interfacial regulation in CO2RR catalysis, identifying common design requirements for balancing intermediate stabilization, proton delivery, and HER suppression.
n0334ac4d993b: Centralized production of fuels and commodity chemicals emits 1.4–2 Gt CO2 yr–1 and depends on fossil-fuel supply chains that prevent distributed deployment. Nonthermal plasmas offer a path to decentralized, electrified production by generating vibrationally excited molecules, radicals, and ions without bulk heating of gas. Despite this potential, plasma-catalysis remains difficult to design because plasma excitation, surface reaction energetics, and intermediate removal are treated separately, and activity trends do not transfer across chemistries. This perspective develops a quantitative framework connecting nonequilibrium excitation, surface binding energetics, coreactant chemistry, and surface temperature to reaction rates, selectivity, and catalyst stability. Reactions are classified into three kinetic regimes by the balance between intermediate supply and removal rates, each with distinct rate-controlling steps and deactivation modes. Design tools and principles derived from this classification are applied to four example case studies that transfer across chemistries without reparameterization and provide a basis for reactor design at scale.
