nf9305c8813aa: Rational design of oxide photocatalysts with intrinsically efficient bulk carrier transport remains a major challenge because carrier migration is strongly governed by the complex interplay among crystal structure, electronic structure, and chemical bonding. Here, we propose a Frontier orbital engineering strategy to regulate intrinsic carrier transport by reconstructing the Frontier orbital composition within a structurally robust oxide framework. Based on the tunnel-type Na2Ti6O13 structure, the oxide semiconductor K2Zn2Nb4O13 was designed and synthesized through the cooperative substitution of Ti4+ by Zn2+/Nb5+. Combined high-resolution PXRD and NPD refinements confirm the successful realization of the designed tunnel framework with complete Zn/Nb ordering. Orbital-resolved electronic structure and chemical bonding analyses demonstrate that the valence band maximum (VBM) and conduction band minimum (CBM) are mainly derived from Zn 3d−O 2p and Nb1 4d−O 2p antibonding orbitals, respectively. Such orbital decoupling of Frontier orbital contributing units and the continuous covalent networks along the b-axis provide favorable pathways for bulk carrier migration and establish the structural and electronic basis for the proposed Frontier orbital engineering strategy. Experimentally, Pd-loaded K2Zn2Nb4O13 exhibits enhanced photocatalytic H2 generation activity, achieving a rate of 119(3) μmol/h. This work provides Frontier orbital engineering as a design paradigm for functional materials, enabling the rational manipulation of intrinsic charge transport properties through the synergistic regulation of crystal structure, electronic structure, and chemical bonding.
n465bd8456283: Metal nanoparticle sintering in high-temperature oxidizing atmospheres remains a primary deactivation pathway for platinum-group metal catalysts on alumina supports. Here, atomic layer deposition (ALD) was used to deposit alumina on supported Pt catalysts and develop alumina-encapsulated Pt/Al2O3 catalysts that were aged at 800 °C under different atmospheres and characterized by time-resolved high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM), CO-probe diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy (CO-DRIFTS), and propene combustion kinetics. Within the alumina-encapsulated system, a sub-2 nm Pt cluster population formed under all oxidizing atmospheres tested but not under inert atmosphere, and this population persisted for at least 12 h at 800 °C under propene complete combustion (PCC) conditions. Unencapsulated Pt/Al2O3 controls, by contrast, developed only a transient sub-2 nm population, detected within 1 min of aging in air at 800 °C and no longer present afterward, consistent with the rapid disappearance of small particles predicted by Ostwald ripening theory. CO-DRIFTS confirmed the presence of undercoordinated Pt surface sites in all oxidatively aged samples, with no detectable signal when the sample was aged under inert atmosphere. Propene combustion rates measured after aging for an alumina-encapsulated catalyst were approximately two and five times higher than the fresh encapsulated catalyst for catalysts aged under inert atmosphere and under oxygen and steam, respectively. DFT calculations of Pt diffusion through defective Al2O3 identified kinetically accessible diffusion pathways at 800 °C, with activation barriers as low as 0.76 eV. Furthermore, Pt surface binding was calculated to be favored in the presence of O2. These results identify oxygen-driven surface segregation, mediated by defect-assisted diffusion through the ALD overcoat, as a possible mechanism responsible for nanocluster formation in this system. The persistence of the sub-2 nm cluster population for at least 12 h at 800 °C under PCC conditions demonstrates the thermal stability of these sites within the encapsulated architecture.
ndbadc1daa7c1: Layered inorganic materials can exhibit symmetry-breaking transitions in which electronic instabilities and local structural modes are strongly intertwined. Here we compare the isovalent chalcogenides Bi2Rh3Se2 and Bi2Rh3S2 by synchrotron single-crystal X-ray diffraction and density-functional-theory calculations, and identify a static Bi2Rh4 breathing distortion as the common local motif underlying their distinct low-temperature phases. In Bi2Rh3Se2, the transition near 240 K is characterized by the loss of C-centering without a change in the conventional unit-cell volume. The resulting primitive lattice contains inequivalent Rh4 quadrilaterals formed by alternating expansion and contraction, establishing a C-centering-breaking breathing order. Although previous spectroscopic studies have reported CDW-like signatures in Bi2Rh3Se2, the calculated Fermi surfaces of the high-temperature phase do not reveal an obvious nesting vector expected for a simple nesting-driven Peierls-type CDW scenario. Instead, the Rh 4d-derived electronic states at the Fermi level are naturally sensitive to the observed Rh4 breathing distortion, indicating that the transition is best described as a breathing-order transition accompanied by electronic reconstruction. In Bi2Rh3S2, a comparable Bi2Rh4 breathing distortion appears, but its ordering pattern is switched: when described in the high-temperature-cell setting, the Bi2Rh4 units form a large−small−small sequence along the aHT-direction, accompanied by an antiphase relation between neighboring chains, producing a commensurate 3× superstructure consistent with the first-order character of the transition. Calculations based on the experimentally refined structures further reveal a reduction of the density of states near EF and an anisotropic redistribution of occupied low-energy states in the breathing-distorted phases, supporting the coupling between the Bi2Rh4 motif and electronic reconstruction. These results show that isovalent chalcogen substitution selects the in-plane ordering pattern of an intrinsic Bi2Rh4 breathing distortion, thereby switching the collective symmetry-breaking pathway and associated electronic response.
n457564aea7d6: Two-dimensional Cu nanostructures containing noncanonical face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed (fcc/hcp) heterophase boundaries are attractive for CO2 electroreduction but remain difficult to prepare by wet-chemical methods. Here, we report a high-temperature solution reduction route to Cu nanodisks with a thickness of 26.5 ± 2.3 nm and a diameter of 85.6 ± 3.7 nm. Transmission electron microscopy reveals abundant fcc/2H and fcc/4H interfaces on the nanodisk side surfaces, where the 2H and 4H polytypes exhibit AB and ABCB stacking, respectively. In CO2-saturated 0.1 M KHCO3, the nanodisks achieve a methane Faradaic efficiency of 60.4% at −1.25 V vs the reversible hydrogen electrode and outperform fcc Cu nanoparticle and microsheet controls tested at the same catalyst loading. Density functional theory calculations indicate that the free-energy penalty for forming the *CHO intermediate is smaller on the fcc/2H and fcc/4H models than on fcc Cu. These results support a thermodynamic contribution of heterophase interfaces to the observed methane selectivity; the calculations do not establish a reduction in kinetic activation barriers. This solution-phase route therefore provides access to phase-engineered Cu nanodisks and enables structure−property relationships relevant to CO2-to-CH4 electrocatalysis.
n0b819e8ebfc5: Atomically dispersed W activates terrace Mn sites in β-MnO 2 via W–O–Mn charge delocalization, increasing accessible-site density and boosting OER sixfold. Strong W–O bonds suppress Mn dissolution, enabling stable operation for 1250 h at 300 mA cm −2 .
n692210636012: Stretchable solar cells could energize portable and wearable electronics, yet their efficiency and mechanical durability are measured under conditions so divergent that devices of comparable initial performance defy cross-laboratory comparison. Ye and colleagues trace this divergence to routinely overlooked factors, among them substrate properties, strain rate, and strain-induced changes in illuminated area. They introduce metrics for tolerable strain and cycle lifetime, together with a reporting checklist, establishing a shared benchmark for the field and a path to formal standardization.
n36967a5e1662: This work demonstrates an intrinsically stretchable thin-film rechargeable Na-ion battery by addressing the materials challenges and integration compatibilities across the whole battery system. The design combines biocompatible materials selection and organic Na-ion electrochemical system design, with a solvent-resistant stretchable current collector, a strain-adaptable gel polymer electrolyte, and tunable-modulus organic electrodes. It presents a promising platform for next-generation thin-film stretchable power sources for wearable and biomedical electronic devices.
nacf0cbb408c5: Liquid metal (LM) composites transform into stretchable conductors through compressive loading, but how this critical mechanical sintering process creates conductive networks has remained unclear. Here, we show that mechanical loading generates cracks that enable LM to flow, connect isolated droplets, and form persistent conductive networks. A fracture-based model captures this transition across droplet sizes and composite architectures, establishing a general framework for how fracture can reorganize embedded liquids to create function in soft materials.
n69218a252dae: Controlling phase evolution and composition homogeneity are challenging for chalcopyrites. Ma, Wu, Liu, Yan et al. use acetate anions to build complex networks in precursor solution, achieving single-phase crystallization and an 18.53% efficient Cu(In,Ga)Se2 solar cell.
n10a60b686412: Bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells are promising for high area-normalized power output, but factors governing the photothermal stability of perovskite absorbers remains unclear. Xu et al. identify lattice compliance as a descriptor when screening stable perovskites.
nef61abb22bef: Sulfur-based redox flow batteries promise low-cost, long-duration energy storage using abundant active materials, but commercial success depends on much more than low-cost materials. nb5b35a1a035c: The electron-beam-assisted subtraction method enables the controllable fabrication of free-standing metal oxide monolayers, along with lateral heterostructures and twisted bilayers, expanding the material space of 2D quantum systems.
nd2fa4369b0d5: Photonic metasurfaces patterned in anisotropic ReS2 create robust, spectrally scalable directional photonic flatbands, enabling the topological control of polarization-resolved exciton–polaritons and enhanced light–matter coupling.

n3923abf06e24: Porous liquids combine permanent porosity with fluidity, extending the design of porous materials beyond conventional solid frameworks. n76f9dd444ce1: By decoupling ceramic-film densification from high-temperature sintering, molten-salt-mediated liquid-phase growth enables a dense, compositionally uniform proton-conducting thin film to form at 800 °C, despite its melting point exceeding 2,700 °C. n7eff34347f13: Aqueous redox flow batteries (ARFBs) comprising earth-abundant charge carriers could cheaply store grid-scale renewable electricity, but most lab-scale systems have a low open-circuit potential (OCP) that inflates system cost. We report a non-hybrid aqueous flow cell with an OCP of 2.2 V, among the highest reported for this class, pairing an alkaline chromium-1,3-propylenediaminetetraacetate negolyte with an acidic bromide posolyte. The two electrolytes maintain an approximately seven-unit pH gradient across a single cation-exchange membrane, without external oxygen or a bipolar-membrane recovery sub-cell: operando pH measurements and a zero-dimensional model show that the difference is sustained passively by balancing slow proton crossover against hydrogen evolution and positive-side acid generation. The cell cycles for 240 h with a Coulombic efficiency of up to 99.5%; tuning the posolyte additive, electrode, and membrane raises the peak power density to 534 mW cm–2 at 43 °C.
ncf6b42c3c595: Aqueous polysulfide redox flow batteries (RFBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage owing to their low cost and high safety. However, stable operation at high current density remains challenging for polysulfide RFBs (typically cycling below 40 mA cm–2), with the degradation mechanisms remaining poorly understood. Here, we identify current density as a critical factor governing the cycle life and elucidate sulfur deposition-induced degradation. Increasing current density simultaneously accelerates polysulfide crossover and promotes the formation of compact sulfur deposits, which block ion-transport pathways and lead to rapid cell failure. Based on this mechanistic understanding, a surfactant additive was employed to regulate sulfur nucleation and growth, extending the cycle life of polysulfide/ferrocyanide RFBs from 30 cycles to over 500 cycles at 60 mA cm–2. This work elucidates current density and sulfur morphology as critical factors governing polysulfide RFB degradation and provides design principles for durable, high-rate polysulfide-based RFBs.
n4fcf93d66726: While high-power lithium-ion capacitors (LICs) with high energy density emerge as promising pulse-/peak-power solutions for AI data centers, their long-term viability remains severely hindered by the degradation of the activated carbon (AC) positive electrode. To evaluate this aging behavior, we propose a 24-h high-voltage cycling (HVC) protocol integrated with operando Raman spectroscopy, demonstrating that the turning point in the D1 band can serve as a sensitive indicator of corrosion severity. During the early-stage HVC aging, cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) formation and gas evolution passivate defect-related Raman signals, narrowing the D1 band. As aging proceeds, carbon corrosion becomes dominant and broadens the D1 band. By validating this approach across various ACs, we establish a direct correlation between an earlier structural turning point and accelerated capacity decay, thereby uncovering carbon aging mechanisms and offering an unprecedented, rapid diagnostic technique for capacitor-type materials.
n9594c2bc857b: A palladium catalyst supported on porous poly( p -phenylene sulfide) (Pd(0)/PPS) was developed for the chemoselective hydrogenation of α,β-unsaturated carbonyl compounds.
n4787c9ca034a: In situ/operando and rapid freeze-quench Mössbauer approaches enable quantitative tracking of the oxidation state, spin state, and local coordination environment of Mössbauer-active metal sites in single-atom catalysts during catalytic processes, thus providing a deeper understanding of dynamic reaction mechanisms and contributing to the rational design of novel, efficient catalysts at the atomic scale.
nfb1626f9da66: Interfacial hydration fundamentally constrains adhesion in aqueous and physiological environments by preventing intimate contact, competing for binding sites, and weakening the load-bearing interfaces. Although wet adhesives have been extensively designed for durable fixation, emerging technologies in soft robotics, wearable bioelectronics, and minimally invasive medicine require interfaces that can form adhesion, recover after reuse, or detach on-demand under hydrated conditions. This Review discusses reversible wet adhesion through two operational modes: Mode I, cyclic reusability through repeated restoration of adhesion over attachment-detachment cycles, and Mode II, on-demand detachability through trigger-induced conversion of a stable adhesive state into a weakly adherent state through a controlled, low-damage release pathway. We examine supramolecular interactions, dynamic covalent chemistry, mesoscale architectures, biomimetic designs, and hybrid strategies as complementary routes for regulating hydration, interfacial binding, mechanical dissipation, and adhesive state transitions at wet interfaces. We analyze how contact formation, hydration history, fracture pathways, loading history, test geometry, and biofluid exposure shape the measured performance. We further assess current methods for quantifying reusability, switching, durability, and biofluid tolerance, emphasizing failure mode-informed evaluation and standardized reporting criteria. Integrating hydration thermodynamics, binding kinetics, mechanical dissipation, and stimulus-gated interfacial transitions, this Review develops design and evaluation principles for reversible wet adhesive systems in complex aqueous and biointerfacial environments.
n38c22c435a19: High-entropy materials (HEMs) are composed of multiple principal elements stabilized by the configurational entropy. They establish a new design paradigm in electrocatalysis by leveraging local disorder and multielement synergy to create diverse and tunable active site environments. While HEMs have been broadly reviewed, a focused and reaction-specific assessment of their role in gas-involved electrocatalysis is absent. This review fills that gap by examining entropy-driven design principles, entropy-guided synthesis, nanoscale structural control, and advanced characterization of HEMs and by linking these aspects to their reaction-specific catalytic behavior in gas-involved electrocatalysis. We build a unified framework linking high-entropy chemistry to catalytic function across five key reactions: the CO2 reduction reaction (CO2RR), hydrogen oxidation reaction (HOR), oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), nitrogen reduction reaction (NRR), and nitrogen oxidation reaction (NOR). We provide comprehensive coverage across all major HEM families, including high-entropy alloys, oxides, chalcogenides, hydroxides, fluorides, MXenes, and single-atom configurations, highlighting features unique to each system. Key challenges and future directions are outlined, including scalable synthesis, active-site identification, machine-learning-guided discovery, and interfacial engineering. This review provides a reaction-focused framework for advancing HEM-based electrocatalysis and offers guidance for designing next-generation materials for clean energy technologies.
n38c28a122637: This review outlines design principles, printing methods, stretchable electrodes, structural strategies, and cathode chemistries for body-conformable aqueous zinc-based batteries in medical devices.

ndcf5796e5afc: While phosphorus chalcogenides are promising candidates for infrared nonlinear optical (IR-NLO) applications, a fundamental understanding of the microscopic mechanisms driving their second harmonic generation (SHG) response is still lacking. In this work, we address this gap by developing atomate2-ARTATOP, an open-source high-throughput computational framework that integrates atomic response theory (ART) into atomate2 to enable systematic NLO property screening and analysis. Our large-scale screening of 231 non-centrosymmetric compounds spanning thiophosphates (PS), selenophosphates (PSe), and oxygen-containing phosphorus chalcogenides (PSO) reveals a clear SHG performance trend (PSe > PS > PSO), mapping specific chemical families to targeted infrared and ultraviolet spectral windows. Notably, Hg2P2S7 and InPSe4 exhibit exceptional powder-averaged SHG coefficients of 29.15 (∼2.8 × AGS) and 34.28 pm/V (∼3.2 × AGS), respectively, outperforming the industry standard AgGaS2. Interestingly, unlike conventional thiophosphates, ZnGaPS, a mixed phosphide-sulfide, also exhibits a strong SHG response (21.4 pm/V, ∼2.0 × AGS). Additionally, we identify P2S2O3 as a superior ultraviolet candidate, combining a wide band gap (5.35 eV) with an SHG response ∼7.8 times that of KH2PO4. Through partial response function analysis, we demonstrate that the SHG response is fundamentally governed by nonbonding chalcogen p states, with other elements playing a secondary role on average but contributing considerably in individual compounds. Moreover, the net response in many compounds reflects a competition between positive and negative contributions from different structural units. Finally, by identifying compositional features that induce negative SHG contributions, we offer design insights for enhancing constructive SHG contributions. This work provides a quantitative, orbital-level blueprint for the discovery of next-generation NLO materials.
na40199b42991: Phosphorus exhibits rich allotropy that gives rise to diverse polyanionic clusters and networks. The unusual transport phenomena observed in black phosphorus and its magnetic analogue α-EuP3 highlight the potential of extended phosphorus networks to generate emergent electronic properties. At the same time, high pressure has a natural affinity with P-rich polyphosphides, as it offers access to structurally diverse phosphorus networks, presenting them as a promising platform for materials discovery. In this work, P-rich compounds in the Sr−P and Eu−P systems were explored by combining high-pressure synthesis with first-principles calculations. Five previously unknown polyphosphides were synthesized across the P-rich composition range AP8−AP10 (A = Eu, Sr): EuP8, EuP9, EuP10, SrP8, and SrP10. These compounds contain chain-like and cage-like phosphorus frameworks, with varying lone-pair-bearing P concentrations across compositions. Pressure-dependent convex-hull calculations incorporating the experimentally determined structures identify a narrow moderate pressure window of 2−4 GPa in which the discovered P-rich phases become synthetically accessible, thereby providing a practical guide to their high-pressure synthesis conditions. These results demonstrate that computationally assisted high-pressure synthesis provides a powerful approach to discovering unexplored metastable phases and developing magnetic and topological functionalities in anion-rich binary Zintl compounds.
n088519d71e80: As a traditional thermoelectric material, PbTe exhibits a high peak zT value. However, it is highly susceptible to oxidation during either synthesis or device operation. Thus, it is essential to understand the oxidation behavior at finite temperatures and its effects on the geometries of PbTe surfaces. Focusing on oxygen adsorption at two stable PbTe(100) and PbTe(111) surfaces, using cluster expansion, we identify the most stable adsorption configurations of 0.5O−PbTe(100) and 0.33O−PbTe(111) with oxygen coverages of 0.5 and 0.33, respectively. Electronic structure calculations reveal that oxygen atoms form covalent bonds with surface Te atoms. Ab initio molecular dynamics investigations demonstrate temperature is a critical factor that damages PbTe surfaces and drives oxygen atoms into sublayers, forming surface oxides. Oxygen atoms migrate into a deeper sublayer on PbTe(111) than on PbTe(100). Increasing temperature and oxygen coverage aggravate these effects. Surface oxidation fundamentally deteriorates electrical transport characteristics by changing carrier concentration, inducing transitions between n- and p-type conduction, and decreasing carrier mobility. This ultimately leads to significant degradation in its thermoelectric performance. Possible approaches include depositing dense passivation layers to block oxygen adsorption and diffusion.
n92cdca8985a4: Dual-band electrochromic smart windows, capable of independently regulating visible and near-infrared solar radiation, offer an effective route toward reducing building/vehicle energy consumption. However, their practical implementation is often limited by slow switching kinetics, insufficient bistability, as well as challenges in fabricating polychromatic, uniform, and scalable electrochromic films with efficient ion and charge transport. Here, we report an interfacial self-assembly strategy to fabricate large-area polyaniline (PANI) thin films featuring a hierarchically porous architecture and thickness-dependent porosity gradient. The self-assembly process, driven by solvent exchange at the air–water interface and modulated by surfactant confinement, produces interconnected PANI nanoparticle networks with both in-plane hierarchical pores and out-of-plane structural gradation. This architecture facilitates electrolyte penetration and charge transport across the film thickness. As a result, the PANI films enable rapid and stable dual-band electrochromic modulation, exhibiting three distinct optical states (“bright”, “cool”, and “dark”) with independent control of visible and near-infrared transmittance. The assembled devices demonstrate fast response (coloration/bleaching times of 1.8/4 s at 633 nm and 1.2/3.6 s at 1200 nm), high coloration efficiency, and excellent optical bistability, together with effective indoor thermal regulation. These results establish interfacial self-assembly as a versatile approach for engineering functional polymer films for next-generation energy-efficient smart windows.
n49da6049c3ab: Ce-doped HfO2 (HCO) ferroelectric thin films have attracted considerable attention for next-generation integrated ferroelectric devices owing to their excellent compatibility with complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor technology and promising ferroelectric properties. However, previously reported HCO films generally require relatively large thicknesses and high processing temperatures, limiting their application in highly scaled devices. Here, we demonstrate HCO ferroelectric thin films grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD) and systematically investigate the effects of Ce concentration and film thickness on their structural and ferroelectric properties. The HCO film with 5.0% Ce doping exhibits the highest ferroelectric orthorhombic phase fraction, which is attributed to the formation of coupled defects involving Ce-substitution on Hf sites and oxygen vacancies, as revealed by first-principles calculations. Moreover, the HCO films annealed at 700 °C exhibit excellent ferroelectric properties at the thickness ranging from 12 to 24 nm. In particular, the 18 nm-thick HCO film with 5.0% Ce achieves a remanent polarization of 19.4 μC/cm2 and an excellent switching endurance exceeding 1 × 109 cycles. These results demonstrate the potential of ALD-grown HCO as a scalable material platform for highly integrated and multifunctional ferroelectric devices.
n08a9af6739bd: Acid-mediated precipitation of aqueous tungstate solutions is widely used to synthesize WO3 nanoparticles, yet the coupling of reagent identity, ionic strength, and speciation equilibria across different synthetic protocols cloud which variables govern resulting polymorph type and nanoparticle morphology, as well as whether polymorph and nanoparticle morphology can be tuned independently. Here, we systematically vary acid and alkali salt identity, alkali cation concentration, and acid addition rate to isolate their individual contributions. By accounting for differences in ion activities and speciation equilibria, we show that apparent structure-directing effects previously attributed to anion identity instead arise primarily from solution-level differences rather than direct anion−WO3 interactions. In contrast, alkali cation concentration exerts an independent influence on the favorability of the metastable hexagonal phase that persists even after accounting for differences in ionic strength and speciation. We further demonstrate that acid addition rate modulates nanoparticle morphology without affecting polymorph outcome, identifying acidification kinetics as a synthetic handle acting independently of the factors governing polymorph selection. Using these mechanistic insights, we then show the systematic tunability of polymorph-dependent photochromic behavior in the resulting particles. Together, these findings provide independent synthetic handles for controlling WO3 nanoparticle phase and morphology which directly impact their functional properties, and offer a quantitative approach for reconciling and comparing outcomes across diverse reagent combinations and protocols in WO3 NP synthesis.

n1d1514f74b65: Predicting productive enzyme–photocatalyst combinations remains difficult. n44e95b647922: Epitaxial strain and a metallic SrRuO3 bottom electrode are used to stablilize a monoclinic phase in four-unit-cell BiFeO3 thin films. A broad suite of measurements are used to support the presence of both ferroelectricity and d-wave altermagnetism in these ultrathin films.
n327ceed1d6ab: Lipid nanoparticles are increasingly adept at delivering therapeutics to specific tissues and cell types, and, in some cases, the nanoparticles themselves can now modulate cellular behaviour, immune function and therapeutic outcome.
n99a396f7751d: The therapeutic potential of mRNA had been on the radar for decades but it took an alliance with lipid nanoparticle research to make it a reality. Researchers are now looking for ways to better increase efficacy and reduce side effects to extend the potential of the delivery agents from vaccines to pulmonary and neurological interventions.
n2b6705536beb: Implantable magnetic sensing offers a route to wireless physiological monitoring, but conventional metallic magnets persist beyond their functional lifetime. Now, a bioresorbable metal-free molecular magnet is developed that can serve as an implanted magnetic signal source, enabling untethered and continuous monitoring of organ motion.
n368db01e7ac4: Using an artificial intelligence-guided framework combining retrosynthetic prediction, high-throughput DFT screening and chemical expertise, a readily synthesizable self-assembled monolayer for perovskite photovoltaics is identified. The top candidate delivers 27.2% efficiency and retains >95% of its initial efficiency after 2,000 h at 65 °C under maximum-power-point tracking.
n76f2fa058d3f: Decoupled water electrolysis (DWE) separates H2 and O2 evolution, improving safety and flexibility under intermittent renewable electricity, but requires durable, oxygen-tolerant redox mediators. Here we evaluate 4,4′-azo-bis(1-pyridinium-3-propane-sulfonate) (ABPS), a zwitterionic azo molecule, as an electron-coupled proton buffer for acidic DWE. Its azo/hydrazo core supports reversible two-electron/two-proton chemistry at 0.81 V vs RHE, while zwitterionic substituents provide high aqueous solubility and suppress crossover through low-cost sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) membranes. Reduced H2ABPS shows no detectable oxidation after 90 days in air or during >5 h of continuous pure-O2 bubbling. Symmetric flow-cell cycling over 1000 h yields a capacity-fade rate below 1% year–1. With commercial catalysts at room temperature, decoupled flow cells reach 1.2 A cm–2 and operate for >200 h at 500 mA cm–2 with near-quantitative Faradaic efficiencies while producing high-purity H2 and O2. These results establish zwitterionic azo chemistry as an oxygen-tolerant, durable platform for high-rate decoupled hydrogen production.
n661aa18f14e1: Bipolar membranes (BPMs) maintain separated acidic and alkaline environments via water dissociation at the junction, but high-current-density operation remains challenging because rapid hydrated H+/OH– migration away from the junction must be coupled with sufficient water replenishment toward it. A transport imbalance between these opposing processes causes interfacial dehydration and limits long-term operation. Here, we develop microphase-engineered homologous ion-exchange layers to balance this coupled transport. These layers are fabricated from homologous multiblock poly(biphenyl alkylene) ionomers sharing a common backbone and block architecture, promoting interlayer compatibility and interconnected ionic domains. The hydrated pathways accelerate water replenishment and ion transport, thereby maintaining a stably hydrated junction. The resulting BPM enables pure-water electrolysis at 2.11 V at 1000 mA cm–2 and sustains high-purity hydrogen production for over 1100 h at 500 mA cm–2. This work establishes molecularly engineered ion-exchange layers as an effective approach for improving mass transport in high-current-density BPM systems.
n0b7fe3b2693b: A supported copper complex ( mPAN-Cu ), prepared by the immobilization of CuCl 2 over modified polyacrylonitrile ( mPAN ) is explored as a reusable heterogeneous catalyst for Ullmann type C–O Coupling between a series of aryl halides and phenols.

nc9b854a66c24: Strained rings offer an escape from flat chemical space, enabling access to three-dimensional bridged heterocycles. This perspective examines two complementary strategies—introducing heteroatoms through reaction partners or embedding them within strained precursors—and links precursor design and activation mode to topology, stereochemistry, and substituent orientation. It highlights how heteroatom identity and placement tune molecular properties and outlines advances in stereocontrol, precursor accessibility, and medicinal-chemistry validation needed to make strain-release synthesis a practical tool for drug discovery.
nede34e30c33d: Photoinduced symmetry-breaking charge separation (SB-CS) is a fundamental process in molecular photophysics that underpins energy and charge transport in reaction centers and organic, supramolecular, and hybrid materials. Despite extensive investigations across diverse systems, SB-CS is often described in system-specific terms, obscuring the underlying unifying principles. In this Review, we establish a coherent framework demonstrating that SB-CS can be understood within a multidimensional parameter space defined by electronic coupling, energetic driving force, and nuclear reorganization. We critically analyze how the interplay between locally excited and charge-transfer states governs charge separation and recombination dynamics, highlighting the existence of an optimal intermediate coupling regime that enables efficient symmetry-breaking while suppressing nonproductive decay pathways. By integrating insights from solution, solid-state, and single-molecule measurements, we show that environmental fluctuations and structural heterogeneity play a central role in driving charge localization rather than merely acting as spectators or perturbations. Importantly, we distinguish universal physical principles from system-specific manifestations, allowing the formulation of transferable design rules for achieving efficient and long-lived charge-separated states. Finally, we outline emerging directions toward predictive, data-driven models that link molecular structure to SB-CS dynamics, providing a foundation for the rational design of next-generation optoelectronic and energy-conversion materials.
nb10954689895: Water and aqueous electrolytes at surfaces, interfaces, and in confinement behave differently from the bulk, yet linear spectroscopy rarely combines the chemical specificity, surface selectivity, and temporal resolution needed to resolve electric double-layer formation, specific-ion adsorption, and hydration at interfaces and under nanoconfinement. This review assesses how ultrafast nonlinear vibrational spectroscopy, comprising two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy, vibrational sum-frequency generation (SFG), and time-resolved SFG, probes the hydrogen-bond network and the dynamics of interfacial water and electrolytes on femtosecond-to-picosecond timescales. We first establish vibrational benchmarks for bulk water and simple electrolytes, then treat soft aqueous boundaries, including air–water, hydrophobic and hydrophilic, lipid, surfactant, and nucleic acid interfaces. We next examine solid–liquid and electrochemical systems, spanning metal oxides, minerals, and field-induced effects, before turning to water and proton dynamics in nanoconfined geometries and complex architectures. Throughout, experimental results are set against theoretical and computational frameworks, from polarizable force fields to machine-learning potentials. Our aim is to identify which molecular-level features of interfacial water are now firmly established, where the prevailing mean-field description of the electric double layer breaks down, and which experiments would resolve the outstanding discrepancies.
n2cfa171be154: Birefringent crystals are core materials for polarization modulation in optical devices, yet commercial crystals generally suffer from low birefringence values. In this work, three hybrid halide crystals, (C5H5NS)2ZnCl2, (C5H5NS)2CdCl2, and (C5H5NS)HgCl2, were successfully prepared by combining 4-mercaptopyridine unit with d10 metal chlorides to further modulate the metal coordination environments. For (C5H5NS)2ZnCl2 and (C5H5NS)2CdCl2, two π-conjugated units directly coordinate to one metal-centered tetrahedron, which further assembles into a one-dimensional structure via hydrogen-bond interactions. For (C5H5NS)HgCl2, two π-conjugated units coordinate to two metal-centered tetrahedra, forming the isolated (C5H5NS)2Hg2Cl4 dimer, and the complete crystal framework is stacked by intermolecular forces. The birefringence of the three compounds exhibits diversity with the variation of d10 metal ions. Notably, (C5H5NS)2CdCl2 sets records among cadmium-based hybrid halides with metal−halogen−organic functional groups. Structural analyses and theoretical calculations demonstrate that the birefringence of the three crystals is jointly contributed by the organic part and inorganic composition. This study verifies that modifying the coordination environment by tuning the ionic radii of metal center ions is an effective strategy for birefringence modulation and advances the research on hybrid halides for birefringent crystal applications.
n55b652de8190: Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) offer recyclability and reprocessability, yet bond-exchange dynamics can reduce mechanical strength and toughness. Although the composite formation of CAN provides benefits in both aspectsstrengthening the CAN and adding recyclability to the compositeit still faces a stiffness−ductility trade-off that limits material usefulness. Here, we demonstrate a CAN composite design in which silica nanoparticle incorporation, combined with interfacial chemical structure, enhances ductility and toughness in a highly crosslinked matrix without compromising the high elastic modulus. Introducing poly(disulfide) dynamic covalent bonding chains into the network and at the filler interface significantly increases ductility, toughness, and stress at break. Together with a comparison to composites with permanent interfacial bonding, these results underscore the important role of interfacial chemistry. Based on these comparative experiments, the observed toughness enhancement is proposed to arise from energy dissipation via reorganization at the interphase through stress-activated disulfide exchange and network topological rearrangement. The resulting stress-responsive viscoelasticity enables stable deformation and allows CAN-based composites to overcome the stiffness−ductility trade-off.
n0b3bfb80d758: The structural behavior of CsTaS3 was investigated alongside that of the new heteroanionic compound CsTaS2.16Cl0.84, synthesized via the reaction of Ta and S in a CsCl flux. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that both compounds are isostructural, crystallizing in the centrosymmetric hexagonal space group P63/mmc with split Ta positions along the face-sharing octahedral chain direction. Pair distribution function analysis of both compounds, supported by STEM imaging of CsTaS3, identifies the local intrachain displacement motif as cooperative Ta sliding rather than alternating Ta−Ta dimerization. While X-ray absorption near-edge spectroscopy (XANES) confirms the decrease of the average oxidation state in CsTaS2.16Cl0.84, the same structural distortion persists, albeit now with a reduced magnitude. Both materials are semiconducting, and Cl incorporation increases the band gap from ∼1.00 eV in CsTaS3 to ∼1.12 eV in the heteroanionic phase. Single-crystal detectors fabricated from CsTaS2.16Cl0.84 exhibit high resistivity, which effectively suppresses dark current and enhances signal-to-noise performance. These devices deliver an X-ray sensitivity of 7470 μC Gyair−1 cm−2, demonstrating efficient charge generation and collection under irradiation.
ncd573c80fc95: Large crystals of metal silicide Zintl phases with general formula (Ca/Eu/Mg)2Si were grown from reactions of silicon with varying amounts of europium and calcium in magnesium/zinc flux. The Eu/Ca reactant ratio determined the structure type of the products. Calcium-rich reactions yielded Ca1−xEuxMgSi (0 < x < 0.7) compounds adopting the orthorhombic TiNiSi structure type in space group Pnma. Increasing europium content led to the prevalence of Eu8−yCayMg16Si12 (0 < y < 3.4) products with the hexagonal Ho5Ni19P12 structure type in space group P6̅2m. Single crystal X-ray diffraction studies indicate mixing of Zn on one Mg site in the hexagonal structures; thus, the formula can be expressed as Eu8−yCayMg16−αZnαSi12. Magnetic susceptibility data indicate europium is divalent in all of the compounds, with low-temperature magnetic ordering transitions. Density of states calculations show a pseudogap at the Fermi level for both structures, indicating semimetallic character; transport measurements indicate p-type behavior. Ca/Eu mixing and higher ratios of Eu2+ suppress lattice thermal conductivity in both structure types. In Ca1−xEuxMgSi, Eu-substitution lowers resistivity but yields minimal Seebeck enhancement; in Eu8−yCayMg16Si12 (Eu8−yCayMg16−αZnαSi12), Ca-substitution increases resistivity and markedly improves the Seebeck coefficient, with Eu7.59Ca0.41Mg15.62Zn0.36Si12 reaching S ≈ 150 μV K−1 at 300 K.
ne6380f562cf4: Hierarchical architectures are ubiquitous in nature; however, the bottom-up construction of multilevel chiral macroscopic assemblies from small organic molecules remains highly challenging. Herein, we report an unprecedented assembly strategy for constructing hierarchically organized particles (HOPs) through the co-assembly of achiral o-carborane-based molecules (C-1 and C-2) with chiral (R/S)-limonene. Intriguingly, C-1-(S)-limonene forms microscale cocoon-like superstructures, whereas C-1-(R)-limonene undergoes self-assembly into fibrous architectures that ultimately evolve into random aggregates at the micrometer scale. In contrast, C-2-(R/S)-limonene assembles into bowtie-shaped microarchitectures. Graph Theory (GT) analysis reveals structural complexity indices (CIs) of 5.5 and 54 for the C-1-(S)-limonene- and C-2-(S)-limonene-based HOPs, respectively, indicating significantly higher architectural complexity for the latter. These assemblies exhibit distinct circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) properties: C-1-(S)-limonene displays intense CPL emission at 504 nm with a high luminescence dissymmetry factor (glum) of +0.006, whereas C-2-(S)-limonene exhibits CPL emission at 560 nm with a glum value of +0.002. These results demonstrate that chirality signals are transferred across multiple length scales from the molecular level to macroscopic architectures. The observed structural divergence originates from the synergistic effects of nonclassical dihydrogen bonding (Bδ+−Hδ−···Hδ+−Cδ−) between achiral o-carborane derivatives and chiral limonene, together with molecular polarity and elasticity effects. This study establishes a paradigm for fabricating chiral o-carborane-based hierarchical aggregates with programmable architectures and tailored chiroptical properties.
na0b1aca03d21: Although fluorination introduces tunable lattice rigidity and steric matching that influence molecular dynamics, the use of progressive fluorination as an effective method for structure−property tuning remains limited. Here, we report structural, thermal, dielectric, vibrational, and optical investigations of two members of zero-dimensional (0D) hybrid bismuth bromides with the general formula A3BiBr6, where A denotes 2,2-difluoroethylammonium and 2,2,2-trifluoroethylammonium cations. Differential scanning calorimetry reveals that the difluorinated compound undergoes a first-order phase transition at 184.3/177.5 K (heating/cooling), similar to the monofluorinated analogue, whereas its trifluorinated counterpart exhibits no structural phase transitions within the studied temperature range. A single-crystal X-ray diffraction study shows that the trifluorinated compound adopts trigonal symmetry (space group P3̅). In contrast, the difluorinated analogue crystallizes in the orthorhombic space group Pnnm at room temperature and transforms upon cooling into a monoclinic phase described by the P21/n space group. Temperature-dependent infrared and Raman spectroscopies indicate that the phase transition mechanism is governed by order−disorder processes. The noncovalent interaction calculations support that the F···F intermolecular interactions originate from sterically constrained packing rather than attractive interactions, contributing to dense crystal arrangement. Optical studies reveal that band gap energies correlate with octahedral deformation and level of fluorination. The difluorinated compound exhibits orange luminescence of excitonic origin, which is still observable at room temperature. The presented data demonstrate that degree of fluorination is a versatile design strategy for tuning dipolar degrees of freedom, intermolecular interactions, the strength of organic−inorganic coupling, and optical properties in hybrid halides.
nc25d3496676c: The integration of ultrathin and conformal interphases onto electrodes can lead to advanced electrochemical systems with control over the near-surface nanoenvironment impacting the double layer, electrode stability, reagent access, and solvation. However, the precise fabrication of nanometric interphases with tailored thickness and composition without blocking active surface sites is challenging, especially on porous application-relevant electrodes. Here, we report the reductive and self-limiting electrodeposition of polymer networks (EPoN) as a versatile and tunable method to uniformly coat non-planar and porous electrodes with physically adhered ultrathin functional polymer networks. The deposition chemistry is based on cathodically mediated methylpyridinium crosslinking and achieves the fabrication of polymer thin films on oxidation-sensitive catalytic metals. Our reductive EPoN process follows a self-limiting growth mechanism, yielding uniform and defect-correcting coatings with tunable nanometric thickness and charge density. The polymer network interphase is permselective, retaining molecular access to the functional surface, but modulates its permeation and activity based on charge and size, as demonstrated with a positively charged nanometric interphase as a functional barrier for regulating the hydrogen evolution reaction on copper. Our reductive EPoN strategy establishes a robust platform to tailor catalytic interphases for precise control over the electrochemical nanoenvironment.
n25dbc5ab372f: For nearly a century, alloy design has been guided by the Hume-Rothery rules, which describe the conditions required for solid solution formation and have traditionally constrained the compositional space available to materials scientists. The emergence of high-entropy alloys fundamentally altered this paradigm by demonstrating that configurational entropy can stabilize compositions that would otherwise be thermodynamically unfavorable. Since their discovery, high-entropy concepts have expanded beyond metallic systems into ceramics, including oxides, carbides, silicides, nitrides, and borides, creating new opportunities to access unconventional chemistries and local atomic environments. This review examines how high-entropy alloying can be used to transcend classical alloying limitations and stabilize elements in coordination environments that are inaccessible in conventional materials. Particular emphasis is placed on high-entropy borides, where ordered boron frameworks provide a structural scaffold that accommodates chemically disparate elements while preserving phase stability. Recent examples, including Pt- and Si-containing high-entropy diborides, demonstrate how entropy stabilization enables the incorporation of elements that do not form stable binary diborides (MB2), resulting in unique electronic structures, bonding environments, and functional properties. More broadly, these systems illustrate how the interplay between disorder and local order can be leveraged to design next-generation materials beyond the boundaries imposed by traditional alloying rules.
ne3fea283d9d5: Spinel oxides generally show subpar activity for electrochemical water splitting because of low electronic conductivity, suboptimal adsorption energies, and poor operational stability. To overcome these limitations, Pd2+ is introduced to induce lattice strain in a metastable Co3O4 phase featuring off-centered cobalt and oxygen atoms. While pristine Co3O4 typically crystallizes in the centrosymmetric Fd3̅m space group, 1.2 at % Pd transforms it to the dominant non-centrosymmetric F4̅3m space group. This unconventional lattice contains two non-equivalent tetrahedral sites and one octahedral site. Pd2+ preferentially substitutes the Co1 atom at the (0, 0, 0) 4a tetrahedral position, with a relative stabilization of −1.02 eV. Pd2+-induced enhancement of the density of states near the Fermi level tunes the d-band center, while Co-to-Pd charge redistribution activates the otherwise less active tetrahedral site alongside the intrinsically active octahedral site, thereby enhancing alkaline water electrolysis. For oxygen and hydrogen evolution, this bifunctional catalyst delivers mass activities of 60.6 and 31.0 A/g and turnover frequencies of 0.32 and 0.28 H2 s−1 at 300 and 250 mV overpotentials, respectively. In a two-electrode configuration, it reaches 50 mA/cm2 at an iR-uncorrected cell voltage of 1.85 V, while at 200 mA/cm2, it produces 25.4 mL/h H2 at a cell voltage of 2.31 V.
n0955aef50dca: The AtomicLimits ALD/ALE database is a community resource that catalogues atomic layer deposition (ALD) and atomic layer etching (ALE) processes reported in the literature. While widely used, it currently captures only a small fraction of the available information, with limited process information per entry, and relies on manual curation. As ALD/ALE process development grows in demand and complexity, with many interdependent parameters and increasingly sophisticated chemistries such as for multicomponent films, decades of experimental and simulation knowledge remain locked across publications, supplementary files, and lab notebooks. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML) and large language models (LLMs), offer a path to unlock this knowledge for data-driven analysis and process design, but realizing this potential depends on structured, machine-readable data. In this perspective, we propose a framework to evolve AtomicLimits into an AI-ready knowledge infrastructure that integrates literature-extracted, experimental, and simulation data through a community-defined schema, a structured template that specifies which data fields to capture and how to organize them. We outline the AI capabilities this enables, from structured querying to autonomous experimentation, and discuss the coordinated community effort required to realize this vision for the atomic-scale processing field.
n41d182504942: Despite great progress in tailoring the molecular structures of donor−acceptor (D−A) copolymers, the ability to precisely tailor their solid-state chain packing and establish a comprehensive structure−property relationship remains a grand challenge. Here, three diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP)-based copolymers adjusting alkyl side chains with various lengths are developed to control their aggregation behavior in different solvents and the corresponding crystallite orientation in thin films, establishing the structure−charge -transport −property relationship and elucidating the underlying mechanism. Specifically, DPPs with longer side chains exhibit weaker solution aggregation, favoring the formation of a face-on orientation in as-cast films, where the face-on to edge-on orientation can be further achieved by strengthening their solution aggregation via changing the solvent from chloroform to chlorobenzene and xylene. Remarkably, by using a floating-film transfer method, the initially face-on crystallites in as-cast DPP films can be transformed into narrower distributed edge-on crystallites, resulting in the charge mobility being nearly tenfold higher than that of the corresponding as-cast sample. This study highlights how molecular engineering and processing strategies collaboratively guide the aggregation and packing of DPPs in the solution and solid state, offering key insights into the structure−processing−property relationship of D−A copolymers for high-performance optoelectronic devices.
nf2bdf1a1d15c: Zinc phosphide (Zn3P2) is a promising photovoltaic absorber for thin-film and flexible solar cells due to its earth-abundant composition and favourable optoelectronic properties. Recent advances in epitaxy have enabled the growth of high-quality Zn3P2 thin films despite the challenges posed by its incompatible lattice parameter and thermal expansion coefficient. However, Zn3P2 remains prone to intrinsic extended defects, such as rotated domains, that can limit device performance. Here, using (scanning) transmission electron microscopy, we identify a class of extended defects that appear as planar faults described by displacement vectors lying in the (001) plane. Within a pseudo-cubic description of Zn3P2, we establish a direct correspondence between planar faults and rotated domains, showing that both arise from the flexible ordering of vacant sites in the Zn sublattice. First-principles calculations reveal an extremely low planar-defect formation energy of 2.5 mJ m−2, demonstrating that these defects form at essentially negligible energetic cost, in excellent agreement with their high experimentally observed occurrence. Additional density functional theory calculations show that the studied intrinsic planar defects neither introduce mid-gap electronic states nor significantly perturb the local electrostatic potential, indicating that they are electronically benign. Our results suggest that any connection between the observed planar defects and a reduction in device performance must therefore involve indirect mechanisms, such as strain effects or interactions with other defects.

n15c75996fd62: Polymer–solvent interactions influence polypropylene chain conformation and catalytic performance. Among the solvents tested, methylcyclohexane enhances polypropylene conversion, favouring naphtha-range liquids over gaseous products.
n1e41f13d5c78: Microporous-layer-free cathodes deliver high-rate, durable CO 2 electrolysis, challenging conventional electrode design principles and simplifying device architecture.
nc3b35eff382c: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), or “forever chemicals,” are emerging environmental contaminants often used as coatings. To provide a sustainable replacement, here we engineer the superhydrophobic lignin-integrated particle (SLIP), a bioinspired coating material based on natural plant water vasculature. SLIP coatings achieve superhydrophobic performance matching that of PFAS materials. Additionally, the SLIPs are demonstrated to be biodegradable and tolerant to abrasion and UV light exposure. SLIPs show significant environmental benefit over PFAS use through quantified social and environmental cost analysis.
n2536967af3f8: The 2026 Chemistry Nobel Prize celebrates how molecular handedness can be created and amplified. From a materials perspective, the award invites a wider question: can chiral crystal faces, pores, and minerals provide the asymmetric stage on which chemistry first learns to choose left from right?
n97add992c8e9: The para-C–H activation of free aromatic carboxylic acids without directing groups remains a challenging task. Now, the authors report on an iridium-based catalytic system that leverages the synergistic effect of multi-noncovalent interactions to overcome this issue, enabling direct access to para-functionalized carboxylic acids and their derivatives.
n39728f0d6aac: The isolation of oxoboranes (RB≡O) featuring a genuine B–O triple bond has remained an outstanding challenge owing to the electron deficiency of boron and the intrinsic instability of the B≡O linkage. So far, direct evidence for such species has been largely limited to gas-phase and matrix-isolation studies and only recently inferred in solution. Here we report the isolation of a stable, free oxoborane generated via a carbon-monoxide-triggered transformation of a heterocumulene. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction establishes a terminal B≡O unit, while electronic structure analyses reveal two orthogonal π bonds consistent with a highly polarized triple bond. Mechanistic studies support a carbon monoxide coordination–insertion–isomerization pathway. The resulting oxoborane exhibits ambiphilic reactivity, enabling access to both neutral and cationic derivatives. These findings establish free oxoboranes as isolable species under condensed-phase conditions and provide a platform for exploring low-coordinate boron–oxygen multiple bonds. The isolation of oxoboranes featuring a genuine B–O triple bond is challenging owing to the instability of the B≡O linkage. Now stable crystalline oxoboranes have been prepared through a carbon-monoxide-triggered transformation, revealing a highly polarized B–O triple bond and enabling access to both neutral and cationic derivatives through ambiphilic reactivity.
n02d3dfe40622: Oxoboranes, molecules bearing a triple bond between a dicoordinate boron atom and a monocoordinate oxygen atom, are some of the longest-sought reactive main-group species. Their syntheses have been the subject of a series of documented attempts dating back to at least the early 1960s, leading to gas-phase/matrix isolation and evidence of chemical trapping, as well as isolation of oxoborane derivatives with reduced B–O bond orders. However, their detection or isolation of base-/acid-free oxoboranes in the condensed phase remains challenging. Here we present a remarkably simple synthesis of three oxoboranes that are stable as crystalline solids at room temperature. These species feature exceptionally short (1.208(4)–1.217(4) Å) and strong B–O bonds. Their properties are elucidated by both experimental and computational methods, and an explanation for their unusual stability is provided. Oxoboranes are among the longest-sought species in main-group chemistry. Now, stable crystalline oxoboranes with exceptionally short and strong B–O bonds have been prepared through the reaction of a diboracumulene with carbonyl-bearing compounds.
n4c9e68be9b0c: Energy poverty is a growing concern, but we still know little about which measures actually improve people’s health and living conditions. Here the authors find that structural measures and consistent financial support deliver the clearest benefits.
ncba5523cca40: The microscopic origin of ionic memory in two-dimensional (2D) nanofluidic memristors remains debated. Voltage-induced blistering of the confining walls of 2D nanofluidic channels is identified to trigger memristive hysteresis leading to nonlinear ion transport in the channels.
n4c660f8c68f6: Intrinsic electric polarization in III-nitride semiconductors is an advantage for large-scale optoelectronic devices but remains largely unexplored in sensory-memristive devices. Polarization-induced spatial separation of photogenerated carriers at the interfaces of III-nitride heterostructures enables efficient and scalable in-sensor computing at room temperature.
n7918f6736cde: Asymmetric photocatalysis generally relies either on compact molecular catalysts or much larger photoenzymes. Now, a photocatalytic tetrapeptide, combining a substrate-binding site and a visible light-absorbing photosensitizer within a modular scaffold, enables highly enantioselective photochemical transformations.
ncdf10b4af13c: A Pt catalyst supported on N-doped C with isolated Fe sites is developed for electrochemical ammonia cracking towards H2 production at 1.5 A cm−2. The catalyst suppresses Pt oxidation and promotes the removal of poisonous N species, enabling stable operation for 500 h.
n3b70555f1a66: Substituted cyclohexanes are key motifs in drug discovery; therefore, stereoselective methods for their synthesis are valuable. However, the synthesis of thermodynamically disfavoured stereoisomers remains challenging. Now, a dual-ligand nickel system enables stereoselective three-component synthesis of substituted cyclohexanes, through Ni-catalysed 1,1-arylfunctionalization of substituted methylenecyclohexanes.
n910f94bd03f6: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry recognised the status of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) at the forefront of materials chemistry. The increased visibility brought by such recognition, however, also calls for renewed attention to the fundamentals, reminding us that being on everyone’s lips should not lead us to overlook the basics. Here, we wish to turn the spotlight on what is possibly the most fundamental aspect of all, that is, the determination of the chemical composition of MOFs. We provide a brief overview of routine analytical methods and a series of suggestions for deriving the chemical formula.
n2515ce2b234a: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) has revealed many possible Li-induced interfacial reactions in solid-state electrolytes (SSEs), but most in situ studies form Li|electrolyte interfaces through non-electrochemical Li deposition, including evaporation, sputtering, or electron-beam-induced deposition. These routes may introduce additional energy that activates reaction pathways not accessed during electrochemical Li plating. Here, we use lab-based operando XPS to directly evaluate oxide solid-state electrolyte stability during electrochemical Li formation. Using this approach, we find sharply different responses for two representative oxide SSEs: NASICON-type Li1+xAlxTi2–x(PO4)3 (LATP) is reduced upon Li plating, forming a Li+/Ti3+-rich mixed-conducting interphase that partially relaxes through coupled ionic–electronic redistribution, whereas garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) shows no spectroscopically resolvable Zr or La reduction. This work represents the first direct operando XPS evaluation of SSE stability against electrochemically plated Li metal.

n8a4a4ea5188b: 5-Hydroxy-2(5 H )-furanone (HFO) emerges as a versatile bio-based platform chemical, combining renewable accessibility, rich multifunctional reactivity, asymmetric synthesis potential, and routes to high-value chemicals and sustainable materials alike.
ne7d878d963e8: Icosahedral carboranes have extensive applications owing to their unique properties. This review summarizes advances in the mechanistic study of transition metal-catalyzed carborane cage B–H activation and functionalization.

n3366e6e80a3f: Cost-effective Li2ZrCl6 halides with regulated configurational complexity combine rapid lithium-ion conduction with ultralow electronic conductivity and superior oxidative stability. A robust zirconium oxychloride cathode-electrolyte interphase is formed during cycling, enabling 4.4 V all-solid-state LiNi0.85Co0.1Mn0.05O2 batteries to operate for up to 3,700 cycles.
n2948bef3ea14: Why does corrosion attack specific sites under some conditions but spread uniformly under others? Liang et al. combine real-time nanoscale imaging with atomistic simulations to show that corrosion reflects a competition between local structural heterogeneity and thermodynamic driving force. Near equilibrium, strained regions preferentially corrode and promote localized pitting; far from equilibrium, stronger driving forces overwhelm these local differences and produce rapid, uniform corrosion. The findings provide a framework for understanding and controlling localized material degradation.
n167c83bc2fce: Stable α-FAPbI3 is promising for high-performance X-ray imaging but is difficult to produce without alloying. Here, polymer coordination with PVP enables stable, alloying-free α-FAPbI3 thick films by controlling crystallization and lattice strain. The resulting detectors combine high sensitivity, low-dose operation, and fast response, enabling high-resolution, real-time X-ray imaging.
n3e1139421df5: Regioselective esterification remains challenging, particularly when multiple alcohol groups with similar reactivity are present. Now it has been shown that aldehyde dehydrogenases can be engineered into oxidative ester synthases with programmable alcohol selectivity, enabling controlled ester bond formation through active-site remodelling.
ne5f768710e1b: Formamidinium lead iodide (α-FAPbI3) perovskite, despite its ideal bandgap, requires high-temperature (≥150 °C) annealing for the δ-to-α phase transformation, hindering its application in low-temperature processed inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), particularly on flexible substrates. Herein, we demonstrate that the alicyclic Lewis base caprolactam (CPL) effectively drives the complete δ-to-α phase transformation of FAPbI3 at a reduced temperature of 100 °C. Experiments and theoretical calculations reveal that CPL lowers the phase transition energy barrier and retards crystallization kinetics via strong Pb2+ coordination and controlled desorption. This strategy yields highly crystalline, fully phase-converted α-FAPbI3 films with improved morphology, reduced defect densities, and enhanced optoelectronic properties. Consequently, CPL-modified inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.64% with good operational stability. The low-temperature processability also enables high-performance flexible PSCs with a PCE of 23.73%. This work presents an additive engineering approach for realizing efficient and stable α-FAPbI3 PSCs through low-temperature manufacturing.
nea02888a1208: Ultra-wide-bandgap (UWBG) metal halide perovskite solar cells are essential for multi-junction solar cells with higher power conversion efficiency (PCE) potentials. In this work, we report the dual functions of 5-iodoisophthalic acid (I-BDC) to suppress phase segregation and uncoordinated Pb2+ related defects to enhance UWBG perovskite cell performance and stability. An I-BDC incorporated 1.95 eV perovskite film exhibited stable photoluminescence after 120 min of illumination. The best I-BDC cell achieved a certified reverse scan PCE of 16.5%, the highest for 1.95 eV perovskite cells to date. These UWBG perovskite solar cells are the most stable reported to date, with one encapsulated device retaining 90% of its initial PCE after 500 h of maximum power point tracking at ∼40 °C and another retaining 95% of its initial PCE after 206 thermal cycles (–40 ↔ 85 °C), passing the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) 61215 testing protocols at the cell level.
n712c6d476bae: High-energy batteries require cathodes with greater capacity and specific energy. Ni-rich-layered oxides approach the performance limit of LiNiO2 (LNO), yet its practical use is hindered by severe chemomechanical degradation. Near 4.2 V, the H2-H3/H4 transition drives substantial c-axis contraction, volume shrinkage, O1 formation, oxygen loss, and rapid capacity decay. Here, we show that only 5% cobalt-free complex concentrated doping stabilizes LNO without sacrificing energy density. The modified LNO reduces c-axis strain from 7.4 to 2.1%, exhibits near-zero-strain behavior, and delivers 258 mAh•g–1 and 973 Wh•kg–1. In pouch cells, it retains 80% capacity after 1800 cycles and shows markedly improved thermal stability. These results demonstrate that complex-concentrated doping at low dopant loading can suppress strain and phase transformations at the full-Ni limit, providing a broadly applicable strategy for stabilizing high-energy intercalation electrodes while preserving their intrinsic capacity and specific energy during prolonged electrochemical cycling.
n230e941a234c: In this work, we report an innovative interface engineering strategy combining bidirectional chemical anchoring and electronic bridging via a 2D reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and MXene conductive network. This hierarchical 2D structure suppresses the aggregation and stacking of single-layer MXene nanosheets while mutually compensating for individual charge transport limitations. Specifically, the abundant functional groups passivate interfacial defects (Pb2+ and I–) and bond with the PCBM layer via coordination, hydrogen bonding and π–π interactions. This synergistic architecture lowers the electron energy offset. Consequently, PSCs incorporating the rGO-MXene interlayer achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.96% (certified 25.05%) and retain 96.43% of initial efficiency after 1000 h in ambient air. Furthermore, 10 × 10 cm2 large-area PSM yields a high PCE of 20.25%, maintaining 96.05% of initial efficiency under maximum power point tracking for 963 h.
n2b243381fb6b: Developing robust multi-junction tandem photovoltaics remains constrained by the instability of mixed-halide perovskite subcells, given their dominating contribution to overall power output. Integrating near-infrared (NIR) PbS quantum dots (QDs) with FAPbBr3 and crystalline silicon (c-Si) broadens spectrum utilization while improving overall operational stability by reducing the perovskite power contribution. However, enlarged (100) facets and the trade-off between film thickness and quality limit efficient NIR photon harvesting. Herein, a Lewis-basic dihydrazide molecule achieves universal passivation across diverse PbS QD facets via synergistic lead chelation and hydrogen-bonding interactions. Consequently, 0.8 eV PbS QD solar cells with a 685 nm-thick active layer achieve a short-circuit current density of 41.31 mA cm–2 and a 1100-nm-filtered efficiency of 1.80%. The resulting FAPbBr3/c-Si/PbS triple-junction tandems achieve a promising efficiency of 31.04%, with the perovskite subcell contributing 30.4% of the total power output, demonstrating a well-matched operational lifetime. This work offers a strategic framework for efficient multi-junction tandem photovoltaics.
nb868a2c8a215: LiNiO2 (LNO) is a promising high-capacity cathode, but its practical application is hindered by severe structural and microstructural instability. Herein, we develop a two-step calcination strategy that decouples lithiation from Ta introduction. This approach promotes the segregation of a Ta-rich phase at grain boundaries, producing nanosized, radially aligned primary particles that mitigate strain and suppress microcracking. It also preserves a layered–rocksalt nanostructured multiphase that reversibly transforms into a layered–spinel-like state during charging, which may contribute to structural stability and Li-ion transport. The optimized TS-Ta-LNO delivers 252.7 mAh g–1 and retains 88.4% of its capacity after 100 cycles. Furthermore, a TS-Ta-LNO/Li-metal pouch cell maintains stable voltage profiles under an electric vertical take-off and landing dynamic-load protocol, demonstrating its potential for high-energy, high-power batteries.
n615084cc7254: Hot carriers (HC) offer a potential route to surpass conventional efficiency limits in solar cells. Generated after light absorption, these high-energy carriers can significantly boost device performance if extracted before dissipating energy as heat. Although HC cooling has been studied in tin-based perovskites, interpreting these dynamics is challenging because high-energy, high-fluence pump pulses required to generate HCs have shallow penetration depths, confining excitation near the surface. In tin-based perovskites, surface properties differ from the bulk, and surface defects may strongly contribute to the optical response. Here, by using pump-push-probe ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy, we photo-excite the semiconductor thin film with a low-energy pump, in a photon density range typical for solar cell operation, making relevant the bulk electronic properties, and selectively re-excite the photo-carriers only once they cool down, enabling direct tracking of HC relaxation in the relevant spectral region while minimizing surface contributions. We track the cooling process in FA0.85Cs0.15SnI3 (FA = Formamidinium) as a benchmark sample and extend the analysis to single-cation FA+, MA+ (MA = methylammonium), and Cs+ tin perovskites. Across all compositions, and at different doping densities, we find cooling timescales in the 150–600 fs time range. These results highlight the central role of phonon-mediated interactions and show that ultrafast cooling fundamentally limits hot carrier extraction in tin halide perovskites.
n472b3f592c93: Sodium-metal batteries present a more abundant alternative to lithium-based batteries, with high theoretical capacity and comparable reduction potential. Ether electrolytes perform well in sodium-metal batteries under continuous cycling and are presumed to have a stable solid-electrolyte interphase (SEI). However, the solubility of sodium SEI components is a cause for concern, and SEI evolution during calendar aging is not commonly studied for the ether sodium-metal system. In this work, SEI mass formation and dissolution are quantitatively measured for NaPF6 in diglyme. For varying potential hold levels, significant SEI dissolution is observed, from 55 to 76% of the originally formed SEI. Characterization shows that in addition to organic component dissolution, inorganic salts such as NaF and NaxPOyFz are unstable in SEI during open circuit rest. This instability results in continuous corrosion of sodium metal during calendar aging, highlighting an important understanding and concern of SEI stability in sodium-metal batteries.
n352917b010cd: Fast Na+ transport and durable interfacial stability remain challenging for wide-temperature Na- metal batteries. To address these issues, we developed a synergistic solvation-interphase regulation strategy by integrating methyl propanoate (MP) with a combined VC/NaDFOB additive pair. MP modifies the Na+ solvation sheath and facilitates Na+ desolvation, while VC and NaDFOB cooperatively generate a mechanically robust hybrid organicinorganic interphase. This coupled regulation enables enhanced ion transport and interfacial stability over a broad temperature range. The EC/EMC/MP + VC/NaDFOB electrolyte exhibits an ionic conductivity of 2.52 mS cm–1 at –40 ̊C and an increased Na+ transference number. Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cells retain 96.5% of their initial capacity after 1000 cycles with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.98% at room temperature. At –20 ̊C, the cells deliver 69.4 mAh g–1 for over 900 cycles, corresponding to 82% of their room-temperature capacity. This work establishes a practical solvation-interphase regulation approach for wide-temperature Na- metal batteries.
n626efefab170: NMR chemical shifts are plainly transformed into machine learning features that have rational and intuitive chemical meaning. A small number of these features are used to predict molecular reactivity (via the HOMO-LUMO energy gap), resulting in a model that is not reliant on a priori knowledge of chemical structure or charge.
n6e245f30a071: This review discusses transferrable lessons and parameters from solution-based COF syntheses and small molecule mechanochemistry for the mechanochemical syntheses of imine and imine-derived COFs.
n2969b07b530f: By anchoring H 2 O molecules and reconstructing the hydrogen bond network through a hydrophilic delignified wood-based separator, the transport of Zn 2+ and H 2 O was decoupled to inhibit H 2 O-induced side reactions while ensuring Zn 2+ diffusion.
n74ccc94c1753: Conformation-flexible molecule 1,4-CHD not only passivates defects in the perovskite film but also constructs a dynamic molecular spring at grain boundaries to dissipate stress, enabling 23.53% efficient wide-bandgap perovskite solar cells with superior thermal cycling and operational stability.

n4c8470583766: The ORR and OER activity of α-K x MnO 2 simultaneously improve with increasing electrolyte pH. Electrochemistry, operando spectro-microscopy & grand-canonical DFT link this behavior to pH-dependent electrode charging and bulk cation (de)insertion.
n564b237ad3b0: Public battery datasets are growing rapidly, but fragmented hosting and inconsistent descriptions make them difficult to find, compare, and reuse. Battery Data Commons presently indexes 349 datasets in a living, searchable metadata registry, using human- and machine-readable descriptions linked to the original sources. This exposes experimental context without relocating raw data to give datasets wider visibility and a second life to legacy ones. Together, these capabilities provide infrastructure for reproducible battery science, engineering, and AI-enabled innovation.
n98f1126b8042: Protein conformational dynamics govern how proteins assemble across distinct pathways. This review unifies native crystallization, amyloid fibrillization, and reduction-induced phase transitions, revealing how dynamic assembly routes can be harnessed to design adaptive, hierarchical protein materials with programmable functions.
n5bd7d775a315: Paramagnetic molecules can serve as electron spin qubits for quantum information processing, provided that they preserve their spin coherence for a sufficient time to allow for computation and error correction. Here we report the rare isolation of stable Zr(III) aryloxide complexes, where Zr is an earth-abundant metal ion with a coherently manipulable electron spin. Density functional theory calculations reveal the trigonal planar d 1 geometry stabilizes a 4 d z 2 –5 s hybrid singly occupied molecular orbital with little ligand contribution and significant s character (25–27%), yielding large isotropic hyperfine coupling constants of 803–809 MHz. We observed long spin–lattice relaxation times ( T 1 ) up to 87 ms and dephasing times ( T m , T m CPMG ) up to 123 μs using isotope-selective pulsed electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy. Nutation experiments further showed coherent manipulation of several electronic and electronuclear transitions. This study introduces Zr(III) aryloxides as competitive molecular qudits and expands the scope of metal ions to more earth-abundant metals.
nd5fe017b305b: The lack of standardized reporting and annotation of nucleic acid nanostructures limits reproducibility, interoperability and the efficient reuse of published designs. NanostarDB is a community-driven knowledgebase that standardizes nucleic acid nanostar designs through persistent identifiers, structural annotations, and integrated computational tools for design exploration, analysis and reuse, and is compliant with principles of findability, accessibility, interoprability and reusability (FAIR).
n594ee9b84f39: Margarida Costa Gomes, CNRS Research Professor at École Normale Supérieure de Lyon, talks to Nature Synthesis about understanding the molecular behaviour of porous liquids and the challenges of translating that understanding into functional materials.
